The up-to-date, real-time system model produced by an Enterprise GIS is required for the Company to meet 
long-term REV initiatives, including establishing the DSPP, and facilitates timely and current load flow 
modeling that control center personnel will depend on in the future. 
 
Additionally, distribution circuits will become vastly more complex to plan and operate due to the continuous 
integration of DERs.  One of REV’s goals is to defer utility spending on capital reinforcement of these circuits 
by way of non-wires solutions.  An Enterprise GIS will improve the accuracy of load flow modeling to streamline 
the benefits of siting non-wires solutions.  REV will also enable more customer-centered initiatives including 
time of use rates, more customer energy choices and programs, and customer access to load data to better manage 
their usage.  An Enterprise GIS will provide a single integrated platform for managing and disseminating the 
requisite network models and provide employees access to geospatial data from a suite of centrally managed 
applications. 
 
Emergency Planning & Response  
 
The modern GIS technology is steadily transforming the capabilities to respond to major events. 
Hurricane Sandy heightened the use of GIS by federal, state, and local governments in the northeast.  For 
example, New York City recently established a Disaster Assessment and Power Restoration Plan, which 
incorporates GIS at the center of response planning, field assessment, and public outreach.  In addition to the 
telecoms and peer utilities, Con Edison is a participant in this plan.  This and similar programs in Westchester 
County present an opportunity for outage management and municipal collaboration. 
 
 
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 37 of 118


--- Page 118 ---
Emergency planning and response rely on geographic information to predict areas that are most at risk. An 
Enterprise GIS will enable the Company to share spatial information about assets affected by events with the 
New York City Office of Emergency Management (“OEM”) and Westchester County to prioritize relief 
efforts.  In general, emergency management services increasingly rely on GIS platforms to generate crisis maps 
based on a combination of satellite imagery, remote sensor readings, statistical models, and crowdsourced data.  
For instance, utilities and first responders use spatial analysis of utility assets and customer social media posts 
to create a map of locations in urgent need of relief during storms.  Robust and accurate geographic 
information is necessary for first responders to make well-informed decisions, and ongoing refinements to real-
time data analysis are increasing GIS accuracy.  Enterprise GIS would allow the Company to deploy turn-key 
mobile applications during emergencies.  Such mobile apps have been deployed during recent major events 
such as Hurricane Harvey and the Northern California Campfire.5/6 
Employee & Public Safety  
 
Enterprise GIS platform integration with the Company’s Outage Management System (OMS) and Supervisory 
Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system will enable electronic switching orders for electric distribution 
circuits and replace a manual process that can lead to operating errors.  The built-in visual trace capability 
inherent to modern GIS platforms improves the safety and reliability of gas and electric distribution circuits 
through validation of circuit continuity and reducing mapping errors. 
 
Con Edison electric and gas crews will benefit from an Enterprise GIS system by being able to more readily 
view field hazards/conditions as a layer that is available on the GIS visualization platform.  For example, today, 
electric crews are often dispatched and arrive to find that the structure cannot be worked on due to a safety 
hazard.  Having an integrated Enterprise GIS will allow for any field safety hazard or “D” fault to be tagged to 
the asset.  For example, should a feeder joint be “D” faulted, the mapping system will allow for that structure to 
be displayed as “tagged”.  This status would be immediately reflected to all users and displayed on all map 
products.  This will yield efficiency by eliminating the unnecessary dispatching of a crew(s) to hazard locations.  
Other examples of potential field hazards include, environmental (oxygen deficient or hydrogen sulfide in 
structures) or structural (condemned due to structural defects) hazards.  The Company would also be able to 
share this data with other City agencies in spatial format. 
 
Grid Resilience 
 
An Enterprise GIS will improve grid resilience and reduce outage restoration times. Some of these benefits 
include: 
 
• 
Vegetation Management – An Enterprise GIS will enable new spatial analytics capabilities combined 
with accurately mapped facilities that will enable efficiency gains in the planning and tracking of 
vegetation management to reduce unplanned outages.  In addition, the Enterprise GIS will provide the 
capability of targeting vegetation management based on circuits and migrate to condition based 
vegetation management program vs. time-based program thereby optimizing investments.  Enterprise 
GIS will enable integration of LiDAR technology to enhance vegetation management programs in the 
near future.  
  
• 
Outage Management – Enterprise GIS will improve the accuracy of outage counts in the OMS system 
and facilitate faster restoration of customer outages during normal blue-sky events as well as major 
storms.  Combining geospatial visualization of AMI data with predictive analytics tools is enabling 
utilities to reduce the duration of the outages from weather events and identify weak points in the 
electrical distribution system to prevent future outages.7

Damage Assessment – Enterprise GIS will allow the Company to deploy a standardized damage

Enterprise GIS for Gas  
 
An Enterprise GIS also benefits the Company’s gas system.  With an Enterprise GIS, Gas Operations will be 
able to reduce excavation risk and operating errors, engage in real-time collaboration with City agencies when 
responding to gas public safety incidents or coordinating planned work, more efficiently monitor the 
performance of gas transmission and distribution systems, and better manage gas outages and restoration 
efforts.  Gas Operations could also have potential integration opportunities with AMI to monitor system 
performance at the service level.  Additionally, the Company could create gas flow modeling and simulations 
for planned and emergency work.  An Enterprise GIS would also provide a gas system inventory which will 
give the Company the ability to trend data and analytics required to identify threats for our 
Distribution/Transmission Integrity Management Programs, as well as ad-hoc reporting.   
 
 
 
 
 
Customer Experience 
  
Con Edison, as the Distributed System Platform Provider (DSPP), remains committed to increasing the amount 
of data available, making it easier to access system data through its online portal, and supporting stakeholder 
data needs.  An Enterprise GIS will allow for future use cases for system data availability, identify additional 
datasets to share, and respond to stakeholder requests to improve ease of access to system data.  The Company 
currently provides extensive system data as part of the hosting capacity platform within the system data portal.  
The existing hosting capacity maps are customized web-based GIS format to show locations where it is 
beneficial to interconnect distributed generation.  With continued enhancements to the Enterprise GIS through 
the phased implementation, the Company will continue to provide useful information to customers and 
developers looking to interconnect to the Con Edison distribution system.  A few use cases include: 
 
• 
GIS platform will enable asset management capabilities for all assets behind the meter and reduce the 
time needed to analyze grid impact of citing DER resources. 
  
• 
Spatial proximity analysis of new electric and gas service requests within existing infrastructure will 
reduce the time for new business and DER requests. 
 
• 
The current systems proprietary coordinate systems and obsolete data formats substantially inhibits the 
Company’s ability to exchange and/or integrate third party data.  The Enterprise GIS technology uses 
Application Programming Interfaces (API) architecture that will provide the ability to incorporate data 
from external entities into dynamic map displays.  Examples of available data include New York City / 
New York State / FEMA “GeoHub” portals, public improvement job sites, contractor drawings, 
parcel/cadastral data, flood zones, census bureau zones, and associated demographic data. 
 
Single Source of Information  
 
The Enterprise GIS will provide efficiency gains associated with mapping, facility records management, and 
data analysis.  At the end of the project, the Company will create a single reliable source of information for all 
the Company’s assets and customer assets that interoperate with the grid.

Data integrity and accuracy will improve as mapping teams will update a single system at work order

Cost Reduction   
 
Consolidating the mapping applications into an enterprise wide GIS platform will reduce total cost of ownership.  
Cost efficiency gains include: 
 
• 
Software licensing and infrastructure costs – These costs are higher for unsupported mapping systems 
due to need for custom support and with no additional functionality. Mitigation of cybersecurity 
vulnerability with unsupported infrastructure components require additional investments that affects end 
users access to these systems and increases support costs.  Migrating to enterprise wide GIS will allow 
the Company to consolidate the mapping systems and reduce software and hardware costs associated 
with multiple systems. Deploying an Enterprise GIS platform will allow the Company to develop 
strategic partnerships with vendors to standardize technology platforms and effectively manage support 
costs. 
 
• 
Reducing non-Enterprise GIS applications – An Enterprise GIS will reduce costs and streamline 
business processes by using Company-wide application platforms.  Enterprise wide GIS platform will 
reduce the segmentation of the application portfolio and matching support levels to system needs. 
 
• 
Support costs – An Enterprise GIS will reduce costs associated with training and sourcing of limited 
resources supporting outdated mapping technology platforms. An Enterprise GIS platform will allow 
the Company to focus talent on the highest value work, such as technology enablers, and using vendors 
for standard work. Standardizing common mapping tools will also lower support costs by mitigating the 
need for custom tools. 
 
• 
Software integrations – Software integrations with obsolete outdated mapping platforms increase 
implementation and operational costs of operational utility systems such as WMS, OMS etc. Enterprise 
GIS will reduce the integration costs of future software platforms as well as improve the availability and 
security of these platforms by replacing non-standard integrations.  Enterprise GIS will reduce 
cybersecurity risks due to obsolete technology, promotes enhanced infrastructure utilization.

Advanced Future Capabilities   
 
With the increase in the availability of spatial data, GIS enabled solutions are driving new capabilities for 
utilities. The global GIS solutions market is expected to reach $17.3 billion by 2023 according to P&S 
Market Research.8  GIS investments are providing substantial positive payback across the industry. For 
example, King County, WA has undertaken a GIS ROI Study where the County has realized $775 million 
from its GIS investments.9  Future use cases for Con Edison include: 
 
• 
New York State Smart Cities Initiative – Con Edison’s GIS implementation will support New 
York City’s initiative to develop the Subterranean Information Model that includes all utility and 
city assets that allows all stakeholders access to buried infrastructure.10  There is a strong business 
need to map underground infrastructure, but it is limited by availability of spatial data and the 
security concerns associated with sharing the data amongst facility owners.  Securely 
incorporating asset data into this model will allow the Company to identify its infrastructure 
amongst all the buried infrastructure. 
 
• 
Location Based Services – GIS will enable real time location processing, which may allow the 
potential for incorporating autonomous vehicle locations in the future to automatically direct field 
crews nearest to a job.  This could enhance post-disaster outage recovery operations and enable 
customers to track utility restoration crews. 
 
• 
Artificial Intelligence – Advancements in AI and machine learning (ML) enabled by cloud 
computing infrastructure will enable rapid integration of 3D (three dimensional) visualization 
tools on modern GIS platforms.  Modern GIS platforms support integration of Virtual Reality 
(“VR”) and Augmented Reality (“AR”) to enable new capabilities.  Artificial intelligence is 
another rapidly evolving technology that has been applied to GIS projects in recent years. For 
example, AR enabled 3D models of hazardous locations can be utilized for safety training of field 
crews. 
 
• 
Environmental Sustainability – One important application for GeoAI11 is in planning urban 
infrastructure and tracking changes in an area over time.  For example, researchers in Los 
Angeles wanted to know how land use and roadways impacted air pollution and, in turn, how 
pollution would affect health in residents.  GIS helped them analyze traffic patterns over different 
times of day in relation to the concentration of harmful particles in the air.  By using this 
information to predict when pollution levels would become dangerous, the city could issue 
warnings as early as possible.

SCOPE OF THE PROGRAM 
 
Con Edison has initiated a phased deployment plan to consolidate the various mapping systems in stages 
that reflect the three primary mapping systems and deliver business benefits along the way.  When 
complete, GIS will result in a single model that displays the Company’s electric, gas, and steam 
distribution systems, with the capability to turn layers on and off so a user can see all or some of the data. 
All data and assets will also be displayed on a google based real word coordinate mapping application 
that allows the user to toggle on/off various mapping systems. 
 
Phase 0 
 
In 2014, the Company undertook a Phase 0 planning project for an enterprise wide GIS deployment.  During 
this project, the Company engaged GIS product and data migration service vendors to: 
 
• 
Conduct functional, data migration, and system integration workshops with subject matter experts

In 2017, the Company expanded on Phase 0 to conduct additional data quality assessment and to evaluate 
the latest GIS technology.  In 2018, the Company began competitive sourcing for parts of the project.  The 
Company incorporated lessons learned and information gathered from Phase 0 into this business plan. 
 
Phase 1 
 
Phase 1 ($25 million) will focus on replacing the VISION system, which consists of the Company’s low-
tension maps for all electric customers supplied by 120V and 465V cables and all gas customers supplied 
by gas service pipes.  Phase 1 will combine these Company electric and gas maps into a single, new GIS 
platform.    
 
Phase 1 will occur from 2019 to first quarter of 2020.  Benefits of Phase 1 include:   
 
• 
New Mapping Tools for secondary electric distribution system and gas distribution 
o Spatial Asset Management Tool 
o Planning & Analysis tool 
o Field Mobility Mapping Tool 
• 
Create a new visualization tool

Phase 3 
 
Phase 3 ($125 million), which is outside the horizon of the Company’s 2019 rate filing, targets the

essentially PDF images, to a modern GIS platform.  At this time, Phase 3 is envisioned to be most 
complex technically and labor intensive of all the three phases.  When Phase 3 is complete, GIS will 
enable the Company to display all mapping systems on a single platform.

GIS PRODUCT OVERVIEW 
 
Figure 3 (below) illustrates the planned system architecture and application components for the Enterprise 
GIS. 
 
 
Figure 3 – GIS System Architecture 
 
The Enterprise GIS system is based on a Services Oriented Architecture (“SOA”), which allows software 
applications to leverage a common set of services.  Services can take many forms including: 
 
• 
Geo-processing services (e.g. deriving coordinates for an address) 
• 
File transformation services (e.g. PDF file creation of a map display) 
• 
Application programming interface (“API”) services 
• 
Map display services (e.g. a map display service that provides an interactive map with electric 
features and the location of historical outage records) 
 
Major components include: 
 
• 
Spatial Asset Management, Planning & Analysis tool – The tool will be used primarily by 
mapping teams for maintaining Con Edison’s facility models, updating maps, and publishing map 
services that can be used by the web and mobile users.  The desktop GIS product is Schneider’s 
ArcFM. The ArcFM product is an extension to Esri’s ArcGIS Desktop product.  The ArcFM 
extensions are functionality specific to electric and gas utilities.  ArcFM will replace Con Edison’s 
current mapping systems (VISION Electric, VISION Gas, Primary Mapping, EDFIS and Conduit 
Mapping). 
 
• 
Visualization tool – All Company users will be able to access general map displays and specific 
application logic via a web browser. The map displays are maintained in the form of map services.  
Examples of map display services include a visualization that allows for the display and querying 
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 48 of 118


--- Page 129 ---
30 
 
of primary electric features and conduit/duct locations.  The web-based component will ultimately 
replace the multitude of visualization applications currently deployed including NetMap and Area 
Profile System. Map Centric data studies have demonstrated significant improvements in decision 
making using maps. 
 
• 
Field Mobility Mapping Tool – The mobile applications will be based on Esri’s ArcGIS Mobile 
platform and will replace the Byers application.  This is expected to support over 3,000 mobile field 
users.

DATA CONVERSION  
 
Data conversion has been recognized as a high risk for cost/schedule overruns.  There are three components 
of data conversion: 
• 
Conversion: digitizing maps from paper or raster (picture) 
• 
Migration:  processing data from one digital source to another 
• 
Conflation: adjusting graphic data and aligning to the real world 
 
The data conversion tools have matured since Phase 0 in 2004 with the availability of Safe Software’s 
product FME (Feature Manipulation Engine).  Three market leading vendors have also emerged with 
proven conversion software products:  Avineon, Cyient, and RAMTeCH.  At this time benchmarking 
indicates that migration and conversion risk is more process and execution based than software-based.  The 
following table is a summary of data conversion lessons learned and a high-level plan to mitigate data 
conversion risks. 
 
# 
Lesson Learned 
Risk Mitigation  
1

component.  Pare it down to the most 
important elements to ensure performance 
and flexibility.

and Gas in Phase 0. 
2 
Carefully evaluate vendor expertise, 
capacity and methodology. 
• 
Established relationships with market

qualified resources.

Work Description: 
  
This effort is to migrate the Electric WMS (Work and Asset Management) system to the enterprise Maximo WMS 
platform. This is in keeping with IT’s strategy of moving to a “One Enterprise” Work and Asset Management solution 
for all of Con Edison’s business areas, to realize the full benefits of a true enterprise solution across all business areas. 
Electric WMS is now on the CGI ARMS platform and is experiencing severe limitations in the product line to meet the 
current and growing needs of the business. Significant investments have to be made to enhance the current 
functionalities of the Con Ed CGI ARMS implementation which can be met with Maximo out of the box capability. 
Maximo has been successfully implemented and has been in use in several business areas at Con Ed for many years: 
Central Operations, Steam, and Transmission Ops. In 2021 the platform was upgraded and the Controlled Enterprise 
license, which had some limitations in terms of the number of Maximo products licensed and the business areas 
covered, was re-negotiated to a true enterprise model which gives Con Edison and its affiliates use of any/all modules 
within the Maximo work and asset management suite of products on a subscription basis. A roadmap has been 
established to migrate over 45 disparate legacy WMS systems over the next decade. The Steam Job Tracking System 
migration to Maximo is now underway and Constructions WMS will be migrated starting the fourth quarter of 2021. 
With this unrestricted use of the product line and total user base coverage, Electric Operation can now access and utilize 
all of Maximo’s Work and Asset Mgt modules under the current enterprise license.  
The current Electric WMS system manages and tracks all work done by Electric Operations including:  
• 
Emergency repairs 
• 
Maintenance and inspection 
• 
New construction and customer connections 
• 
System performance/reliability programs 
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 56 of 118


--- Page 137 ---
 
This effort will encompass all major categories of work and asset management currently tracked in CGI ARMs, 
understand the limitations of the existing solution to meet the current and future needs of the business, and fill in the 
gaps. It will look at a cross section of, but not limited to:  
 
• 
Work Initiation – initiate work from various sources  
• 
Design and Estimating - The use of Compatible Units (CU) to define the labor, material and associated 
accounting  
• 
Prerequisite and Materials Management – Prerequisites, such as parking data, is asset part of an embargo area, 
is a permit required to work on the asset or any special equipment needed, are set up for the work prior to the 
clerical effort required for dispatch. The materials are defined in the compatible units (CU’s) of work to be 
performed  
• 
Scheduling - The scheduling process starts with planning and forecasting the work, then scheduling. 
• 
Dispatching and Resource Management – Dispatching is an extension of the scheduling process where the work 
is dispatched to field forces and resources around this are managed. Mobile, Work Closure and Time Reporting. 
Justification Summary: 
 
In keeping with IT’s strategy of establishing a true “one enterprise” WMS platform for all operating areas, all legacy 
WMS systems are roadmapped to be migrated to the Maximo Platform including Electric WMS. In addition, potential 
risks associated with limitations in CGI’s capabilities to continue meeting Electric Operations’ changing needs with their 
ARM suite will be mitigated. 
 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
Long Range Plans 
A roadmap has been defined for legacy work and asset management systems which are running on  obsolete 
technology/and or are limited in capability and need extensive enhancements to address current and future business 
needs. These need to be migrated to the Maximo Enterprise Platform. The total number of systems identified is around 
45 applications which can be migrated within the next decade, including Electric WMS.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Do not migrate to Maximo but keep the limited WMS Logica implementation. This is not in keeping IT’s strategy for 
establishing a state of the art enterprise Work and Asset Mgt solution for all of Con Edison which fully meets/exceeds 
the current and growing needs of the business. 
 
 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Electric WMS has work management capability limitations. The product line cannot support the growing needs of the 
business.

2. Major financial benefits 
 
A 12 week assessment was done at a high level to determine the fit for Electric WMS and 19 other disparate legacy WMS 
systems to the "One Enterprise" Maximo platform and estimate the benefits of migrating (both quantifiable and non-
quantifiable. Of the quantifiable benefits, it was estimated that $52 million, on the conservative side, will be realized over 
a ten year period following the systems migration of all 20 legacy systems.

5. Conclusion 
 
The current system's platform vendor, CGI, is not investing in their technology roadmap and do not have a vision for 
future capabilities needed for work management. As such, their technology will likely be obsolete within 3 to 5 years 
(e.g., Powerbuilder)

business. Migrating to a "One Enterprise" WMS system will bring new and greater efficiencies, consolidated platform 
and system support, and the ability for the business to leverage new and innovative functionalities to meet its current 
and future needs.

Work Description: 
  
The objective of this program is to enhance the functionality of the Gas Work Management System (WMS)  by adding 
new functions, automation, and additional integrations to improve business processes. An example of new functions 
that will be implemented are: Operator Qualifications, Material Traceability, Fuse Tracking, Paving Schedule, Pre-
requisite Functionality, Auto Scheduling, etc.  These functions are needed to further achieve the goals and objectives of 
Gas Operations. Furthermore, other applications such as the new CSS (CORE) and the Graphical Information 
System (eGIS) have commenced implementation and enhancements are needed in Gas WMS to make the 
integration seamless.   
 
This program will also yield strategic benefits that support both corporate and Gas Operations’ goals and objectives. 
Some examples are an integrated view of financial and operational data resulting in more effective risk mitigation 
strategies, increased transparency, more effective trending and analysis, improved operational efficiencies, and an 
enhanced customer experience through more accurate and timely information around work flow and job status.  
 
Certain aspects of this program (particularly the Contractor Portal and OQ integration), will begin the road to 
compliance with certain aspects of proposed OQ rules recently re-released by DPS Staff. Of particular compliance 
concern is the proposed language related to 255.604(b)(2)(i), which requires detailed records kept, for the purposes of 
DPS Staff auditing, of work performed by non-qualified individuals. The above referenced program aspects are only the 
first step in compliance with this proposed rule; however, additional future programming will be needed to achieve 
compliance.

Justification Summary: 
 
Requirements for enhancements to Gas WMS (a CGI ARM application) and interfaces will be required as the Customer 
Information System (CIS) is replaced and the implementation of a Graphical Information System (GIS) is 
completed.  Along with new integrations and additional items that are not currently available in Gas WMS,  additional 
cost savings such as following are also planned: 
• 
GEM (Gas Work Management Mobility): 
o 
As updated are made in the ARM suite corresponding enhancements will need to be made to the GEM 
Mobile application to insure continuity for our production users.    
• 
OQ/Contactor Portal 
o 
Integration to contractor portal and OQ solution to capture operator qualification and field data from 
contractors into ARM  
• 
NYC DOT Paving Schedule: 
o 
Add an integration with ProceMX to receive the NYC DOT Paving schedule.  This will allow Con Ed to 
get any work on the block done before the NYC-DOT paves the block.  Con Edison can be liable for 
very high repaving costs when we excavate a recently paved street. 
• 
Fuse Tracking 
o 
Ability to bring fuse tracking into the ARM platform and leverage a cohesive WR system to identify 
details on fuses. 
o 
Eliminate additional licensing costs 
• 
Contractor Portal 
o 
Ability to have contractor interact with ARM through middle layer allowing for timely field data 
collection 
• 
CGI ARM Pre-Requisite Functionality: 
o 
Add functionality improvements to better understand the Pre-Requisites that need to be managed and 
the status of those Pre-Requisites to minimize delay time, created by items such as no access. 
• 
EBS Pre-Requisite Integrations: 
o 
Integrations with Oracle EBS to better understand the full cost of managing a Pre-Requisite such as 
Cone hive, Flagger, or NYC Parking signs.  Today it is very hard to marry these costs to the work that 
was done. 
• 
Auto Scheduling: 
o 
Develop an Auto Scheduling engine that will automate like and kind replacement work such as shunts, 
bridges, and open mains rather than needing significant planning and scheduling time from 
Schedulers, Work Organizers, and Clerical.  This automation will use the new CGI ARM Pre-Requisite 
functionality mentioned above. 
• 
Parking/access information: 
o 
Adding a mechanism to better capture parking data associated to the Facilities within Asset Manager 
and use that data to create a more effective work schedule. 
o 
automatically manage the Pre-Requisites and build out the Work Request for the pole replacement. 
• 
ARCOS: 
o 
ARCOS is a crew management software with a very sophisticated user interface.  The Work 
Management System has an application Called Central Configuration that allows for similar 
functionality but the user interface is very difficult to use.  As such, the clerical is updating crewing 
information such personnel assigned to the crew, shift pattern, training schedules, vacation, etc. in both 
systems.  We plan a bi-directional integration between ARCOS and ARM Central Configuration to 
eliminate this double entry. 
• 
HR Payroll: 
o 
HR Payroll intends migration from HR payroll to Oracle's HCM (Human Capital Management).  This 
will likely require retiring the existing WMS to HR Payroll integrations and replacing them with new.   
Additional reporting in Tableau to utilize the additional data being captured

Work Description: 
  
Information Technology has established a roadmap consisting of several work and asset management legacy 
applications to be migrated to Maximo. This is in keeping with IT’s strategy of moving to a “One Enterprise” Work and 
Asset Management solution for all of Con Edison, to realize the full benefits of a true enterprise solution across all 
business areas, as well as to address technology obsolescence and mitigate cyber risks.  
 
Maximo has been successfully implemented and has been in use in several business areas at Con Ed for many years: 
Central Operations, Steam, and Transmission Ops. In 2021 the platform was upgraded and the Controlled Enterprise 
license, which had some limitations in terms of the number of Maximo products licensed and the business areas 
covered, was re-negotiated to a true enterprise model which gives Con Edison and its affiliates use of any/all modules 
within the Maximo work and asset management suite of products. With this unrestricted use of the product line and 
total user base coverage, we are looking to extend the current use of the implemented Maximo, eliminate disparate 
legacy systems which are challenging and costly to maintain, many currently running on obsolete technologies, and 
continue to build out and improve on the current functionalities  
 
There are a total of 17 migrations to be done in 6 years. The current assumption is we will implement based on the 
timeline below. 
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 69 of 118


--- Page 150 ---
 
 
The dollars requested in the rate case were determined based on a Legacy WMS Portfolio (17 Applications) assessment 
done by Cognizant International as a starting point. This assessment estimated at a very high level, the feasibility and 
cost of migrating all 17 applications to Enterprise Maximo. The estimated migration cost is $61M.  However, this did not 
include all legacy WMS applications/functionalities currently in use throughout Con Edison via legacy applications as 
well as paper processes. The dollars requested are based on Cognizant’s estimate plus dollars and contingency added to 
fill the gap listed above. The additional contingency added was $26M. 
Some of the legacy systems/requirements not included in this assessment are: 
1. Migrate IT Infrastructure and Operations Paper Processes to Maximo 
2. Migrate IT Corporate Security Paper Processes to Maximo 
3. Additional Enhancements 
• 
Facilities (MOC Integration, Inspection Forms, Mobility and Engage Integration 
4. Implement OOWP (Operating Orders and Work Permits) for LNG 
5. Migrate Capital Tools application and paper processes to Maximo 
 
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
There are several legacy work management systems in CECONY which are running on obsolete  
technologies and present a cyber risk unless re-written or replaced. These need to be migrated to  
Maximo. Others are limited in functionality and simply need to be migrated to Maximo to be able to leverage new and 
advanced WMS capabilities, a consolidated application and platform support, and to realize new efficiencies now and 
accommodate future needs.

A total of 52M of cost avoidance and financial benefits were estimated.

5. Conclusion 
 
IT currently supports a wide portfolio of disparate WMS legacy applications. Many are running on obsolete technologies 
while others have reached their functional limitations and can no longer adequately support the current and growing 
needs of the business. This raises cybersecurity concerns. Cyber-attacks have increasingly targeted critical infrastructure 
providers. Malicious actors have increased their capabilities, and such attacks can cause serious disruption to the 
operation of the Company’s corporate IT network, operational networks, and critical energy infrastructure. Obsolete 
systems lack the ability to allow the Company to leverage the latest cybersecurity tools such as advanced monitoring and 
alerting and multifactor access control. Replacing these systems will allow us to modernize cyber controls such as these. 
This cybersecurity risk is compounded by the dwindling number of skilled resources with the background to support 
the obsolete technology in the legacy applications. Due to the cybersecurity risk, and because the current asset 
management practices and business processes are not sustainable, it is critical to pursue this project during the 
upcoming rate case.

Work Description: 
  
In March 2018, two consecutive nor’easters struck our service territory damaging our distribution electrical system. 
Several compounding factors lead to issues with the Outage Management System (OMS) landscape negatively affecting 
our customer’s experience. The Company put together a Storm Assessment Team to analyze Con Edison’s response to 
the weather events and engaged McKinsey and Company to conduct a technical review of the OMS landscape and an 
evaluation of the Customer Outage Journey. These efforts produced a list of suggested corrective actions. The goal of 
this project is to address these suggestions and any other PSC orders. The work can be categorized into seven work 
streams. 
• 
Technology – Address current technology issues. 
• 
Architecture – Re-architect or correct current system design issues and set standard for future projects.  
• 
Data Optimization – Correct and set data standards for integration between systems, 
• 
IT Process Management Tool – Improve maturity of core IT processes. 
• 
End to End testing environments – Build environment and test procedure that allow full system testing and 
validation of business rules. 
• 
Standards & Governance - Define enterprise enforcement and implementation standards for application, 
integration and infrastructure. 
• 
Business Led Technology – Transform current business process to work with existing technology.  
This opportunity will be used to excel at the basics (e.g., increase system stability) while also laying the foundation for 
advanced capabilities and new systems implementation (e.g., GIS), and enhancing the customer experience.  
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 75 of 118


--- Page 156 ---
Justification Summary: 
 
This program is in direct response to technical and systematic issues experience during winter storms Riley and Quinn 
identified by Storm Assessment Team and the McKinsey study. The proposed enhancements will both correct current 
technical gaps as well as set the building blocks for future integrations, enhancements, and testing. 
The hardware/infrastructure upgrade will enable High Availability (HA) architecture mitigating the need for 
prolonged maintenance outages for software patching, as well as significant reduction in Disaster Recovery (DR) times 
during failover. To implement the HA architecture, the Company will deploy the new Exadata hardware which is 
Oracle's latest platform for hosting databases. In addition, the Company will deploy virtual infrastructure (Nutanix) to 
support the new environments. These platforms will increase system performance and recovery times. The new HA 
architecture will include additional test environments that closely match production environments and will increase the 
Company's capacity to undertake additional testing.  
Develop an OMS DR option to further strengthen availability, resiliency and scalability of our OMS systems. 
 
The Company has also committed to perform semi-annual OMS end to end testing in order to comply with a PSC 
requirement that came out of the Riley/Quinn Winter storms in 2018. Following the Tropical Storm Isaias storm in 
August 2020, the PSC has directed NYS utilities to additionally conduct testing of their OMS systems to simulate 90% 
customer impact. As a result of these ever-increasing testing requirements, the Company will make investments in its 
systems and processes to support these testing initiatives in 2021 and beyond. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
A robust OMS platform is a key input to the Company’s OMS Storm Hardening initiatives. Key investments in a modern 
high availability architecture maintain the OMS under peak system usage which is essential during storms of ever-
increasing intensity. In addition, the OMS software upgrade will further enhance the user experience and keep the 
Company current regarding the vendor’s product offering.   
 
Following the Riley/Quinn Winter Storms in March 2018, the NYPSC directed all NYS utilities to conduct semi-annual 
end-to-end testing of their OMS suite of applications. This requirement was added as a Key Risk Indicator for the 
Company and incorporated in Company’s Emergency Response Plan (ERP). Following Tropical Storm Isaias, the NYPSC 
took this requirement a step further and directed all NYS Utilities to conduct end-to-end testing of their OMS systems 
simulating an outage impacting 90% of their customers. To meet this new requirement now and into the future, the 
Company must continue to invest in robust testing environment and processes.

Work Description:  
The goal is to implement Oracle E-Business (EBS) Cloud and retire the existing local Enterprise Resource Planning 
(ERP) solutions. For Oracle EBS, all business requirements will be reviewed and validated. Gaps in functionality will be 
evaluated and solutions determined. The adoption of Cloud applications requires standardized processes and is 
expected that configurations resolve most gaps. The Oracle EBS System has 515 Con Edison-specific modifications to the 
base system, which require evaluation and testing. These modifications change how the system works to conform to 
Con Edison’s business practices. 118 Functional Extensions 121 Inbound Interfaces 99 Outbound Interfaces 149 Custom 
Reports 28 Custom Workflows. Testing will include all finance and supply chain functions, interfaces to other Con 
Edison systems, and external systems such as banks and vendors. The information currently stored on-premises in the 
EBS system will be converted to Oracle's cloud solution.  
 
A Phase 0 assessment will assist in determining the scope of the EBS move to the cloud. It enables the Company to:  
• Understand and capture the functional and technical components of the cloud environment  
• Clarify the purpose, goals, and expected benefits of the cloud implementation  
• Perform a holistic review of all cloud modules and applications sharing a single instance and tenancy across the 
enterprise  
• Derive Key Design Decisions (KDD) 
• Obtain a gap-fit analysis  
• Determine the scope of, and organizational readiness for, desired larger-scale changes such as Projects modules 
redesign; implementation of Oracle Assets for asset accounting; and redesign of the chart of account structure.  
• Understand the extent of time, investment, and resources required to plan for a 2024/2025 go-live  
• Identify mandatory business change as a result of descoped customization  
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 82 of 118


--- Page 163 ---
 
• Provide early-on business change management via proof of concepts of new/changed functionality, access to 
experience the new look, and canvassed feedback  
• Identify business drivers for required customization and determine feasibility – such as Complex Service Purchase 
Orders  
• Contribute to the completeness of the scope included in the formal Request for Proposal to implement the Cloud 
migration. 
 
 In addition, Consolidated Edison Inc. entered an Oracle Strategic Partnership (OSP), which aligns with Con Edison’s 
strategic business cost optimization, enhances operational efficiency, and improves customer experience through 
technology innovation. It supports Con Edison ability to:  
• Innovate on new technologies that benefit Oracle's industry leadership and enable Con Edison to improve business 
processes and customer service  
• Deliver and adopt software and services that are best-in-class for scope, functionality, performance, and quality  
• Collaborate utilizing Con Edison's knowledge of the industry to assist Oracle in improving their solutions and Oracle 
system knowledge to determine critical solution design decisions and 
• Prioritize work that focuses on the highest value for both companies  
Justification Summary: 
 
Oracle's strategic direction is to migrate all on-premises solutions to their cloud platform. Oracle is devoting most of 
their development resources to the cloud, with limited spend on local software. This means that on-premises software 
will have a time lag in bug fixes and eventually will not be enhanced.  
If Con Edison does not perform this migration, supply chain and finance operations will be susceptible to delays in 
enhancements and bug fixes.  It will also require periodic and costly upgrades to the local software. 
 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
Risk 1 Name: Department.Information Technology.Unsupported technology in computer systems 
Risk 1 Description:  
The software vendor, Oracle, is moving all their applications to the cloud. Oracle EBS has been available on the cloud for 
several years. By 2021 it will be a mature product while Con Edison's on premise version will be obsoleting.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Con Edison could maintain the current local solution or delay the migration to the cloud. These alternatives would 
require Con Edison to maintain a technical support staff as well as maintain on-premises infrastructure such as storage, 
networking, and servers.   
 
Risk of No Action: 
. 
Risk 1 
Con Edison's investment in the Oracle EBS would depreciate as Oracle devotes more time and resources to their cloud 
solutions relative to their on premise solutions.  Although the on-process Oracle EBS would continue to work, it will not 
improve as quickly as the cloud solution.  
Risk 2 
If a Phase 0 assessment is not performed, there is a risk that major uptakes, key design decisions and scope 
considerations may be overlooked as we embark on the cloud migration project.   
There would also be significant impacts to the actual implementation timeline due to lack of clarity on the project scope, 
business process gaps (fit-gap analysis) and key design decisions that would be achieved in Phase 0.   
These oversights could result in disruption to the business and post migration implementation costs. 
 
 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
 
Oracle's current cloud user interface has a modern look and feel. During the next few years, the cloud product will 
continue to evolve and improve. The timing of the project will provide Con Edison with a mature yet modern solution. 
One example is the standardization of work flow approvals in the cloud.  The on-premises Oracle EBS has a different 
method of implementing workflows which increase the system complexity and cost.  The cloud version has a simpler 
and more efficient workflow process.  This would help to speed ordering, receipting of goods, and payments. 
  
Increased safety, reliability and efficiency 
  
The cloud product support's the Company's ability to: 
• 
Continue to focus on technological innovation and effective and efficient support systems 
• 
Continue to produce clear, accurate and timely financials for both internal and external customers and reduce 
the risk of misstatements in Corporate Accounting 
• 
Continue to provide cost savings and productivity savings in Finance and Operations

•

Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup) 
1. Cost-benefit analysis (if required) 
 
There will be savings/cost avoidance over a five-year period after implementation. These will come from the process 
improvement in the major Supply Chain work streams: Supplier Enablement, iProcurement, Sourcing, Order 
Management, iSupplier Portal, OBN, and Inventory. Additional savings/cost avoidance will result from the Accounting 
and Finance work streams: Payables, iExpense, Receivables, iReceivables, General Ledger, Assets, Cash Management, 
Project Costing, Advanced Collections, eBTax and Project Billing  
Our software vendor, Oracle is committed to improving their Supply Chain and Finance platform.  We have witnessed 
this with their introduction of the Account Reconciliation module that is only available on the Cloud.  Cloud platforms 
offer more functionality and current technology without the need for financial investments in hardware and internal 
resources to support an on-premises application.  Performing Supply Chain and Finance functions is fundamental and 
operationally required for all companies and a cloud platform will provide the most cost-efficient way to continue 
providing these required services.   
The remaining savings/cost avoidance will be achieved as more of Con Edison's system are hosted on the same cloud 
platform.  Already, Con Edison has moved the Budgeting and Forecasting, BI Cloud and Project Management 
(Primavera) to Oracle's Cloud. Soon CEB's will have their financial system in Oracle's Cloud.   
In addition, implementing the Oracle solution provides the added incentive of utilizing the Oracle Strategic Partnership 
and realizing the cloud credits upon implementation and also by retiring our on-premises Oracle EBS application. 
 
 
2. Major financial benefits 
 
Eliminate the need to upgrade the on-premises application which should happen every 2 to 3 years. This would also 
eliminate the need to upgrade the servers every 5 or 6 years. 
The estimated total cost of the Oracle EBS ERP cloud migration is $127 million which is reflected in the requested five 
year budget detailed in this whitepaper.  The $127 million is spread over the 2021 ($1.5 million), 2022 ($7.1 million), 2023 
($50.6 million) and 2024 ($66.4 million) and 2025 ($1.4 million) budget years. 
The Capital Project will require the 7.3% of the cost to be allocated to Orange and Rockland Utilities.

Work Description: 
  
The scope of this project includes the replacement of Peoplesoft’s HCM and CRM applications (the HR Payroll and 
myHR Connection systems), the consolidation of disparate HR systems to a single platform, the development of 
advanced and predictive workforce analytics and the creation of a long-term workforce data platform to store 35 years 
of electronic history and new data from the HCM Cloud. The HR Payroll system was implemented in 2009 as an on-
premise solution and it is the responsibility of the Company to maintain and upgrade the system when the version is no 
longer supported by Oracle, every three to four years. It is also the Company’s responsibility to purchase and maintain 
hardware to house the production and all the test environments. The support provided by Oracle includes security 
patches, tax update and upgrades to the underlying technology called PeopleTools. Furthermore, there is a complex 
manual effort to gather and consolidate data to produce basic workforce analytic reports used to make data driven 
staffing decisions and manage succession planning. These factors increase risk and decrease efficiency and effectiveness 
of workforce planning. In 2018 the Company signed a Strategic Partnership with Oracle to support the company’s 
technology which includes the subscription fee for the Human Capital Management (HCM) Cloud application which 
resulted in HR and Information Technology (IT) completing a rapid assessment to determine the level of effort and cost 
estimates to consolidate and migrate all employee related business processes to the Oracle HCM Cloud. The assessment 
included how the Company will reduce compliance risk, support enhanced business practices, increase the efficiency by 
offering mobile applications, create advanced workforce analytics, create a long-term data archive and replace obsolete 
HR and Learning and Inclusion (L&I) systems. 
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 89 of 118


--- Page 170 ---
 
Justification Summary: 
 
Migrating to Oracle HCM Cloud will provide new functionality for employees and eliminate the need to maintain and 
upgrade our on premise application and hardware. 
The implementation of the HCM Cloud, will result in both tangible (quantitative) and intangible (qualitative) benefits.  
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
 
Risk 1 Name: Corporate 
ConEd.Operations.Cybersecurity 
Risk 1 Description:  
Oracle releases quarterly updates to the HCM Cloud for 
security patches, application updates and tax and compliance 
updates.  In the Cloud environment Oracle will be pushing 
these changes into the system and IT Support teams will no 
longer be required to download and apply these patches.  
Updates will need to be reviewed, tested and accepted by the 
HR Payroll Support team then applied by Oracle on a quarterly 
basis.  This process increases the efficiency of applying system 
updates to remain in compliance with required regulations or 
changes to the law.

Alternatives: 
 
Phased Implementation  
This alternative would delay a portion of the investment summarized above but would be costlier over the long run and 
delay the benefits of fully integrated and standardized employee processes and system implemented across the 
company.   
Multi-Year Postponement  
An alternative to postpone the HCM Cloud implementation for two or more years.  This alternative would prolong the 
Company's ability to address the risks and inefficiencies associated with the current environment and realize the 
benefits of a recently negotiated agreement with Oracle.  
Risk of No Action: 
 
One alternative that was considered was to maintain the status quo and to use and maintain the current, separate 
systems that support employee, contractors and retiree processes. This alternative would expose the Company to the 
Exhibit___(IT-1)

following risks: 
• 
Highly manual process for onboarding, succession planning and workforce analytics with increased chances for 
errors and mismanagement

tasks by employees and managers.  i.e., performance reviews, timesheet entry and approvals. 
• 
Support of homegrown HR systems has significantly reduced over time making the development of new 
enhancements or the maintenance of compliance related functionality difficult.   
•

consolidated view of workforce data to support effective analysis and decision making.

Regulatory Mandated/ Reduce and Manage Risks 
Oracle releases quarterly updates to the HCM Cloud for security patches, application updates and tax updates.  In the 
Cloud environment Oracle will be pushing these changes into the system and IT Support teams will no longer be 
required to download and apply these patches.  Updates will need to be reviewed, tested and accepted by the HR 
Payroll Support team then applied by Oracle on a quarterly basis.  This process of increase the efficiency of applying 
system updates to always remain in compliance with all required regulations or changes to the law.  
Operationally Required 
A deferral of this project would have consequences on the existing HR Payroll System. The support and maintenance for 
PeopleTools will expire in January 2023 and the system will require an upgrade. Without the upgrade, security patches 
will longer be available leaving the system vulnerable for a CyberSecurity attack. 
Improve Customer Experience:  
The HCM Cloud platform offers the ability to deliver a modern experience for users via displaying content as tiles and 
on mobile devices.  This will allow for the deployment of the employee and manager self-service transactions to mobile 
devices. This will enhance self-service to field employees thus reducing call volume in the call center and productive 
time of the HR Professionals.  
Moving all employee related business functions to a consolidated platform will provide a single place for employees to 
manager their personal information and for managers to gain insight into their team.   
Enhance External Relationships:  
Migrating to HCM Cloud will ensure long term sustainability of the Company's payroll/time keeping process.  Oracle's 
support is now providing updates and patches to cloud applications first before traditional on premise applications such 
as PeopleSoft illustrating Oracle's support priorities.   
Reduce Costs and Strengthen the Company Processes:   
The HCM Cloud will give field employees the ability to use self-service functionality anywhere at any time. The mobile 
applications will increase employee productive time as they will no longer need to come into the office, log onto a 
computer to make simple changes, such as change of address. In addition, the latest software version allows for 
improved performance with regard to reporting processing time and improved dashboard capabilities, which will allow 
for more streamlined business processes.

Work Description: 
• 
  
From 2021 through 2025, continuous efforts to identify and incorporate enhancements within the modules utilized by 
the OMS system will supplement efforts to better identify opportunities for enhanced operator training. The Company 
will undertake a software upgrade of the Oracle Network Management System (NMS) system to the latest version 2.5. 
This upgrade will deliver enhanced operator functionality that increases ease of use and additional automation 
capabilities. This software upgrade is also critical to the continued stability, reliability, and resiliency of the OMS. This 
also enables the Company to take full advantage of new enhancements offered by the OMS product line as well as 
ensuring adequate support in terms of service packs and patches from the vendor. The Company plans to implement 
the Oracle Mobile Application (OMA) platform. We believe that the move to these enterprise class systems will allow us 
to continue to meet the increasing demands and changes in the industry. In addition, collaboration with other utilities 
and vendors has demonstrated the need to regularly upgrade associated software to remain in alignment with product 
improvements and changing industry technologies as well as avoiding exposure to unsupported hardware and 
software. Additionally, there are other modules that are currently not used by the Company, that need to continue to be 
evaluated for further enhancements on how we do business. Expected growth and development in Distributed Energy 
Resources and REV initiatives is expected to drive opportunities for improvement in the OMS systems utilized by the 
operators in order to better understand the impact the effect of these systems on the distribution system.  
Justification Summary: 
 
Oracle NMS version 2.5 is a leading end to end distribution management platform with advance optimization, outage 
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 96 of 118


--- Page 177 ---
and field management capabilities. The NMS 2.5 upgrade will provide high availability and reliability at local and 
remote sites. The updated version allows for faster routine patching and faster failover to a remote site. This will 
improve operational efficiency in performing common outage updates and completing action using the right click 
menusuch as updating the estimated time of restoration or assigning or updating the crew status. The Company will 
also pursue configuration of the monitoring system within the NMS application. In addition, this upgrade will provide 
a better user experience, that includes application supporting low-lit and daytime work environments. 
OMS GIS Integration will help replace existing custom model extractor process with Oracle's standard ESRI adapter to 
import GIS assets and their associated connectivity model, which in turn should help with both standardization and 
enhanced support and reliability. In addition, with the GIS integration, assets within OMS will be stored and visualized 
in real world co-ordinates which will help improve outage accuracy and allow future opportunities to further enhance 
processes like Damage Assessment, Site safety and Outage Analytics. 
Operations Mobile Application (OMA) brings a central set of NMS functionality for field crews to view, allowing crews 
to assess damage, update estimated restoration time, capture cause, resolve, and close out outage restoration activities. 
Tasks and safety documents are organized in separate tabs, along with this, users will have easy navigation to and from 
the network map. The application will be effortless for the users and efficient application leading to a smoother 
restoration effort.

Technical Evaluation/ Analysis 
 
Con Edison is committed to developing best practice outage restoration processes and information systems.  These 
processes and systems help facilitate the correct assessment of customer outages, effective restoration planning, and 
timely return of service to customers.  The Company continues to make significant improvement in its ability to quickly 
understand the number of customers impacted by power disturbances and provide customers with timely information 
on restoration times.  These accomplishments were achieved through a series of process improvements and 
enhancements of the Outage Management suite of systems including STAR, which is based on Oracle's Distribution 
Management System software suite.  The Oracle product continues to be one of the leading outage management 
software suites and is utilized worldwide by many large utilities. The technical evaluation considered the following 
activities that are expected to be evaluated and implemented over the upcoming years: 
• 
Continue to implement additional functionality available to improve the accuracy of customer ETRs. 
• 
Use of the mobile application to allow field crews to update ETRs, and provide outage causes to customers. 
• 
Investigate and implement improvements as required for Damage Assessment to enhance remote damage data 
capture and interfaces with STAR or other OMS solutions for the timely development of work plan and 
customer level ETR's.   
• 
Implement improvements to enhance training capabilities by creating more e-learning modules, and quick 
videos while providing additional in-class training for OMS processes and systems.  
• 
Continue efforts to maintain alignment with major software release upgrades.

Other projects that have close relationships include all applications related to improving how the Company manages 
Customer interfaces and related communications including the Customer Project Management System (CPMS), Work 
Management System (WMS), the Outage Management Dashboard (BI) and external Customer Portal.

Work Description: 
   
The scope of this project is to purchase and implement a protective relay settings repository software solution.  The 
settings repository will be the sole source of truth for relay settings and asset information for the Company’s protective 
relay systems.  This initiative will also replace legacy systems that house protective relay information, and will also need 
to be Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) compliant.  This includes protective relays across the electric transmission 
and distribution systems, as well as related equipment such as instrument transformers, communication lines and control 
circuits. In addition to protective relays, other systems such as SCADA and disturbance monitoring may be incorporated. 
The settings repository will be integrated with other systems such as Maximo, Logica and CAPE (Computer Aided 
Protection Engineering). A settings management workflow will be development and implemented using the software. 
Additionally, automated relay testing and settings verification features will be developed and deployed as part of this 
project. 
 
Please refer to exhibit below that explains the project in more detail: 
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 102 of 118


--- Page 183 ---
 
Justification Summary: 
 
Benefits of a relay settings repository include the following: 
· Perform extent of condition analysis on relay or settings issues 
· Track and trend relay system performance history and metrics 
· Deploy a mature settings management process with baseline configuration controls 
· Implement automated testing features 
· Automatically verify correct settings are in each relay 
· Improved lifecycle management of relays 
 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
This project aligns with the Company’s long-term goals of using asset management principles to improve asset performance 
while decreasing lifecycle costs.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Relay settings could be stored in existing databases such as Maximo or CAPE. However, this would require a high level of 
customization to incorporate all the needed features. An off-the-shelf settings repository would not have this issue and 
would be integrated to other systems as needed. 
 
Risk of No Action: 
 
1. Lack of robust settings management and documentation leads to settings errors, lack of understanding of deployed relay 
settings, which ultimately leads to increased risk for relay misoperations and loss of a substation. 
2. Unable to perform extent of condition analysis on relay settings issues 
3. Increasing NERC compliance obligations such as testing and coordination are made manageable through a relay database.

forces by not having to supply personnel which would take away from the day-to-day obligations. This solution is 
significantly more efficient than the current paper-based process.  Lack of robust settings management and documentation 
leads to settings errors and lack of understanding of deployed relay settings, which ultimately lead to increased risk for relay 
misoperations and loss of a substation.  This solution enforces and streamlines relaying standards across the enterprise.  This 
database will also streamline the Preventative Maintenance being performed on relays, instead of tracking the testing by 
zones of protection we can track by individual relay type and reduce redundant periodic maintenance.

Work Description: 
  
This program funds the technology improvements needed to upgrade, enhance, automate, or establish substation 
processes with the goal of increasing safety, efficiency, and improving reliability.   Substation Operations has 
established numerous procedures, instructions, and guidelines to ensure the safe operation and maintenance of the 
equipment.  Numerous processes have been developed to ensure adherence to a governing course of action involve 
data/information collection, transfer, and storage.  As technology advances, this program serves to identify and take 
advantage of opportunities to improve the efficiency of these processes by implementing new tools or upgrading 
existing ones to enhance how data is collected, transferred, and/or stored. 
Justification Summary: 
 
The implementation and upgrade of new technology is instrumental in ensuring Substation Operations continually 
improves efficiency and reliability.  The use of technology to streamline processes results in better resource utilization 
and a reduction in task time requirements.  Better data collection, and storage, facilitates enhanced data analysis and 
trending which ultimately leads to improved reliability and equipment performance. 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
This project is in alignment with corporate goals of leveraging automation and technology and utilizing enterprise 
solutions to lower business costs.

Alternatives: 
 
An alternative would be to do nothing.  The reason for rejecting this alternative is because implementation and 
upgrades of technology are vital to ensuring safe, efficient, and reliable operation of the transmission system.  
Risk of No Action: 
 
The risk of no action is as follows: 
• 
Increased probability of loss of substation due to failure to update technology of critical systems/processes. 
• 
Increased probability of environmental release from a substation due to failure to update technology of critical 
systems/processes.  
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
 
• 
Improved reliability due to hardware and software tools. 
• 
Improved employee development and engagement by ensuring current technologies are utilized in the 
workplace. 
• 
Promotion of technology through mobile computing and automation. 
• 
Lower risk of unsupported operationally required software.

Work Description: 
  
The Work Management Project including process change, organization restructuring and the deployment of CGI-Logica 
ARM Suite (Work Manager, Scheduler, Central Configuration, Asset Manager and Mobile Field Manager) completed 
project implementation at the end of the fourth quarter 2014. 
 
Enhancements to the CGI-Logica application and interfaces will be required as the Customer Information System (CIS) 
is replaced and a Graphical Information System (GIS) is implemented.  New integrations and automation to facilitate 
cost savings such as the following are also planned: 
•   NYC DOT Paving Schedule: 
o 
Add an integration with ProceMX to receive the NYC DOT Paving schedule.  This will allow Con Edison to get 
work on the block done before the NYC DOT paves the block.  Con Edison can be liable for repaving costs when 
we excavate a recently paved street. 
•   CGI ARM Pre-Requisite Functionality: 
o 
Add functionality improvements to better understand the Pre-Requisites that need to be managed and the 
status of those Pre-Requisites to minimize delay time such as no access need for flushes. 
•   EBS Pre-Requisite Integrations: 
o 
Integrations with Oracle EBS to better understand the full cost of managing a Pre-Requisite such as Flaggers, or 
NYC Parking signs.  Currently it is difficult to marry these costs to the work that was done. 
•   Auto Scheduling: 
o 
Develop an Auto Scheduling engine that will automate like and kind replacement work such as shunts, bridges, 
and open mains rather than needing significant planning and scheduling time from Schedulers, Work 
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 113 of 118


--- Page 194 ---
 
Organizers, and Clerical.  This automation will use the new CGI ARM Pre-Requisite functionality mentioned 
above. 
•   Parking/access information: 
o 
Adding a mechanism to better capture parking data associated to the Facilities within Asset Manager and use 
that data to create a more effective work schedule. 
•   Enhanced STAR Referral: 
o 
Enhancing the STAR Referral interface to automatically build out a WR based on required data entry by the 
STAR user making the referral.  This will eliminate the time necessary to manually building out the WR. 
•   NJUNS: 
o 
We are required to make notification to the various entities that are attached to poles of our intent to replace a 
pole and the status of this work.  Significant time is spent by Regional Engineering, Overhead First Line 
Supervisors, and Clerical manually updating the data within the National Joint Utility Notification System 
(NJUNS).  We plan to build integrations to automate this work based on progressing the Work Request. 
•   Periodic Pole Inspection and Treatment: 
o 
We are required to test the structural integrity of our poles at least once every 12 years.  This program is called 
Periodic Pole Inspection and Treatment.  Presently this work is managed outside of the Electric Work 
Management System and requires manual entry of the rejected poles into the Work Management System.  We 
also do not have records withing the Work management System of the results of those inspections.  We also are 
not having the inspection vendor capture the information necessary to help us manage the Pre-Requisites such 
as parking/access to replace the defective pole.  We plan to have the vendor capture the Pre-Requisite 
information and also the specifics of the pole so we can automatically manage the Pre-Requisites and build out 
the Work Request for the pole replacement. 
•   ARCOS: 
o 
ARCOS is a crew management software with a very sophisticated user interface.  The Work Management 
System has an application Called Central Configuration that allows for similar functionality but the user 
interface is difficult to use.  As such, clerical is updating crewing information such as personnel assigned to the 
crew, shift pattern, training schedules, vacation, etc. in both systems.  We plan a bi-directional integration 
between ARCOS and ARM Central Configuration to eliminate this double entry. 
•   HR Payroll: 
o 
HR Payroll intends migration from HR payroll to Oracle’s HCM (Human Capital Management).  This will likely 
require retiring the existing WMS to HR Payroll integrations and replacing them.   
•   Pole Survey: 
o 
A joint pole survey between Con Edison, Verizon, and the various pole attachers will result in new data such as 
the pole owner, what entities are attached to the pole, and if there are any safety concerns.  This survey data will 
require integration to the Electric Work Management System and applicable data.  
•   SEAPOT: 
o 
Add integrations with SEAPOT to create work in WMS to: 
 
Cut and abandon mains that are likely to fail based on age or previous failure history. 
 
Group the above with required PSC repairs to bundle cost  
 
Additional reporting in Oracle BI by modification of Oracle Project Accounting interface will also be reviewed.  A more 
effective solution to “Tableau” data analysis and reporting will be considered with a possible migration to the Oracle 
BIEE reporting environment. 
Future upgrades 
• 
Hardware upgrades of approximately $200 k are necessary to support enhancing the system performance as well as 
adding additional servers to support new initiatives such as OMP enabled applications and ORDS reporting 
functionality. 
• 
Additionally the Exadata hardware is three years old and will need additional storage and processor capability 
upgrades. 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
The original implementation of WMS had a business case that drove both Capital and O&M cost savings and paid for 
its implementation within five years.  The WMS Sustainability Project continues that work by implementing new 
Exhibit___(IT-1)
Page 114 of 118


--- Page 195 ---
 
functionality, automation, and integrations to improve business processes that reduce delays (and therefore, improve 
productivity), improve visibility into the costs/delays associate with pre-requisite management, reduce field work and 
administrative backlogs, etc.  There are also other Capital programs such as GIS and the new HR Payroll system.  WMS 
Sustainability also funds the WMS side of those programs.  WMS Sustainability also funds necessary hardware 
replacements.

Work Description: 
  
This project is a replacement of the existing Allegro transaction system, which is required in order integrate the risk 
module into our new FIS Aligne Procurement / Settlement System .   The vendor chosen must meet the requirements of 
purchasing, scheduling, accounting for and reporting of financial and physical power transactions. The vendor chosen 
through a request for quote process will meet those requirements. In addition, the corporate effort to consolidate 
standalone applications will be reviewed as the selected system has the ability to process financial transactions. 
Justification Summary: 
 
 
The current Allegro system is the main tool to manage the Company's financial and physical power hedge 
portfolio.  The current version of Allegro performs the following tasks and this software or its replacement requires 
enhancements and has the potential opportunity to automate processes:  
• 
Energy Management maintains a $2 billion supply portfolio, and requires a supportable software platform to 
track and schedule the trade life cycle – trade entry, credit risk management, trade confirmation, invoice 
generation and trade settlement, and accounting. 
• 
The Energy Management business changes frequently and requires a flexible platform to accommodate new 
business opportunities. 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 2 of 185


--- Page 201 ---
• 
The proposed solution will continue with automation of accounting functions such as Accounts Payable (AP), 
Accounts Receivable (AR), and General Ledger (GL). 
• 
Energy Management and Energy Risk Management require strict compliance with Sarbanes Oxley (SOX) 
controls, and audit capabilities. 
• 
For this process, an evaluation will be made to leverage and modify existing trade systems for financial and 
physical power transactions, which in theory may be significantly less costly. This would result in all trades 
being in a single system, which is best practices. However, this is an evaluation that will be done at that time.  
• 
The Allegro System needs to be replaced because we are transferring the Allegro function to the new FIS Aligne 
Procurement / Settlement System which is expected to go live in early 2022. Integration of the risk module into 
the new system eliminates multiple data entry and touch points, reduces the chance for errors, and increases 
process efficiencies.  
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
Risk 1 Name: Department.Finance.Compliance 
Risk 1 Description:  
The credit monitoring system sets limits on the amount of 
business we can enter into with a single counterparty.  This 
feature ensures compliance that limits are not exceeded. 
Risk 2 Name: Corporate ConEd.Regulatory and 
Compliance.Fraud 
Risk 2 Description:  
The credit function determines which counterparties we can do 
business with.  This reduces the opportunity for fraud or third 
party risk to occur.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
The alternative to this project is to not update the system which would ultimately mean lack of vendor support for the 
system in 2023 and to hire additional employees to process the transactions along the trade lifecycle. This is a Sarbanes 
Oxley system. 
Risk of No Action: 
The risk of no action would be the inability to provide a flexible power transaction processing platform to meet the needs 
of our customers. 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
Efficient management of energy portfolio, reduced errors, proper and accurate financial reporting, and standardized 
reports (internal & external) 
Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup)

2. Major financial benefits 
 
The financial benefits of this project are increased productivity, enhanced functionality, and continued ability to support 
regulatory requirements by using a vendor supported software platform. 
3. Total Cost ($000) 
 
The total capital cost of $3.5 M includes hiring a vendor to design, build, and deploy the replacement software, hiring of  
a System Integrator, UAT Coordinator, Documentation and Report Writer, software license and modernization to the 
cloud, and internal Con Edison IT and project management support. 
4. Basis for estimate 
Cost estimates were put together with the assistance of subject matter experts and costs associated with 
similar internal projects.
