Work Description: 
The Analytics Center of Excellence manages and supports the Company’s Enterprise Data Analytics Platform (EDAP), a 
central data repository and analytics engine delivering advanced analytics solutions to the enterprise. EDAP integrates 
Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), customer, outage, work management, and other systems to build a 
comprehensive view of the data and performs analytics to provide users operational insights. As users’ analytical skills 
mature and the demand for near-real-time analytics for operational use increases, EDAP must upgrade its system 
infrastructure to improve its resiliency and reliability, lower recovery time during outages, increase overall 
performance, accommodate more ad hoc analytics, and enable self-service analytics capabilities.  EDAP supports key 
Company analytics initiatives, including Grid Mod Data Analytics and Customer Data and Analytics and is a key 
component to support various initiatives around DERMS, IEDR and clean energy goals. 
This project seeks to expand existing technical capabilities to further the Company goals of finding new opportunities 
for cost savings, risk reduction, and improvements to safety and customer experience. This will include the streamlining 
of data access and sharing across platform components from consolidating into a single cloud environment, increased 
flexibility by enabling new components that allow further development of custom application interfaces, increased 
precision through the deployment of technologies to track model accuracy over time and streamlined deployment 
through the building of mechanisms to integrate analytical results into operational systems and processes. 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 8 of 185


--- Page 207 ---
Justification Summary: 
The Analytics Center of Excellence (ACE) is the Company’s centralized team supporting Data and Analytics initiatives.  
ACE’s mission is to enable and deliver data-driven insights across the Company; a key component of the strategy for 
executing this mission is growing and managing the analytics technologies needed to support business use cases and 
enable innovation.  EDAP is comprised of a suite of technologies to deliver enterprise analytics capabilities, such as big 
data processing, centralizing raw data, building and sharing datasets, modeling and forecasting, and self-service 
analysis and reporting.  The platform ingests data from systems across the Company, transforms it, performs analytics, 
and provides insights to business users.  
Over the past two years, user demand for analytics has increased dramatically, particularly for self-service analytics 
across large data sets, such as AMI metering, work management, outage, network, and customer information.  Users not 
only require historical data to be readily accessible for analytics, but there is also an increased demand to have the most 
up to date results available for situational awareness and proactive analytics.  This increase in demand is driven not 
only by predefined analytics projects but includes ad-hoc requests to analyze Company data to improve safety, 
operational excellence, and customer experience (i.e., using EDAP to investigate an issue with a smart meter 
installation).  To meet this increased demand, support new business use cases, EDAP upgrades, enhancements and 
expansion are required to accommodate more users on the platform, improve its resiliency and reliability, and improve 
streaming analytics.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
• 
Status quo: This would impede performance and the use of data and analytics in business decisions. 
• 
Decentralized analytics: Business units could independently address their needs for advanced analytics on a 
project-by-project basis, leading to increase in cost, redundancy and inefficiencies in use of people, process, and 
technology  
Risk of No Action: 
• 
EDAP does not increase capacity and resiliency and it cannot meet enterprise demands. 
• 
Users may conduct analytics in isolation, outside of EDAP, without sharing benefits to other business units 
• 
Increased data duplication, diminished data quality and inconsistent analytical results could lead to a lack of 
trust by users 
• 
Propagation of overlapping platforms and toolsets could lead to increased licensing, maintenance, and support 
costs 
• 
Inconsistent practices could lead to poor solution quality 
• 
Improper utilization of existing Company analytics talent located across the organization 
• 
Lack of centralized prioritization that identifies highest business value projects could lead to diseconomy 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
This program will generate non-financial benefits for the Company, such as: 
• 
Transparency: Enhanced visibility of projects and spending 
• 
Shared knowledge: An archive of analytical models, methods, and data for reuse 
• 
Data science and big data platform skills: Provides the appropriate skills and technologies to solve advanced 
analytics problems 
• 
Consultative services: Determine the applicability of advanced analytics to problems reducing the need for 
external expertise 
• 
Cultural change: Promote a corporate culture where data-driven decision-making is pervasive 
• 
Standardization:  The consistent use of management practices, data sources, tools, platforms, and analytics 
methods 
• 
Efficiency: Proper utilization of resources

Work Description: 
  
Increasingly, companies are implementing technologies such as Robotic Process Automation (RPA), PowerApps, SharePoint, 
Customer and Employee Engagement Channels, and middleware to streamline operations and reduce costs. These technologies 
automate low-value, rules-based business processes, thereby enabling business users to devote more time to more strategic and 
higher-value tasks. These technologies can also enable business users to develop applications quickly and without traditional lead 
times associated with complex-coding. By using these technologies, Con Edison can improve efficiencies and foster better 
communications with customers, suppliers, employees, and other stakeholders.   
As part of Con Edison’s Digital Transformation, IT has established a Process Automation Center of Excellence (PACE) that provides 
the governance, structure, and operating model to enable businesses to use this technology  throughout the company.  PACE governs 
the use, quality, and deployment of RPA, PowerApps, and SharePoint.  A center of excellence (CoE) is a team of business process 
management and subject matter experts that utilize best practices and tools. The CoE promotes and governs the use of a given 
technology, such as RPA.  PACE will expand the team structure, methodology, processes, and governance to support these various 
platforms to effectively and successfully implement throughout the organization.   
Major components include: 
• 
Definition, design, testing, deployment 
• 
Design and implementation 
• 
Governance 
• 
Transition planning and management

• 
Process selection 
• 
Automation tool selection 
• 
Organization capability and capacity assessment 
• 
Team design and training 
• 
Organization communications 
• 
Platform support 
   
Con Edison will also upgrade to Blue Prism Version 6.11 or later version for its Robotic Process Automation platform as part of its 
larger program. Implementation will include provisioning and set up of infrastructure related to new environments (Dev, Test, Prod), 
migration and automation development. 
Benefits Included 
• 
Improved capabilities for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox browser automation 
• 
Improvements to Audit Logs

Process and Object Studio - only the names of all available environment variables are loaded and cached locally.  
•

direct and indirect components.  
• 
Users can now edit an expression directly on the Expression Test Wizard window which displays when clicking 
the Evaluate Expression button in a stage property window.  
• 
Users can now identify which runtime resources are connected to which application server at start up without 
having to log into each of the runtime resources.  
• 
The Create Object/Process Wizard now provides the option to open the newly created item 
 
The Company uses these enabling technologies to automate existing processes in areas such as IT, Customer Service, Finance, Supply 
Chain, Emergency Preparedness, and Law.  Various organizations throughout the Company have implemented some form of 
automation technologies or are considering implementing RPA, PowerApps, and SharePoint. 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
These technologies align with several Company-wide initiatives.  There is a demand for new cutting-edge technology that matches 
technology industry standards. As part of Con Edison’s strategy and the organization’s ability to deliver automated business value 
solutions, there is a need for transforming to Rapid Application Developments (RAD) to deliver products faster according to the 
growing business needs. This effort is underway, and a team is already undertaking business critical processes. It is imperative at 
this stage to formulate a proper team structure with defined methodologies and processes. 
The growth of these platforms (low-code) where business users can build enterprise applications with point-and-click tools without 
direct use of coding languages has resulted in both an increase in productivity and a new set of challenges for IT. These business users, 
termed as ‘citizen developers’, have discovered they are able to use their aptitude and their understanding of business operations to 
create powerful applications. The applications they can be deployed within their organization to teams ranging in size from small to 
large, with development times as short as two weeks. The results have included dramatic advantages in terms of business process 
automation, digitization, and productivity 
PACE will provide best practices, knowledge transfer, expertise, experience, guidance, and re-useable assets to improve the success 
of individual projects and the Company. The benefits of a CoE will continue to grow as the organization becomes more agile and 
improves processes over time.  
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation)

Effectively establishing and running PACE will allow for increased auditability and consistency in performing business transactions, 
with fewer errors or re-work; metrics driven management of projects; improved quality and reliability and increased IT-business 
alignment and partnership to achieve Company goals. From a risk management perspective, governance, promoting one enterprise, 
and cost avoidance will be accomplishied through this project/program. 
Risk 1 Name: Department. Information Technology.

Risk 1 Description:

Risk 2 Name: Department. Information Technology. 
Cost Avoidance  
Risk 2 Description:  
Governance leads to reusability and replication. 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Without a centralized governance and support team, siloed deployment of these technologies leads to inefficiencies, such 
as duplicated efforts, redundant tools, and less controls increasing unnecessary costs and labor-intensive fixes at scale. 
Organizations will go into silos to implement automation processes and onboard various tools, which will result in a 
mixed environment that is hard to support. 
 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Organizations may independently implement Enabling Technologies using disparate approaches and technologies, 
compromising IT support and increasing the potential for cybersecurity vulnerabilities which could ultimately impact 
customers. Processes that span multiple systems could be made more efficient by implementing a bot rather than 
modifying the multiple systems to implement process improvements (capital cost avoidance). 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
• 
Maintaining a CoE with proper tools to route RPA, PowerApps, and SharePoint requests establishes a best-in-
class operation that is scalable and repeatable. Documented processes can be easily rolled out to new business 
units and will reduce the learning curve for future groups implementing technologies. Automating low-value, 
rules-based business processes, will enable business users to devote more time to more strategic and higher-value 
tasks for our customers while also decreasing the need for complex traditional software development. 
• 
An improved relationship between IT and Business Units, including increased collaboration and a jointly 
defined mandate to create impact, which will result in higher work process adherence, easy to use (minimal 
training needed) products and a more unified organization. 
• 
A new collaborative, agile culture can help Con Edison transform its talent base in IT. Con Edison will be able to 
recruit cutting edge talent to modernize IT, which will ultimately lead to more efficient, effective, and safe service 
to our customers. 
• 
Enterprise-wide standard using the new platforms will allow greater transparency into costs, scheduling, work 
status, and productivity metrics through a consistent data platform and advanced analytics engine.

Work Description: 
 
Con Edison owns and operates a private communications network called the Corporate 
Communications Transmission Network (CCTN). This network enables reliable, resilient, diverse, and 
secure communications circuits for SCADANet, voice, video, feeder relay protection, and the complex 
computing and storage environment we maintain. CCTN enables computing resource consolidation, 
disaster recovery infrastructure, as well as cost savings by eliminating the need for public carriers, 
especially for expensive high-speed digital circuits. Control Centers, substations, data centers, and work 
out locations are hosting the fiber optic cables, network equipment, wireless, and ancillary equipment 
used by CCTN.  
 
Here are the components included in the Company CCTN Program: 
 
1. CCTN Fiber Expansion 
2. CCTN Network Modernization 
3. CCTN Facilities Improvement 
4. CCTN Expansion WiMAX “Wireless Mobile Access” 
 
During the coming budget years 2022-2026, the CCTN Fiber Expansion, CCTN Network Modernization, 
CCTN Facilities Improvement, and CCTN Mobile WIMAX Access Network are planned to be 
implemented.  
 
1. CCTN Fiber Expansion 
 
The Company continuously expands, upgrades, and replacies  fiber cables on the CCTN fiber cable 
infrustructure.  The CCTN fiber cable are installed in communications rooms, huts, and environmental 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 20 of 185


--- Page 219 ---
2 
 
controlled cabinets at various Con Edison owned properties, including substations, owned or leased 
utility poles and transmission towers, underground infrastructure, and collocation facilities. The CCTN 
fiber optic cable has been installed to provide communications services that supports SCADA, Feeder 
Relay Protection, RTU, CORP LAN, and telecommunication services between ECC/AECC and 
substations.  The need to expand the CCTN fiber cable infrastructure to substations and data centers that 
do not have CCTN will address mission critical and high bandwidth service demands.  
 
Our CCTN Outside Fiber Plant started to be installed in the 1980’s and with age, these cables are also 
exposed to underground and overhead environmental conditions that has detrimental effect to the cable 
that can cause fiber cable failures. Both the need to expand capacity to address business requirements 
and the replacement of deteriorating fiber optic paths continue to drive expansion projects.   IT has 
developed an approach to maintain fiber optic cable by proactively identifying sections prone to failure 
and replacing them in advance. This eliminates costly projects to replace entire spans wherever possible. 
 
In budget years 2022-2026, the following CCTN Fiber Expansions are planned: 
 
• 
Identify and build new fiber cable routes and enhancements in each borough where there are no 
CCTN presence and communication services are required. 
• 
Identify fiber cable routes that needs to be replaced due to age, condition of the fiber cable, and 
capacity upgrade.  
• 
Requisition of fiber cables and associated materials for projects that includes  new CCTN fiber 
cable routes and upgrade of aging and debilitating fiber cable routes to higher cable counts.  
 
2.  CCTN Network Modernization 
 
The following Nokia /MPLS implementation is planned in budget years 2022-2026: 
 
CCTN Network Modernization is funding the different projects to meet the CCTN growing day to day 
needs.  It also includes the implementation of the Nokia Multi-Protocol Label Switching ‘MPLS’ network 
to replace the End of Life Synchronos Optical Network ‘‘SONet’’  technology. The Nokia MPLS solution 
provides the Company with a high-speed, reliable, and cost-effective alternative to complement public 
carriers. The Nokia MPLS network implementation will include the installation of the MPLS equipment 
at CCTN sites that supports SCADA, voice, video, feeder relay protection, and CORP LAN infrastructure 
that provides network reliability to company locations including Data Centers, Control Centers, 
substations, and workout locations. 
 
The CCTN nodes have the communication equipment that delivers communication circuits that rely on 
Synchronous Optical Networks ‘‘SONet’’network technology to build resilient and secure mission 
critical communication networks. The ‘SONet’ network offers reliable circuit connectivity for Time 
Division Multiplexing (TDM) based end user equipment to operate a variety of mission critical 
applications such as SCADA, voice, substation feeder tele protection, and emergency communications 
such as automatic ring down (ARD) and private mobile radio. The ‘SONet’ network technology is end 
of life due to electronic component obsolescence and decreased demand because of the 
telecommunications industry’s shift to IP over MPLS. This situation is driving CCTN and other service 
providers to retire their ‘SONet’ infrastructure and migrate the TDM services to the Multiprotocol Label 
Switching (MPLS) infrastructure. MPLS can bridge the past to the present and scale for the future needs 
of the communication network that can provide better network performance, quality of service (QoS), 
reliability and security of a ‘SONet’ network and has the capabilities for future network evolution. 
Information Technology has established Nokia as the equipment provider in building CCTN’s MPLS 
infrastructure.  This multi-year project provides a plan to implement the new MPLS infrastructure and 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 21 of 185


--- Page 220 ---
3 
 
perform the network migration of the CCTN circuits, however, we do not expect service interruptions 
as we convert these circuits to MPLS. 
 
In budget years 2022-2026, the following Nokia/MPLS stages are planned: 
 
• 
Purchase equipment and develop the project plan for the Nokia MPLS network deployment. 
• 
Establish the Cisco DWDM and Nokia/MPLS backbone connectivity between Brooklyn, 
Queens, and Bronx. 
• 
Deploy of the Nokia/MPLS network to CCTN locations, and transition services from ’SONet’ to 
MPLS as nodes are inserted 
• 
Remove and retire legacy equipment at transitioned locations  
• 
Deploy Microchip GPS Time Source for frequency timing and NTP services at key CCTN 
locations. 
• 
Hire 2 additional resources will be utilized to assist with the design, planning, implementation, 
and operation of the Nokia MPLS network and OSP Fiber. 
 
3. CCTN Facilities Improvement 
 
Each location that has CCTN equipment located in CCTN network communication room is  equipped 
with AC & DC backup power systems, cabling, heating, ventilation and cooling systems, single point 
grounding systems and security access systems. They also provide for a redundant and diverse design 
for the network. Failures associated with these components will cause failures to critical 
communications circuits needed for energy delivery systems and computer networks. Within the 
course of CCTN fiber expansion, we will build stationary housing facilities rooms for our CCTN 
communications equipment. The new facilities will be in-building rooms, huts, indoor cabinets, or 
outdoor cabinets depending on the available footprint of the installation location. The facility will 
include the structure itself, AC and DC power plant, HVAC, racks, inside plant fiber / copper, 
network, and ancillary equipment to establish the node on the network. 
 
There are several Inside Plant initiatives that ensure the reliability and availability of the CCTN. This 
program performs upgrades on the facilities listed below at 4-10 CCTN locations every year. The work 
includes: 
 
1. Replacement of HVAC systems 
2. Cable segment upgrades  
3. UPS & DC Power system upgrade commensurate with the criticality of the location 
4. Grounding upgrades.  
5. CCTN communication room reconfiguration and expansion. 
 
Work on the Facilities Improvement enhancement programs are typically done concurrently on an 
ongoing basis throughout the year and in no particular order, as conditions and circumstances allow or 
dictate.  
 
Specific locations for similar CCTN facilities improvement work 2023 through 2026 will be determined 
at the end of each rate year.

CCTN also provides the wireless network infrastructure for the radio systems (including dispatch 
applications for man-down radio system) to support voice to field crews and machine to machine smart

Continue to evaluate new technologies. 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
CCTN provides the Company with a high-speed, reliable, and cost-effective communication alternative 
to public carriers as well as provide diversity and redundancy to public carrier circuits for critical 
applications that require it. CCTN provides the network for SCADA, protection and data services to 
critical substations necessitating capital projects to improve reliability, diversity, and capacity to those 
locations. CCTN is expected to serve as the corporate backbone for communication services for the 
foreseeable future.  
 
The projects identified in this white paper addresses departmental and corporate risks associated with: 
 
• 
Failure of critical corporate and operational applications 
• 
Infrastructure constraints 
• 
Network reliability to company locations including Data Centers, Control Centers, substations, 
and workout locations. 
• 
Critical radio system infrastructure in transmission and distribution stations to support 
personnel communication and safety,

Additionally, deployment of a high-speed mobile data network on the proven standard based radio 
frequency (RF) technology platforms like LTE or WiMAX provides the potential to diversify redundant 
local loops to every facility that is currently served by two or more backhaul circuits.  
 
Deployment of the VoIP common dispatch platform will allow the needed interoperability for 
communications during incidents like Superstorm Sandy. 
 
Typically, wired access networks, either fiber or copper, are affected by the same emergencies that cause 
severe damage to the public underground infrastructure such as major operational events or other events 
such as contractor damages, water main breaks, etc.  
 
A high-speed wireless data infrastructure can provide diverse backhaul connections to facilities affected 
by such incidents over the air as opposed to under the ground, where recovery is significantly easier and 
faster. 
 
While unlicensed wireless communications are in service at targeted sites to provide wireless local loop 
access, licensed spectrum is required for an effective wireless broadband system that meets the widest 
communications needs on a single technology. 
 
To this end, several efforts are underway to make broadband spectrum available and to pilot a system 
on equipment that can be initially deployed on unlicensed spectrum and be easily reconfigured to 
operate on licensed spectrum. 
 
Once a high-speed data network is built with mobile capability, it can also be used to provide voice 
services via VoIP technology, eventually replacing the voice radio infrastructure with a single wireless 
access network that can provide voice, video, and data as it is built out in greater density while 
leveraging the CCTN fiber core and the existing IP expertise on staff. 
 
The projects identified in this white paper addresses departmental and corporate risks associated with: 
 
• 
Critical radio system infrastructure 
• 
Safety 
• 
Failure of critical business applications 
• 
Physical damage of corporate server farm 
• 
Critical IT projects  
• 
Failure of the Distribution Automation and Smart Grid applications 
 
The migration of the CCTN OSP fiber cable inventory in the map-based GIS Software enhanced the 
information flow by reporting data in a geographical view. The system is available on the corporate 
network to authorized users and allows staff to quickly determine fiber routes to assist with repairing 
fiber breaks or designing new fiber cable routes. This map-based GIS software will integrate and 
correlate data such as Network Equipment, Network Facilities, and Circuit Layout Records.

Expanding CCTN: 
 
Through experience, CCTN regularly outperforms the carriers on reliability, bandwidth, priority, and 
restoration.  Typically, CCTN is designed to be more disaster resilient, with greater backup power or 
onsite generation. 
 
As such, CCTN provides diversity and redundancy to public carrier circuits for critical applications 
that may require it. The communications diversity provided by CCTN enables the Company to 
maintain operations independent of the public carriers, which is critical for ‘black-sky days’, such as 
major storms or other unforeseen events that substantially impact communications systems including 
public carrier services. Communication requirements for data, voice, feeder protection, SCADA and 
video circuits will result in the installation and deployment of modern communication technologies to 
many Company facilities. CCTN provides the network for SCADA protection and data services to 
critical substations, necessitating capital to expand the presence of the network to meet expanding 
SCADA and automation needs.   It serves as the corporate backbone for communication services for 
the foreseeable future.  
 
The additional communication pathway created through the development of fiber-embedded primary 
cable is an important development in a dense urban environment because wireless communications to 
and from field devices can be challenging.  Field device information will be communicated through the 
fiber to strategically located wireless communication devices for further backhaul.  This may also offer 
cost savings by reducing the number of wireless communication devices necessary to monitor the 
system. 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
Alternative 1 
 
The alternative to CCTN is to procure all communications from carrier services. This approach is not 
recommended due to frequent failure rates associated with carrier circuits, unusually long lead times 
associated with repair and new service delivery, and especially, extensive costs.  
 
Alternative 2  
 
The alternative to Wireless Mobile Access & Interoperability is to continue to operate using expensive 
fiber construction, existing narrowband private frequencies or carrier services wherever required in an 
inefficient mish mash of disparate wireless technologies. 
 
Alternative 3  
 
The alternative to MPLS is to maintain the current environment with its unsupported technology. As a 
precaution, we have acquired spares for our legacy equipment, however this approach is not 
recommended due to failure rates associated with the devices and the inability to scale for new capacity 
requirements. This would also risk sustainability of future platforms. Investments need to be made to 
keep the network sustainable and reliable.

Risk of No Action 
Risk 1 
 
CCTN risks include loss of service resulting from other infrastructure providers disrupting Con Edison 
fiber and affecting service.  Other risks include the inability to fix fiber failures without considering a 
full replacement due to deterioration over time and increased communications failures associated with 
HVAC, cabling, and power loss. The resultant failures would need to be repaired on an emergency 
basis, increasing costs of procuring equipment, OT of employees and the loss of service while the 
repair is completed. 
 
Risk 2 
 
Wireless risks include limited communication to assets not directly on company property, limiting data 
acquisition and control applications. The Company’s 800 MHz iDEN voice radio system will be 
obsolete in 4-5 years. In fact, the largest two iDEN operators have already chosen LTE as their next 
generation wireless broadband services platform. 
 
Risk 3 
 
Additionally, risks include increased communications failures associated with the unsupported and 
aging legacy platforms. The resultant failures would need to be repaired with limited options and 
potential for difficulty in obtaining replacement parts. Fiber optic lasers, used to transmit data via light, 
have limited life expectancies. Their failure rate is expected to increase over time resulting in more 
maintenance that is frequent and eventually the scarcity of replacement parts and unsupported 
platforms introduce cybersecurity risks since the firmware and software is no longer maintained to 
correct flaws in the code.  
 
 
Non-Financial Benefits 
 
Non-financial Benefits: These programs have resulted in an overall decrease in the number of trouble 
tickets over the past few years and corresponding reliability gain. For example, the grounding work 
eliminated further lightning damage to equipment at Buchanan where the radios had been replaced 
twice before remediation in 2011- but never since. The proposed projects and use of CCTN at Con Edison 
offer the following other benefits: 
 
• 
Provides carrier diversity to critical communication circuits 
• 
Offers the highest level of cyber and physical security 
• 
Provides a higher reliability level than carrier circuits 
• 
Scales capacity over time through card replacements 
• 
Delivers faster recovery time from communications failures 
• 
Provides services outside of local Telco carriers 
• 
Avoids construction delays and costs needed for carrier services 
• 
Improves recovery time from communications failures 
• 
Provide reliable and diverse communications for REV, AMI, DSP, and other utility of the future 
applications

4. Basis for estimate 
 
Cost estimates are based on experience with previous fiber jobs; labor estimates from construction 
management and internal forces; current pricing from vendors for fiber, innerduct, and splicing; and 
estimates from Regional Engineering who is responsible for assigning conduit routes. 
 
The estimates are also based on the nominal costs of trenching for new cable (where necessary), 
facilities, equipment (e.g., fiber cable, routers, and optical equipment), labor and overheads, and 
building additional equipment and facilities for the different types of communications infrastructure.  
Nominal cost estimates are based on historical spending for each type of communication. In practice, 
the costs will vary depending on the specific deployment of the expected endpoints (e.g., incremental 
footage, facilities).   
 
5. Conclusion 
This project should continue because of the immediate operational benefits realized so far and for the 
strategic benefits described above. 
 
 
Project Risks and Mitigation Plan 
 
The major risk with any communications migration and upgrade project is the technical risk that the 
current technology standard will supplanted by new technological developments and adoption. This 
risk is mitigated by engaging the various service & equipment providers for continued support 
guaranties, and implementation of backward compatible components. 
 
Another risk is escalation is cost of materials and labor to buildout outside plant physical 
infrastructure. This risk is almost impossible to control but the impact will be mitigated by focusing on 
deployment of the most operationally impactful plant that will maximize utility and benefit if all 
planned infrastructures cannot be built.

Work Description: 
 
As Con Edison deploys Grid Innovation systems, applications, and devices, many will require supporting 
network communications infrastructure to maximize the value of the investment. The Company will develop 
network communications infrastructure to manage the transport of the data generated by these Grid Innovation 
systems. The Company’s network communications strategy must deliver sufficient capacity and diversity of 
network communications channels to accommodate the necessary systems and devices (sensors) with the 
required levels of service.  This network infrastructure generally must be installed or upgraded in advance of 
planned device deployment. Further, this strategy must address cybersecurity and other operational 
requirements.  
 
To accommodate future Grid Innovations systems, applications, and devices (sensors), the Company will expand 
or enhance existing network communications infrastructure to meet the needs of each application. This network 
infrastructure expansion will span a twenty-year horizon in alignment with Con Edison’s Grid Innovation plan. 
Optimal network communications solutions were identified through system, application, and device 
requirements gathering and may include: 
 
• 
Expanding the Corporate Communications Transmission Network (“CCTN”), e.g., new fiber 
• 
Expanding commercial carrier wireless and wireline communications 
• 
Implementing Software Defined Network Technology 
 
Expanding CCTN: 
 
Con Edison owns and operates a private communications network called the CCTN.  This network enables 
secure communications circuits for SCADANet, voice, video, feeder protection, and the computing and storage 
environment.  CCTN enables computing resource consolidation, disaster recovery, as well as the reduction of 
public carrier costs.  There are over 200 Company locations which host the fiber optic and ancillary equipment 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 30 of 185


--- Page 229 ---
2 
 
used by CCTN. The CCTN equipment is installed in communications rooms, communications huts, and 
enclosures at the various facilities.  These facilities are typically at Con Edison owned properties, including 
substations, and owned or leased utility poles and transmission towers.  Since the late 1980s, over 600 miles of 
fiber optic cable has been installed to provide CCTN communications services.  In most cases, these fiber runs 
were combined with electric distribution cable installations. The need to expand capacity to address Grid 
Innovation requirements drives this CCTN expansion project and it included modernizing the CCTN network 
towards modern fiber optics network technologies (for example Multi-Protocol Label Switching ‘MPLS’).  
Enhancement options include adding AMI access points to existing CCTN facilities, extending CCTN reach or 
services over microwave, and building new CCTN facilities, depending on local topography and SCADA or 
capacity needs. 
 
During the years of 2020 through 2022, Con Edison will build fiber routes in each borough, extending the reach 
of the CCTN facilities.  The location of the CCTN facilities build out is dependent on the locations of the planned 
installation of SCADA assets. 
 
Recently, the Company has explored innovation to include fiber optic cable and/or microducts alongside 
primary distribution cable to enhance communications on our distribution network.  Fiber imbedded in the cable 
or blown through the included microducts will provide a communications pathway for data 
gathering.  Available fiber optic cable will enable data transfer from numerous underground cable structures to 
a common communication point.  Use of this technology for Grid Innovation infrastructure will be done on a 
limited basis to selectively extend the reach of communications networks.  As this technology is proven effective 
through field trials, it may be used on a more widespread basis. 
 
Expanding commercial carrier wireless and wireline communications: 
 
Carrier services present another communication channel for Con Edison assets for both wireless and wireline 
uses.  A wireless option that has proven effective in the Company’s dense urban environment, and can be made 
suitably secure and responsive for SCADA control devices, is to use wireless modems and networks through 
carriers like Verizon or AT&T.  Wireline solutions the Company is evaluating include Multiprotocol Label 
Switching (“MPLS”) services over fiber optic cable.  The deployment of high-speed wireline services over fiber 
presents another option for backhauling AMI access points.  This offers more takeout points, a lower hop count, 
and higher performance for SCADA applications. 
 
These options are suitable when performance requirements for certain applications exceed the design capability 
of the AMI network.  Though effective, the downside to this approach is that it is relatively expensive to scale as 
each modem requires a carrier account, and it does not provide the network control or resiliency that is needed 
during extreme events. 
 
During the years of 2023 through 2025, the Company expects it will deploy wireless modems and wireline 
communications where appropriate as needed by the operations Grid Innovations applications (for example new 
sensor implementations). 
 
In practice, the communication path to bring field asset data back to upstream management systems will leverage 
a combination of these options.  For instance, the Company could leverage the AMI network to transmit data 
from field assets and other edge devices to AMI access points. The backhaul network would then transmit the 
data through the established CCTN and/or carrier networks to decision management systems and other 
applications.  
 
 
Implementing SD-WAN (Software-Defined Wide Area Network) technology: 
 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 31 of 185


--- Page 230 ---
3 
 
As the Company looks to enable network communications for DERs, one of the technologies mandated by the 
governing bodies is SD-WAN.  The use of SD-WAN (Software Defined – Wide Area Network) technology will 
be evaluated and if feasible will be implemented to further streamline the communications effectiveness among 
the various carrier-based technologies. The SD-WAN provides a stable and secure way to utilize public networks, 
like the internet for certain SCADA and telemetry applications by providing an independent control plane to 
manage various transmission services. 
 
O&M 
 
Any significant expansion of network communications infrastructure sustained over several successive years as 
is required to support the expected expansion in the number and complexity of applications that define Grid 
Innovation will inevitably result in an increase in O&M activity. The O&M increases will occur in three areas, 
namely, cost for new carrier services, cost for new staff, and cost for more maintenance activity. 
 
O&M related to this project is included in the Telecom O&M budget and White Paper. 
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
Network communications infrastructure is foundational to Grid Innovation. Deploying additional 
communicating devices without the requisite performance, (e.g., bandwidth, latency, etc.) and supporting 
network infrastructure would lead to stranded costs of the assets or even disruption of existing assets that use 
the communication networks.  This infrastructure is a requirement of Grid Innovation and Distributed System 
Platform (“DSP”) projects, including Volt-Var Optimization (“VVO”), Overhead and Underground Resiliency, 
and Distributed Energy Resource Management System (“DERMS”). Each of these investments relies on field 
assets, like smart sensors and controllable network protectors, to inform Company applications and systems for 
planning and/or operational purposes. These Grid Innovation systems, applications, and devices will provide 
real-time visibility and control of grid assets and distributed energy resources (“DER”) on the system.  
The holistic design of the network communications infrastructure for Grid Innovation addresses several 
departmental and corporate risks, including: 
 
• 
Failure of Distribution Automation and Smart Grid applications 
• 
Failure of critical business applications 
• 
Infrastructure constraints 
• 
Safety  
• 
Failure of public carrier wireless services 
Each of the proposed communication solutions has distinct benefits and applications, described below. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk 
Mitigation) 
 
Expanding CCTN: 
 
CCTN continues to provide the Company with a high-speed, reliable, and cost-effective communication 
alternative to public carriers.  Through experience, CCTN regularly outperforms the carriers on reliability, 
bandwidth, priority, and restoration.  Typically, CCTN is designed to be more disaster resilient, with greater 
backup power or onsite generation. 
 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 32 of 185


--- Page 231 ---
4 
 
As such, CCTN provides diversity and redundancy to public carrier circuits for critical applications that may 
require it. The communications diversity provided by CCTN enables the Company to maintain operations 
independent of the public carriers, which is critical for ‘black-sky days’, such as major storms or other unforeseen 
events that substantially impact communications systems including public carrier services. Communication 
requirements for data, voice, feeder protection, SCADA and video circuits will result in the installation and 
deployment of modern communication technologies to many Company facilities. CCTN provides the network 
for SCADA protection and data services to critical substations, necessitating capital to expand the presence of 
the network to meet expanding SCADA and automation needs.   It serves as the corporate backbone for 
communication services for the foreseeable future.  
 
The additional communication pathway created through the development of fiber-embedded primary cable is 
an important development in a dense urban environment because wireless communications to and from field 
devices can be challenging.  Field device information will be communicated through the fiber to strategically 
located wireless communication devices for further backhaul.  This may also offer cost savings by reducing the 
number of wireless communication devices necessary to monitor the system. 
  
Expanding commercial carrier wireless and wireline communications: 
 
The commercial carrier wireless or wireline communications offer SCADA-ready latency and can be designed to 
meet cybersecurity requirements for SCADA applications.  Wireless commercial services are typically more 
scalable for deployment when devices require a short lead time.  Though wireline services require more lead 
time, there are certain locations where extending commercial carrier wireline solutions is a more cost-effective 
solution than extending CCTN.  Where commercial carrier wireline solutions are extended, and ultimately 
connect to CCTN, it extends the CCTN point of presence.  The use of wireline commercial carriers to extend 
CCTN point of presence becomes more important as an AMI mesh network expands the number of sites that are 
viable for commercial carrier extension, greatly expanding the usefulness of network.   
 
Upgrades to commercial carrier wireline services are also critical for area and unit substations without existing 
CCTN facilities to increase the capacity in order to handle the increased demand of SCADA-enabled grid assets.  
Commercial carrier and broadband services provide redundancy and additional diversity among carriers in the 
event of network outages of company-owned networks like CCTN (and vice versa).  Furthermore, these may be 
the only options available where the Company’s networks do not provide coverage or network build out is not 
cost-effective. 
 
Devices that may use commercial wireless or wireline communications include targeted network protector relays 
and smart sensors; distribution automation reclosers and switches on overhead circuits; underground 
interrupters; capacitor bank monitors; and some power quality meters to enable VVO. 
 
O&M 
 
Usage charges will apply for incremental wireless and wireline services needed to backhaul additional access 
points in the private meshed wireless access network that provides last mile connectivity to the various endpoint 
assets described above and for assets that communicate directly over carrier wireless networks. 
 
The expansion of fiber optic outside plan and telecommunications facilities housing multi-point and point to 
point microwave terminal and MPLS and DWDM network gear will require additional technical staff to design, 
deploy, configure, troubleshoot, maintain, and upgrade this plant over the lifecycle of these complex systems. 
There will be increases in common plant like rectifiers, uninterruptible power supply units, and batteries that 
will also need to be maintained. 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 33 of 185


--- Page 232 ---
5 
 
 
Any increase in outside plant incurs exposure to risk to damage from normal field activity and weather events. 
There will also be repairs associated with normal failure for equipment that is in service. Some examples of these 
maintenance activities include replacement and repair of fiber optic cables damaged by construction interference, 
electric system burnouts, rodents and crews working in manholes with fiber cable; storm damage to overhead 
fiber optic cables; ongoing proactive inspections and remediation including tree trimming; replacement of 
electronic components like optical cards, power supply units, transmitters, lightning and grounding protection 
and radio frequency antennas and waveguides. 
 
O&M related to this project is included in the Telecom O&M budget and White Paper. 
 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
For each field device, multiple communication channels were considered. The communication channel was 
ultimately selected based on the following: 
 
o 
Risk of loss of communication – where the redundancy and communication channel 
requirements are more stringent as the risk increases when that communication channel is lost 
o 
Company vs. third party ownership – where company ownership provides greater control, 
particularly during extreme events 
o 
Backup power requirements – where locations with available backup power generation or 
batteries can meet more stringent backup requirements 
o 
Cybersecurity requirements – where cybersecurity requirements vary for monitoring devices 
vs. those that will be controlled by operators 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
Risks of no action include limited communication with field assets and edge devices, limiting data acquisition 
and control of applications, and eroding the value of the investments. Failure to consider holistic solutions to 
communications needs could result in unreliable communications for critical grid control assets or the inefficient 
buildout of network capacity.  Interruptions to control devices reduce an operator’s visibility and control, which 
limits their responsiveness to manage a dynamic grid and presents a risk to maintaining system reliability.  
Inefficient capacity on these networks would result in bespoke communications solutions deployed on a device 
basis, rather than leveraging the scale of the networks to appropriately build capacity. In addition, without a 
comprehensive communication strategy and funding to preserve it, the Company will not be in a position to 
support Reforming the Energy Vision (“REV”), DER integration, and other customer focused initiatives. 
 
Non-Financial Benefits 
 
In addition to enabling many of the Grid Innovation and DSP investments that deploy communicating devices, 
like structure observation systems and controllable network protectors, the proposed communication 
enhancements maintain cybersecurity and provide resiliency through diverse communications. 
 
Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup) 
 
1. Cost-benefit analysis (if required)

While this project does not offer immediate financial benefits, as additional company-owned infrastructure is 
built to support the additional communicating devices, the Company will have a clearer path to retiring some 
legacy communications like leased Distribution Automation System (“DAS”) radio sites. The annual O&M cost 
for DAS sites is about $850,000; i.e., nominally $40K/month for vendor support and $340K/year in site lease 
costs. 
 
2. Major financial benefits 
 
The major financial benefit is capital cost avoidance to build multiple wireless data infrastructures to support 
the various Grid Modernization application with diverse communications requirements. The current DAS 
wireless infrastructure costs about $5,000,000 to build in the 2000-2003 timeframe. 
 
3. Total cost 
 
The total capital cost over the rate years is estimated at $48M. The total O&M cost is estimated at $1.2M over the 
rate years. O&M related to this project is included in the Telecom O&M budget and White Paper. 
 
 
4. Basis for estimate 
 
The estimates are based on the nominal costs of trenching for new cable (where necessary), facilities, equipment 
(e.g., fiber cable, routers, and modems), labor and overheads, and building additional equipment and facilities 
for the different types of communications infrastructure.  Nominal cost estimates are based on historical 
spending for each type of communication. In practice, the costs will vary depending on the specific deployment 
of the expected endpoints (e.g., incremental footage, facilities).   
 
5. Conclusion 
 
This project should continue because of the immediate operational benefits realized so far and for the strategic 
benefits described above. 
 
Project Risks and Mitigation Plan 
 
The major risk with any communications migration and upgrade project is the technical risk that the current 
technology standard will supplanted by new technological developments and adoption. This risk is mitigated 
by engaging the various service & equipment providers for continued support guaranties, and implementation 
of backward compatible components. 
 
Another risk is escalation is cost of materials and labor to buildout outside plant physical infrastructure. This 
risk is almost impossible to control but the impact will be mitigated by focusing on deployment of the most 
operationally impactful plant that will maximize utility and benefit if all planned infrastructures cannot be 
built. 
 
Technical Evaluation / Analysis 
 
Information Technology (“IT”) performs planning and analysis on all technologies introduced. Solutions are 
investigated in conjunction with the IT strategy and vision planning process. Interaction with IT advisors, 
carriers, vendors, and Company employees ensure the selection of the optimal solutions. Traffic model analysis 
measures the current performance of the AMI network and projects performance for areas where deployment is

not yet complete.  This analysis measures both the average utilization of the network and the 95th percentile 
performance to give a measure of both the overall capacity and the peak-traffic performance.   
 
The Company conducted workshops to determine the communication requirements of each field device to be 
deployed through Grid Innovation. Workshop participants included subject matter experts on CCTN, AMI, 
SCADA, and field assets. Requirements such as bandwidth, latency, and control were documented in a 
communications matrix.

excavations are related to the maintenance of Gas, Electric and Steam services through the Con Edison service territory.

Work Description: 
Our data centers are decreasing in size and need as our systems move to the cloud.  Nevertheless, we must 
continue to invest our remaining data centers The Company will need to continue to maintain and upgraded 
them so that they can host certain critical IT assets.  The data centers also provide diversity and redundancy.   
The corporate data centers are strategically located throughout the Consolidated Edison Co. of NY (CECONY) 
and Orange & Rockland (ORU) service territory. Data Centers are operational at 4 Irving Place, Van Nest, Spring 
Valley, 30 Flatbush and Worth Street.   
 
While strategies to consolidate data centers, employ IaaS, SaaS, PaaS and leverage co-locations are underway, 
ongoing capital improvements and operational support are needed for the critical physical infrastructure in the 
Company owned and operated data centers to maintain high availability, reliability and redundancy.  
Components include cooling systems, uninterruptible power systems (UPS), electric distribution, standby 
power, fire detection & suppression, control, environmental monitoring systems, and network cabling 
infrastructure.

Justification Summary: 
 
Data Center Improvements capital projects address solutions for enhancing, upgrading, and new construction 
of: 
• 
IT dedicated back-up power mitigates the loss of computing and communications availability due to 
disruption of utility power sources frequently experienced during weather-related events. 
• 
IT dedicated cooling systems mitigates the risk of failure, premature aging, or damage of IT electronic 
and server/storage equipment due to environmental conditions. 
• 
Racking and cabling systems address the management of physical spaces to accommodate growth, 
moves, or changes in data center equipment. 
• 
Infrastructure and environmental monitoring tools enable quick assessment and resolution of 
unplanned events that can adversely affect IT system availability and help to automate complex decision 
making for power and cooling capacity planning and outage mitigation. 
 
The capital programs and projects funded under the Data Center Improvements budget permit Con Edison to 
maintain the high availability of its computer systems, reducing costs associated with downtime and avoids 
situations that may cause environmental and safety concerns due to system failures (e.g., fires, coolant fluid 
spills, refrigerant releases, etc.).

Work Description: 
 
The Data Governance Program is a strategic initiative intended to improve the governance of data 
cataloging, mapping, integrity, quality, appropriate use, and protections of data within Con Edison. 
This program looks to develop a framework that will promote Con Edison’s data classification policy, 
support privacy legislation, data sharing for programs like IEDR and ensure security of data in line 
with industry data management standards.  The goal  is to build trust amongst customers and others 
with whom we share and process data.   
  
Data governance is a collaborative exercise that spans across all Company functions and lines of 
business. The enhanced program – to include staffing, processes, and tooling – is a collaboration 
between IT, business organizations, and compliance to (i) improve trust in data used to transact 
business activities through accurate and thorough cataloging, (ii) meet regulatory and compliance 
requirements through quality assurance rules and monitoring, and (iii) ensure data protection policies 
and controls are employed effectively through data classification. 
 
The Data Governance Program will develop and deploy a framework focused on the following needs: 
• 
Operating model where roles and responsibilities are clearly defined and understood, 
specifically accountability and appropriate delegation of authority. 
• 
A cross-functional program that takes an enterprise (rather than siloed) view of data issues. 
• 
A centralized knowledge sharing platform, or data catalog, allowing a collaborative approach 
between the business and IT to identify sensitive data and share information about key data 
assets in the enterprise. 
• 
A process and tool to measure and monitor the accuracy of data with appropriate escalation 
channels requirements for action plans to rectify poor data quality.  
 
This project will support the: 
• 
Implementation of data governance tools to validate proofs of concept, pilots, cloud costs, etc.)   
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 61 of 185


--- Page 260 ---
2 
 
• 
Data Stewards staffing by business organization to facilitate data catalog content creation, data 
quality measurement and resolution, and compliance with data protection policies and 
controls.   
• 
IT Operations staffing to develop and maintain a data governance tool that enables data 
cataloging, data quality, master data management, and data issue management workflow 
capabilities (e.g., design, development, deployment, services, licensing, etc.) 
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
A strong data governance program ensures defined ownership and accountability by source system, as 
well as quality assurance and control for data moving downstream with the use of rules and 
monitoring.  Additionally, defining consistent data classifications and cataloging data lineage as part of 
the program ensures appropriate protections are in place for data classified as sensitive, both at rest 
and in motion.  Data of poor quality, incorrect classification, or processed/shared in an uncontrolled 
manner can compromise the Company's ability to build user-friendly and functioning digital customer 
tools, adhere to regulatory requirements, and secure data against cyber-attacks or other forms of data 
loss.  Coordinated data governance also provides the opportunity to decrease data collection 
redundancies, standardize data-related processes and systems, and increase data system and resource 
efficiencies within and across departments. 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
Enhancements to the Data Governance Program are necessary to promote and enforce data 
management and protection controls relevant to the mitigation of operational and compliance risks 
involving information security, cyber security, privacy, and internal/external fraud.  Failure to 
mitigate these risks could result in significant harm to customers, as well as financial and reputational 
risk to the Company.  Con Edison must be innovative and strategic with respect to data management 
and governance, as well as other company goals such as clean energy, to maintain compliance with a 
quickly evolving regulatory landscape (i.e., data subject access rights) and ensure an effective control 
environment to combat internal and external threats of data loss.  Meeting the objectives of a strong 
data governance program promotes trust in internal data used to meet regulatory and compliance 
requirements in the Company, as well as protects customer data for which the Company has been 
trusted by consumers as the data controller.  
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
Alternative 1 description and reason for rejection 
Failure to mature current data management processes and tooling produces an inconsistent, non-
standardized, fragmented approach to managing data assets across the enterprise. As new core 
enterprise systems are implemented or existing ones upgraded - for example, applications in the 
customer, HR, GIS, and outage domains - it is critical to mature the data governance practices in the 
enterprise to ensure that data of high quality is produced and maintained and is consistently available 
to support critical business processes . Data stewardship, data issue management, data cataloging, and 
data protection controls and tooling are foundational capabilities needed to ensure that data is trusted, 
protected, and knowledge about it is collaboratively created, stored, and shared.  
  
In addition, as more analytics projects are launched, more mature and robust data governance 
processes and tooling are imperative for data discovery activities for sourcing data into the analytics 
platforms, as well as, for cataloging the types of data and its meaning in the platforms.

Risks 
Following are the enterprise risks if the Program is not implemented: 
  
• 
Poor data quality undermines trust in data, potentially impacts operational decisions and 
regulatory and compliance reporting. 
• 
According to Gartner, organizations that offer users access to a curated catalog of internal and 
external data will realize twice the business value from analytics investments than those that 
do not. 
• 
Lack of ownership for and ability to track data issues fails to address data issues as they arise.   
• 
Siloed knowledge about the contents of data stores increases the probability of creating 
duplicative data stores or reports to meet business needs, thus, resulting in increased costs. 
• 
Not having an inventory of sensitive data assets and applicable data protection controls will 
likely increase the cyber and privacy risks of data exposure and could make the data assets the 
subject of a cyber-attack. 
• 
Failing to define the systems of record for key data elements in the enterprise negatively 
impacts the customer experience - for example, not having a master source of customer contact 
information may result in customer interactions that do not respect customer preferences.  
 
Non-Financial Benefits 
 
• 
A centralized data issue management platform to record, track, and assign responsibility to 
data issues will improve workflows and communication among departments. 
• 
Automated classification of sensitive data is a foundational capability necessary to ensure 
compliance with customer privacy laws. 
• 
A centralized, enterprise data catalog process and tooling provides the following benefits: 
o 
Increases data understandability, acceptance, and trust 
o 
Decreases time spent searching for data and more on delivering value 
o 
Supports data lineage analysis - that is, increases the ability to trace data from source 
(operational databases) to target (reports)  
o 
Supports impact analysis by increasing the ability to measure the impact of change  
o 
Provides a standard, centralized platform where subject matter experts can share their 
knowledgeable about data sources 
o 
Supports business intelligence and analytics projects  
• 
Development and measurement of data quality metrics enhances the quality of data in 
reporting and analytics platforms and data in transactional systems. 
• 
Enhanced data quality increases trust in data reported to regulatory agencies. 
• 
Data issues are identified earlier in business processes and handled before adversely affecting 
operations and business decisions.  
 
 
Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup) 
1. Cost-benefit analysis (if required) 
 
Costs that can be avoided with a comprehensive Data Governance Program include the following: 
  
• 
Data breach fines. Identification of where sensitive data is located and implementation of data 
protection controls (for example, data access controls, data masking, data encryption) mitigates 
the risk and attendant fines of data being viewed, accessed and stolen by unauthorized 
individuals.  
• 
PSC fines. Identification of walled data that should be separated by business functions (for 
example, marketing vs. transmission data) can be more easily identified and tagged 
accordingly.  
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 63 of 185


--- Page 262 ---
4 
 
• 
Data discovery time. When key data sources are well cataloged, analytics teams spend less 
time during the discovery phase to find the data that they need and more time actually 
building and testing analytics models.   
• 
Longer data issue resolution times. Formalizing data issue management processes to identify, 
assign, and track progress shortens resolution time and produces higher quality data.     
• 
Duplicative data. Cataloging reporting systems reduces redundancy and helps identify 
existing reports that can meet needs. 
 
The data governance program costs will include the following: 
  
• 
Contractor staffing to implement the data governance tools including technology subject 
matter experts and a project management resource 
• 
Business unit data stewards staffing with the following responsibilities: data catalog and 
business glossary content creation, data issue management, master data management design, 
data quality metrics design, and quality oversight 
• 
IT Data Governance Office staffing: responsibilities include, but not limited to data governance 
framework design and socialization; data catalog design and content creation; job aids 
creation; business unit support for data issue resolution; data protection best practices design; 
and collaboration with Law and Information Security      
• 
IT operations teams to support data governance technology maintenance and upgrades  
• 
Software licensing costs for technology solutions  
 
2. Major financial benefits 
 
The major financial benefits of the Data Governance Program include efficiency and cost avoidance in 
a number of areas and business units.  Some examples include the following: 
  
• 
By identifying the location of sensitive data and the necessary data protection controls to 
apply, the Company  ensures that, for example, customer data is safe from cyber-security 
attacks, thus, avoiding the costs associated with the defense from illegal activities.  
• 
Having a platform where knowledge about the key data assets in the enterprise is shared and 
policies are understood and applied reduces costs to store duplicate or low value data.     
• 
The Data Governance framework includes data quality processes, metrics, and data stewards 
responsible to address data issues, thereby reducing the time needed to collect and cleanse 
data to support both transactional processes and analytics modeling.  
• 
Call center response times are reduced when CSRs have access to timely, trusted customer and 
product information. 
  
There will be savings/cost avoidance over a five-year period after implementation of the key 
components of the Program (sensitive data inventory, data catalog, data stewardship operating model, 
etc.). The remaining savings will come from productivity improvements in data issues resolution and 
cost avoidance.

In summary, the Data Governance Program will enhance the processes and tooling across departments 
necessary to ensure valid, reliable and high-quality data is available to meet the needs of numerous

• 
A common understanding of data.  
• 
Improved data quality.

technology areas — including areas such as legal, security, and compliance — are addressed 
consistently.

Increased trust and protection. Data governance enables data that is well-documented, and 
easier to find, and supports the need to keep data secure, compliant, and confidential.

Technical Evaluation / Analysis 
 
Data management industry groups have conducted studies on the impact of immature data 
governance to organizations.  One 2017 study by the US Data Management Association reports that 
“92% of businesses feel their data is inaccurate in some way.  In addition, unreliable, incomplete, or  
poor-quality data cost organizations between 15% and 20% of their operating budgets.” 
 
Project Relationships (if applicable) 
 
The framework, technologies, and operating model to be delivered with the Data Governance Program 
will enable collaboration between IT and business organizations to increase trust in and protection of 
data assets. The Program's framework and technologies will improve the management of data across 
all data projects in the Company. The Program fosters a collaboration between the IT and the business 
orgs. It can be used for new projects, and for systems that want to improve the means they use to 
manage data. The Program advances the concept of data stewardship or ownership by delivering a 
framework whereby IT and the business units work closely to address data issues.

Data integration is a critical IT function and enables business transaction processing, process functions, data 
sharing and exchanging data within the Coned network and external partners in a safe and secure way.  The 
current tools and technologies supporting these functions must be modernized to meet the strategic 
initiatives like DERMS, Privacy, IEDR and the fast-growing demands for the integration across the company. 
 
The project will implement new integration technology, tools and infrastructure and help scale to meet the 
high volumes of data, meet performance and timeliness requirements.  The platform will come with out of 
the box tools that will allow transformation, improve data quality and apply governance controls. Business 
use cases such as asset maintenance, electric/gas system monitoring, smart sensor programs, EDAP and 
privacy will rely on integration capabilities delivered by the integration modernization project.  The project 
deliverables are:  
 
• 
 Design, develop and implement the integration platforms and operationalize for production.  The 
project will process high volumes of AMI data and improve the timeliness and consistency in meeting 
business expectations.  This will lay the foundation for future projects to use the platform.  The 
platform will instrument processes that will enable a centralized access to data eliminating 
duplication and replication that happens today.  
• 
Implement standards: A service-oriented design will be implemented using a modern method (API) 
to reduce development time and efforts, automate security and support multi-cloud configurations.  
This will directly enable and support requirements around Distributed Energy resource Management 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 68 of 185


--- Page 267 ---
(DERMS), sensor deployments, customer analytics, outage, and restoration.  
• 
The integration modernization project will fund the selection and implementation of technology, 
using consulting services and vendor support. A dedicated integration team will be built to help 
grow talent and acquire skills and experience.   In addition, the project is responsible for developing 
processes to operationalize the technology and help business project implementations.  
• Develop best practices:  The team will develop standard architectures, playbooks and blueprints that 
will help projects use the technology and implement business requirements.   
 
Justification Summary: 
 
 Some of the benefits are:  
• 
Improve resilience and reliability in providing data assets in a secure, zero trust fashion. Reduces 
duplication of data across consumer applications. Eliminate point-to-point integrations and increase 
operational flexibility.  
• Enhanced speed to value as projects takes advantage of out of the box capabilities like data streaming 
and build programs and processes once that can be re-used and enhanced without re-inventing the 
wheel. 
• Standardize on a modern integration platform and support mission critical projects and high value 
business operations like AMI, CORE, EDAP, DERMS, IEDR like projects. The platform will support 
on-prem and cloud solutions and handle large workloads and scale quickly to meet high volumes like 
we see during a storm. 
• Enforce governance (security, data, process), instrument common data definitions and provide 
visibility and transparency as data moved across systems.  This is especially relevant for Privacy, AMI 
and outage and restoration processes.  For example, situational data from field (sensors, meters, 
Scada and GIS) must be processed and made readily made available to systems in a unified, timely 
fashion. This results in all systems having access to latest information in a consistent, accurate and 
timely fashion and aids better decision making.

Work Description: 
  
The purpose of this project is to holistically address end user computing technologies.  End user computing 
encompasses a variety of user facing technologies including desktops and laptops, desktop operating systems and 
applications, smartphones, mobile and web applications, and virtual desktops.  These solutions look to deliver 
technology that will meet productivity, efficiency, cost savings, performance, and security goals.  In the past we had 
separate projects to address different components and with evolving technology we have decided to create a single 
program. This project will include multiple areas of technology namely:  
 
• 
Evaluating end user technologies for Coned adoption (device capabilities, software, and mobile features etc.) 
• 
Software to support end user computing capability and experience (collaboration, device provisioning, patching 
etc.)  
• 
Expanding and investing in enterprise end user technologies that are essential to performance, security, and 
scale  
 
Evaluating end user technologies for Coned adoption:   Each year new products and solutions are researched with 
industry experts and vendors before being evaluated, piloted, and implemented in the Con Edison environment. The 
project will fund selection of new technologies aligned to the IT strategy, drivers and business goals and plan for their 
adoption and implementation.  This positions IT to think and plan for technologies that will enable these capabilities to 
meet business needs, such as the evaluation of the latest biometric authentication technology to improve our end user 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 74 of 185


--- Page 273 ---
security posture. 
 
Software to support end user computing capability and experience:  The goal of this software is to provide a standard 
and up to date, set of desktop tools that incorporate the latest technology to improve accessibility, support the remote 
work environment, and collaboration. This work stream will involve: 
• 
Upgrade from Windows 10 to Windows 11 platform version  
• 
Implement new Virtual Private Network infrastructure to better support remote mobile clients by providing a 
scalable secure (multifactor) authentication and access for 15000+ users  
• 
Evaluate the latest biometric authentication technology and plan for future deployment 
• 
Refresh Remote Access technology and get ahead of obsolescence in a timely fashion 
• 
Evaluate multi-cloud management, monitoring, and automation tools  
 
Expanding current enterprise technologies: The project will fund the software, hardware, and a team of resources to 
implement support and manage the expanding Microsoft Office 365 tools, secure printing, and faxing.  This project area 
will continuously improve and enhance the software and hardware, and scale in a structured systematic way. 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
Technology is changing at a rapid pace and cyber risk has been increasing at much higher speeds.   To stay competitive 
and operate in a secure and efficient manner, End User Computing capabilities must evolve with nimbleness and meet 
changing user and business expectations. 
Many technologies, foundational and emerging are implemented and converge to deliver a seamless user experience.  
For example, end user computing devices must maintain latest software and be secured and scanned; they must take 
advantage of cloud capabilities to scale on demand and perform; be fitted with new emerging capabilities like 
augmented and virtual reality on end- user devices with agility to name a few which have become a norm in the current 
environment to improve safety for all.   To achieve these the following broad technology areas are addressed in this 
project.   
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
All current and future business applications require desktop software to be up to date and supportable. Company 
policies require the computing environment to adhere to cybersecurity policy and software compliance policies.
