Work Description 
 
Enterprise architecture (EA) strives to simplify the application and infrastructure portfolio across the organization while 
taking a proactive role in bringing new, innovative technology.  It is essential to meeting the IT vision, strategy, and 
business goals.  Enterprise Architecture is a standard IT methodology for analyzing, planning, designing, and 
implementing IT solutions. It is the equivalent of Distribution Engineering or Central Engineering for IT.  Key 
deliverables are the architecture and design standard documents across various IT domains including security, 
networks, applications, and infrastructure.   These architecture and design standards provide the path forward on how the 
organization should and can adopt newer technologies.  It also assists in optimizing investments and reducing risk.  
This furthers the Company goal of using technology to enable business capabilities and improve safety, operational 
excellence, and customer experience.   
Over the past year, user demand for EA services and tools has increased exponentially.  As we increase our cloud 
deployments, adopt platform solutions (platforms like WMS or CRM), and mature in self-service analytics to meet 
business and technology innovation, EA plays a critical role to properly design these solutions. These services help 
future proof technology in areas such as edge computing, sensors, security (zero trust architecture), WMS 
standardization, CRM and more.  With an evolving utility landscape, enterprise architecture is playing a critical role for 
new initiatives like DERMS, IEDR and privacy.  
The project will meet the following implementation objectives:  
• 
Define and design architecture processes and implement architecture applications needed to operationalize 
EA.  
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 80 of 185


--- Page 279 ---
• 
Onboard EA resources to support application implementation. 
• 
Develop and upskill the talent pool within the EA org, through training. 
• 
Define EA governance processes.  
Justification Summary: 
 
 
Enterprise Architecture is required to: 
• 
Improve Application Portfolio Management to reduce the number of applications, costs, and risks. 
• 
Improve Technology & Risk Management to reduce complexity and resolve security vulnerabilities, 
compliance issues, and the inability to support the business, in a timely fashion. 
• 
Documented architectures and standards to meet the business goals of a future state. 
• 
Reduce delivery times to keep up with a fast-changing utility business environment.   
 
The project will fund expert services, a core team, and the tools to design and implement processes and deploy across 
the enterprise and support steady state operations.  This will result in adoption of standards, improved technology and 
application portfolio management and systematic introduction of new technologies. The enterprise architecture specific 
tools will accelerate and ease implementation using industry best practice and methodologies.   
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
This project will support all company IT projects and initiatives involving technology investments.

Work Description: 
  
The project will continuously improve the Company’s project management capabilities for capital construction projects 
by expanding and implementing our project management software platform, Primavera.  This platform supports 
improved schedule management, cost management, contract management, project lifecycle governance, and document 
management.  
The major elements of work for this project include: -  
Expand the Primavera Unifier on the Oracle Cloud, to support:  
o Leveraging the system implemented and sustain standard project management capabilities within the Company 
 o Better transparency and reporting for project attributes  
 This includes project/program/portfolio reports for better transparency  
o Increased functionality for project lifecycle governance system  
 Establishing a document management repository for key project management documents  
o Increased functionality for construction collaboration - Software integrations - Organizational change management 
and training –  
O&M costs associated with the addition of two FTEs to the group to provide ongoing support and administration of the 
software product.

• 
  
FIG will maintain the existing fraud data analytics platform at the enterprise level. The platform performs automated 
fraud monitoring and alerting. The following was completed in 2021; • Refined and stabilized the system to improve 
the alerts • Implemented proactive monitoring and workflow process to respond to alerts • Developed long term 
strategy and met with partners to begin developing future use cases • Developed in-house fraud data analytics 
capability and expertise by working with various business groups and understanding the business processes and begin 
a governance process

interfaces to accommodate data from systems that migrate to Oracle cloud • Labor to support the above initiatives The

Justification Summary: 
 
Auditing Financial Integrity Group (FIG) partnered with IT to build and implement a fraud data analytics platform to 
enable ongoing automated fraud monitoring and alerting. The platform is a commercially available solution from SAS, a 
market leader in fraud data analytics.   
The implementation of platform was completed in 2020, which involved creation of secure data storage, secure client-
server database environment, interfaces for data sources, strong analytics software for large volume data cleansing, 
multi-dimensional data mining, advance statistical modeling, data visualization and distribution, and repetitive test 
scheduling. A phased approach was used for implementation and for initial phase Oracle EBS (Financial and Supply 
Chain), and Oracle HR (HR, Time & Labor, Payroll) were selected as source. The initial implementation covered 
procurement and vendor activity. Additional data requirements will be identified through FIG’s fraud risk assessment 
planning and prioritization processes and will be addressed in subsequent phases.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Do nothing 
 
 
FIG has made significant investment in SaS Data Analytics platform. If we don’t expand the use of the tool, then we will 
not be able to better detect fraud.  This approach will hinder us from proactive fraud risk management and monitoring. 
This option is not recommended as it opens Con Edison to limited fraud visibility. 
 
 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Fraudulent behavior may cause financial and reputational loss, regulatory exposure, and public embarrassment that 
could result in reputational damage to the Company.  There could also be criminal prosecution and/or significant 
penalties imposed on employees and the Company. In addition, this could lead to low employee morale.  
 
 
Regulatory Risk (Financial Misstatements): Fraud risks not caught/prevented in a timely manner can lead to financial 
misstatements and associated issues.   
 
 
Corporate Risk (Fraud): The Corporate Risk of a Rogue Employee - Rogue employee(s) and/or vendor(s) violate 
laws/regulations for personal gain. Variances in account balances, as an example, can be an indicator that there is a 
discrepancy that required research.  By having the analytics platform, where forensic analytics can be performed to 
detect patterns and anomalies to determine whether any unusual activity is going on, tests can be scheduled, and risk 
alarms can be automatically generated timely.   
 
 
Reputational Risk: Fraudulent activities not identified in a timely manner will have an adverse impact on the company’s 
reputation.   
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
A proactive fraud risk management program will increase overall employees' fraud awareness and consciousness, 
which will help the company to detect and prevent fraud from happening.  
 
Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup) 
1. Cost-benefit analysis (if required) 
 
Association of Certified Fraud Examiners (ACFE) is the world's largest anti-fraud organization. According to the ACFE's 
2018 Report to the Nations, proactive data monitoring and analysis is among the most effective anti-fraud controls. 
Organizations that undertake proactive data analysis techniques experience frauds that are 52% less costly and 58% 
shorter than organizations that do not monitor and analyze data for signs of fraud. 
 
2. Major financial benefits 
 
ACFE estimates organizations worldwide lose 5% of revenues to fraud and 53% of victim organizations have not 
recovered any of their losses due to fraud. The company is proactively managing fraud risks and implementing a 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 94 of 185


--- Page 293 ---
forensic analytics enterprise-wide. Without a robust data analytics platform solution, FIG will not be able to churn in-
depth forensic analytics and build an automated ongoing monitoring process to prevent and detect fraud risks 
enterprise-wide

Work Description: 
 
The Hitachi Password Manager application provides self-service and help desk assisted password 
reset and account unlock capabilities for Active Directory and mainframe user accounts (IMS, CIS, 
TSO and CICS) for  employees and contractors.  The Hitachi application was fully implemented in 
April 2020 and replaced an end of life, home grown application. 
 
In accordance with the vendor’s application roadmap and support cycle, it is expected that an 
application upgrade would be required in 2023 and every 2 years thereafter. In addition, the 
Windows server operating system and SQL database will need to be upgraded to the latest version 
to maintain Microsoft support for patching, bug fixes, etc. 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
An upgrade will be required in year 2023 due to obsolescence of application technology 
components.  The Windows Server 2012 operating system will reach end of life in October 2023. The 
application version will also need to be upgraded in accordance with the vendor’s application 
roadmap.  In addition, the Microsoft SQL version 2014 will be end of life in July 2024. 
 
Ongoing operational and application maintenance support is required to ensure application 
stability and availability.  Maintenance incudes IT labor resources, license compliance, and  
hardware and software upgrades and patching in accordance with vendor roadmaps and support 
cycles.    
 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation)

capabilities.  Self-service password management capabilities reduce the need for Help Desk 
analysts to manually handle such requests and assists the Service Desk with managing the call

operation and availability of the application.

Work Description: 
 
The Company makes many technology investments each year for the continued operation of the 
computing and network infrastructure used to support data centers, applications, and networks.  In 
addition, over the past few years, the Company is increasingly relying on cloud services to play a large 
part in our IT strategy.  Whether for cost savings, process efficiencies, speed to market, redundancy, or 
resiliency, the cloud provides expanding capabilities that the Companies would like to leverage more.  
In either case, the Company protects the investments through maintenance and support contracts, 
managed services or subscription contracts for the hardware, software or cloud services.  
 
Maintenance and Support Contracts 
Maintenance and support contracts allow the Company to keep the hardware and software up to date, 
patch cybersecurity vulnerabilities, replace hardware failures, and take advantage of new release 
features within the products.    This allows sustainability and supportability of the environment over 
time and increases reliability and availability of the network, business applications and infrastructure.  
Technology solutions can be purchased through capital investments which include a negotiated 
maintenance period.  Once that period has expired, the contract becomes an expense to the Company, 
in addition newer solutions may only offer a cloud model.  During the following five years, 
maintenance on the following products will expire and new expenses for maintenance will begin: 
 
• 
Increases in PC hardware maintenance due to growth of inventory; 
• 
Cisco network equipment and servers due to network growth; 
• 
Microsoft Enterprise Agreement to maintain server, operating system, integration, and 
database software versions as well as support; 
• 
Server backup solution;  
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 102 of 185


--- Page 301 ---
2 
 
• 
Data center colocation; 
• 
Virtual Private Network technology upgrade and device mobility growth;  
• 
Server and storage infrastructure growth. 
 
Managed Services 
In order for the Company to maintain reliable on-premise corporate data centers, the Company is 
partnering with a Managed Service Provider ‘MSP’ to maintain the data centers and provide 
emergency coverage across all data centers.  The MSP is responsible to perform all inspections, 
preventative maintenance, work with vendors to perform repairs to any data center equipment 
(power, HVAC, batteries, cabling, etc.) and provide onsite coverage for data center emergencies.  The 
corporate data centers host critical IT systems and expanding the MSP support across all of the data 
centers will ensure reliable data center operations. 
 
Subscription Contracts 
For cloud services these subscriptions fund various foundational tools and innovative projects.  
Microsoft Azure is our primary cloud for various services including our data and analytics platform, 
private cloud (Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)) to extend our data center footprint, and Microsoft 365.  
These services provide scalable solutions which are designed to be provisioned quickly.  The Microsoft 
services were a major investment and have provided improved security, collaboration experience, the 
ability to deploy applications in days and provides improved productivity and disaster recovery since 
the applications are accessible from anywhere.  In addition, Microsoft Office 365 is the current 
corporate standard for desktop productivity and security tools software.  Key benefits and 
functionality of the platform include: 
• 
Seamless integration with the programs we already know and use, including Outlook, Word, 
Excel, OneNote, and PowerPoint; 
• 
Web-enabled access to email, important documents, contacts, and calendar on any device—
including PCs, iPhones, Android phones; 
• 
Collaboration and online meeting solutions by using Teams and SharePoint online which 
have been essential for remote work and external communications; 
• 
Improved security tools to help protect email, documents, and networks; 
• 
Reliability, availability, and performance, with a 99.9% financially backed uptime guarantee 
 
Justification Summary: 
The value of the Company’s technology investments is maintained through support and subscription 
contracts for its various hardware and software platforms and cloud services. The agreements are used 
to provide access to platforms, assist during issues, keep the software up to date, patch cybersecurity 
vulnerabilities, replace hardware failures, and take advantage of new release features within the 
products.  IT provides critical services, and these contracts reduce risk and allow for the sustainability 
and supportability of the environment and increases reliability and availability of the network, business 
applications, infrastructure, and PCs.  Without having these contracts in place, the Company will incur 
a significant risk. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation)  
 
This program supports future growth, allows for security and support for all applications, networks 
and major IT initiatives.

Work Description: 
  
The Testing Center Of Excellence (hereafter referred to as “Testing COE”) is a consolidated and centralized governance 
model for application testing practices, intended to be implemented across an organization. Upcoming or in-flight major 
enterprise application initiatives require a centralized governance model for a common sustained/repeatable process to 
testing, requirement, defect management, and knowledge management.  In addition, to expedite testing and improve 
processes the Testing COE can assist with the regulatory requirements geared to improve system readiness and storm 
restoration capabilities leading to better customer experience. These regulations were a direct result of Winter Storms 
Riley/Quinn in 2018 and subsequently, Tropical Storm Isaias in 2020.  
 
Based on current OMS testing requirements the Company has engaged a 3rd party (Cognizant) to perform an 
assessment of the end-to-end testing process for OMS. The assessment has so far revealed opportunities to streamline 
the processes. For example, it takes 4-6 weeks of preparation time and engagement from 30+ subject matter experts 
across multiple IT disciplines to design and execute the test. In addition, recommendations are forthcoming to 
modernize the OMS testing tool set, introduce additional automation, and create dedicated performance testing 
environments for critical systems.  The goal of the CoE will be improve in these areas and automate testing process 
across all applications. 
 
To meet customer expectations and regulatory requirements, a robust, mature and well-designed testing process, 
function, and service is needed to thoroughly test the readiness of systems.  
Below are several key areas of focus:  
• 
Assessment of current state and tools used across IT portfolio to identify best practices and  where to modernize 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 108 of 185


--- Page 307 ---
or improve  
• 
Standardize on testing tools and processes across the IT organization  
• 
Develop best practices for types of testing and best approach for a given project (i.e. waterfall, agile, etc.)  
• 
Staffing a full-time organization  
• 
Develop training material and templates for knowledge transfer  
• 
Develop artifacts such as reports, dashboards, and score cards to enable transparency and visibility  
• 
Ensure system integrators that perform testing align with this process 
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
Below are additional benefits of a Testing Center of Excellence: 
• 
Impartial quality assessment   
• 
Unbiased & fresh view of code quality through thorough testing.  
• 
Sizable decrease of risks in centralizing software testing for development projects and business as usual 
requests.  
• 
Audits & checklist driven framework to drive high-quality product delivery. 
 
Cost and Organizational benefits:  
• 
Demand consolidation and optimization 
• 
One-time setup expenses, associated with building & managing testing processes, O&M Cost savings in 
consolidating testing tools purchases, maintenance and test environment consolidation.   
• 
Access to best practices. 
• 
Access to specialized skills like performance & automation on demand.  
•

using common, consistent and standardized processes.   
• 
Faster cycle time and repeatable testing processes; Overall efficiencies gain with all 3 levers - People, Process & 
Technology 
 
Further to the above, end-to-end testing is a Key Risk Indicator (KRI) for the Company and is tracked as a part of the 
Corporate ERM matrix. 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
Risk 1 Name: 
Corporate 
ConEd.Strategic.NY 
Regulation 
Risk 1 Description:  
Following the Riley/Quinn Winter Storms in March 2018, the NYPSC directed all NYS utilities to 
conduct semi-annual end-to-end testing of their OMS suite of applications. This requirement was 
added as a Key Risk Indicator (KRI) for the Company and included in the Corporate ERM matrix. 
It has also been incorporated into the Company’s Emergency Response Plan (ERP). Following 
Tropical Storm Isaias, the NYPSC took this requirement a step further and directed all NYS 
Utilities to conduct end-to-end testing of their OMS systems simulating an outage impacting 90% 
of their customers. To meet this new requirement now and into the future, the Company must 
continue to invest in a robust testing environment and processes. To that end, an investment in a 
dedicated organization to plan, perform, manage and own testing practices, ensure alignment 
across the broader IT organization, and modernize testing tools is paramount to achieving this 
objective.

Alternatives 
 
Alternative 1 description and reason for rejection

An alternative to not standing up a Testing COE is to continue to maintain a siloed approach to testing 
similar to the current state process where individual teams across IT BSD maintain their own testing process, 
schedule, and tools without the benefit of a holistic wide area end to end view of the application ecosystem. 
This will continue to contribute to inefficiencies in people and process and will likely contribute to project 
delays as there is no dedicated centralized team managing testing as it stands today. This approach should 
be rejected as the inefficiencies of the current process have led to the exploration of a Testing COE to allow 
the Company to evolve its testing practices. 
 
There is risk in the current process in that it is disjointed in nature leading to the possibility of inadequate 
test coverage and inefficiency in execution. This will lead to undiscovered defects contributing to poor 
customer experience (both internal and external) and potentially impacts to the Company brand/reputation. 
It could also lead to regulatory fines and/or additional regulatory scrutiny for lack of compliance with end-
to-end testing requirements

costs, as well as incurring fines from regulators. 
• 
Exposes critical systems to failure during emergency events affecting customer experience.

Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup) 
1. Cost-benefit analysis (if required) 
Organizations that have adopted a Testing COE have reported an average cost reduction of 35% over 3 years 
(source: https://www.cigniti.com/blog/testing-center-of-excellence-does-your-business-have-one-and-
seven-reasons-why-you-need-it/) 
 
 
2. Major financial benefits 
A Testing COE will lead to more transparency around defects and associated impacts. This will allow for 
more accurate assessment of total cost of ownership for a given system/interface/tool. Additionally, a 
Testing COE will result in less fragmented testing processes across the Company. Reducing or eliminating 
testing silos leads to greater efficiencies in execution and results. A Testing COE will also result in cost 
avoidance as a dedicated team with broad oversight using modern standardized testing toolsets is more likely 
to discover defects in lower environments and ensure timely resolution. This keeps defects out of production 
systems which reduces support costs (internal SME’s, vendors, etc.).

Technical Evaluation/ Analysis 
An assessment was done by Capgemini on the Company’s current testing practices. Their findings showed a 
lack of any standards or formal structure around testing causing inefficiencies, higher costs, and inconsistent 
results. It was concluded that setting up a TCoE would lead to reduced cost, improved quality and reliability 
of technology solutions, and increased agility /speed to market to meet demand. 
 
An assessment was also performed by Cognizant which yielded similar themes to the Capgemini assessment. There is an 
overall lack of efficiency in testing design and execution and current testing practices require a significant amount of 
human capital to carry out. A focus on increased automation/orchestration, modernizing testing tool sets, and process 
efficiency are key findings, all of which are goals of the TCoE.

identified), newly initiated projects requiring testing services will be required to utilize the TCoE for all testing services. 
Completed projects with systems/platforms already in maintenance mode will be expected to leverage and transition over

Work Description: 
 
Metrix IDR is an application that produces the daily electric and steam hourly load forecasts. The 
Company’s system operations office relies on these forecasts to plan daily operations and the 
Company’s electricity supply office uses it to plan short term electric purchasing and generation 
scheduling. The objectives of this project include the following enhancements: 
 
• 
Continuing to develop and implement new forecast models for REV with assistance from 
Itron, the vendor of the MetrixIDR application 
• 
Integration of additional meters for new networks and 1,500 feeders, as well as 5-min 
forecast for feeders and networks  
• 
Development of associated model performance reports and statistics by substation, 
network, and feeder, in addition to model error monitoring 
• 
Integration of multiple weather vendors 
• 
Build an interface with EDAP to provide selected customer’s group forecasts. The interface 
should be dynamic enough for the users to build any selections as required by the business 
needs. For example, forecasting only load for office buildings and forecasting electric 
vehicle charging, distributed generation, non-wire solutions and batteries.  Furthermore, 
pricing data from NYISO enables efficient timing of charging and reduced cost of charging. 
In addition, there are forecasting opportunities for commercial building and residential 
customers (using AMI Data) 
• 
Upgrade the MetrixIDR application to the latest version and upgrade its underlying 
infrastructure as required. This will result in additional capabilities to query data from 
production using API/  
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 115 of 185


--- Page 314 ---
2 
 
• 
Integration of ConnectDER with MetrixIDR to collect actual and forecasted solar 
production data for regions to eliminate forecast errors due to DER programs in NYS. 
Additionally, explore and implement Google’s Sunroof Project for solar irradiance data.  
• 
Integrate MetrixIDR with NYISO notifications for transmission line and generation 
outages, wind, and solar forecast to better forecast zonal pricing or NYISO LBMP 
The project is scheduled to start in early 2023 and complete all tasks by 12/31/2026. 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
Providing an accurate forecast is a key component in supporting operational excellence and 
facilitating decision making in many parts of the Company. Forecasting accuracy leads to improved 
system operation efficiencies and lower energy supply costs. If a forecast is too high, more energy 
will be procured than needed. If a forecast is set too low, energy will be procured at a premium in 
the real-time market of the NYISO.  
 
Regional planning groups are in need to perform a more detailed assessment of feeder capabilities 
based on forecasts and number of customers enrolled in Demand Response programs. Forecasting 
Services is planning to provide these planning groups with additional tools necessary to meet these 
challenges.  
 
Decisions to commit generation units are also sensitive to forecasts. Fuel purchases necessary to 
commit to dispatch have significant impacts on reliability and supply costs.  
 
Should a distribution network market materialize through the development of REV and AMI, 
robust 5-minutes forecasting models will be necessary to support the operation of a distribution 
network market.  
 
Forecasting Services aims to provide the operators, the users of the commodity forecasts and the 
future REV needs, at least two forecasts from two different sources for reliability and verification.  
Without this upgrade, the new small control areas would not be able to dispatch internal resources 
efficiently and potentially result in a brownout or an entire load area blackout.  
 
Microsoft Report server, a companion of MetrixIDR, is used to furnish daily and for specific 
triggers multiple reports and statistics, which is used by many groups around the Company 
regarding its commodity operations. These systems need to be upgraded, as required, to address 
cyber security and to improve the users ability to more easily consume data by enhancing data 
visualization capabilities.  
 
This program will help Con Edison: 
• 
Keep up with any regulatory changes which could impact energy costs to its customers 
• 
Provide state-of-the-art software to assist Energy Management in managing approximately 
$3.5 billion in wholesale energy transactions  
• 
Increase efficiency by making data and results available in a standardized format that can 
be used to generate reports automatically for internal use, settlements, and regulatory 
reporting 
• 
Decrease the possibility for errors by automating processes, as appropriate. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation)

Energy Management has a long- range plan to consolidate applications into a few end-to-end 
platforms for the purchase, scheduling, settlement and accounting of power, gas, and financial 
instruments.   
 
This program is the initial step of the end-to-end process.  MetrixIDR provides the short-term 
forecast for electricity that is used to schedule power at the NYISO.   
 
This project directly mitigations two departmental risks, which include Inaccurate Demand 
Forecasts and Relationships with Stakeholders. 
 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
Alternative 1 description and reason for rejection 
 
If system changes are not implemented, a manual process will need to be developed which is more 
labor intensive and vulnerable to human error, as the existing system will no longer be supported 
by the vendor. All of Energy Management's daily forecast models are in MetrixIDR.  
 
Alternative 2 description and reason for rejection 
 
The Company could use an outside vendor that charges annual fees of around $25,000 per model. 
Currently, MetrixIDR runs approximately 200 models hourly and is planning to add 1,500 more. 
While the Company can benefit from the vendor’s dedicated expertise, the cost of the operation 
increases significantly and the flexibility of the Company to create and test new forecasts for the 
renewable resources is limited and costly. Further, it leaves analysts and forecasters exposed to 
forecasting techniques and unable to provide quality customer service to their internal customers. 
 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
Risk 1 
 
MetrixIDR is used for Electric System daily forecasting and planning. Maintaining and upgrading 
this system as well as increasing functionality for evolving markets, especially the consideration of 
modeling and forecasting of intermittent solar, batteries, and wind resources, are essential to the 
System Operation Organization, which is the prime user of this application.   
 
Risk 2 
 
Forecasting Services has the expertise to expand and automate existing forecasting models for all 
commodities and assist regional operations and engineering with the necessary data. If Forecasting 
Services does not provide the regions with the data, these departments will seek vendors to provide 
them with the information and the Company will not be taking advantage of the economies of scale 
resulting from adding forecasts to the existing tools.

2. Major financial benefits 
  
If these upgrades are not implemented, the Company will need to hire six additional employees. 
Two employees to compile and manage network data, coordinate with Distribution Operations, and 
interface with other REV supporting staff. Another four employees will be needed to create and 
manage network level and DER forecasting models daily, and to help manage the database, as much 
of the data verification and compilation will be performed manually. This would be six additional 
employees if MetrixIDR and the report server are not upgraded.  
 
With the upgrade and development of REV and AMI, we are already looking at increasing our staff 
by two additional full-time employees. 
 
Furthermore, the vendor makes periodic upgrades to the software. Any software version upgrades 
introduced by the vendor must be implemented to avoid any disruption in software support.  
 
In this case, the Company faces the risk of not being able to provide the commodities forecast until 
a new system is implemented.

Work Description: 
  
As part of Con Edison’s Digital Transformation, the Information Technology (IT) team is enhancing the Digital Factory program 
which brings business units and IT together to build impactful software products for the Company field operations employees and 
external customers. The Digital Factory will continue to be a key part of Con Edison’s overall Digital Transformation and will 
spearhead the development of enterprise-wide IT capabilities to develop, integrate, secure, deploy, maintain, and monitor mobile 
applications. The Digital Factory will introduce new roles and software development framework using Agile DevOps (Development 
Operations) methodology to support the Company’s growing need to build turn-key applications more efficiently and inexpensively, 
resulting in safer, more reliable, and cost effective solutions. 
Digital Factory is a program that will operate as follows: 
• 
Design Thinking and user centric approach that will focus on our employees and customers including 
automation of low value-added work and streamline external customer engagement through enhanced self-
service functionality and automation.  
• 
Agile development with a focus on delivering a solution in smaller phases,  so that the business can start 
realizing benefits earlier and increase capabilities. 
• 
Business Case model that focuses on cost reducing, safety, and operational excellence initiatives that align 
with the business vision and goals. 
• 
Cutting-edge DevOps technologies and platforms with reusable components that will speed up the 
development lifecycle. 
 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 121 of 185


--- Page 320 ---
These platforms will enable shorter development cycles (reducing costs) and increased deployment frequency (process consistency 
and avoidance of errors) in close alignment with business objectives (alignment with our cost reduction goals). Additionally, Digital 
Factory will leverage a user-centric approach that aligns tools to the way real people live and work. The Digital Factory will dedicate 
IT and business resources to redesign core work processes for safety, reliability, efficiency, and consistency, jointly owning the success 
of product solutions (lowering change management costs and increasing adoption in the operations groups). 
The Digital Factory will also build a new mobile platform of reusable (build once and re-use in multiple products, for example, a login 
screen) technology components (which will increase deployment speed, development speed, application security, and speed up time 
to market. The platform will leverage: 
• 
Cloud technology  
• 
Common application development framework that enables re-use of code and features 
• 
Catalog of reusable application programming interfaces (APIs)  
• 
Leverage single sign-on for mobile with security controls at platform level vs. application level 
Using this approach of Design Thinking, DevOps, cutting-edge technologies and re-usable technology components to develop 
software products that will drive adoption, process adherence, higher productivity, and higher quality work in the field. 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
 Mobile technology and advanced analytics are no longer optional, they are required. Recent advancements in software 
development tools, cloud technology and analytics are increasing and reducing the technology development lifecycle of 
software products. The Digital Factory has changed the way technology is deployed at Con Edison, fostering a 
collaborative approach between  IT and the Business.  
 
The Digital Factory will continue to alter the way IT can drive value in the business and will work collaboratively with 
an executive steering committee to build an enterprise mobile roadmap to ensure focus on the highest-impact business 
processes. Major use cases (and their potential impact through mobile and other digital solutions) could include:

analytics for reporting)

•

“shovel-ready” work)

corporate communications)

Work Description: 
  
This project covers CECONY and ORU, however the cost estimates for Capital and O&M are only CECONY’s share. 
 
Phase 1 (2022 – 2023) - The objective of this phase is to enhance and upgrade the pool of software scripts utilized by 
Forecasting Service / Con Edison Metering Authority for required NYISO reporting of the information below and to 
perform the following capabilities: 
• 
Automatically upload data for all zones (H,I,J), generation, tie lines (both external & internal), and distributed 
energy resources to the NYISO/PJM WBS 
• 
Perform the monthly O&R Substation Output Report, TOL calculation for specified generators and share data 
with TODRS, Zone Load (H, I, J) calculation  
• 
Select best available metering information based on a data source hierarchy coupled with Generator Status, 
Breaker Status, Source Quality, NYISO dispatch, NYISO PTS system data, etc. for Zone Load Calculation and all 
uploads 
• 
Incorporate the NYISO/PJM correction schedules, (2-day, monthly, four month, etc.) for timely update of data 
• 
Track data submitted to the NYISO/PJM as per their data requirements 
• 
Run queries, flag maintenance/repair/replace deadlines for equipment, track changes to the system, and keep a 
timeline to make sure things are resolved within NYISO required deadline 
• 
Compile the Yearly Meter Inventory as per NYISO Requirement 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 127 of 185


--- Page 326 ---
• 
The new system user interface will allow an inexperienced analyst to generate the reports and perform basic 
troubleshooting of the process 
• 
Better prepare the Company for the many new transmission and generation interfaces that will be built to 
support the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act 
• 
Tie into existing systems MV90, EDAP, MDMS, MAMS, PI, TODRS, NYISO/PJM WBS, EDNA, and any data 
that is provided via e-mail to perform above functions 
 
Phase II (2026) - The planned enhancements of phase 2 include: 
• 
Create a report for all CECONY generators Light and Power (L&P) and share data with TODRS 
• 
Identify meter issues and integrate with Company’s WMS 
• 
Provide automatic alerts if any source is experiencing issues such as alarms, data quality changes, data 
mismatch, data errors based on company specified metrics (feeder & equipment ratings, max generation, 
interconnection agreements, etc.), and if any maintenance, repair, or replacement to equipment is due 
• 
Calculate Load Loss in our service territory in accordance with the NYISO tariff 
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
This software enhancements and upgrade will aid in the rehabilitation, consolidation, standardization, and streamline 
Metering Authority functions. The software will perform the daily and repetitive manual functions of collecting, 
validating, and reporting energy demand data to the NYISO and PJM from transmission revenue class meters located at 
transmission ties with neighbor utilities and local generating stations.  
This function is required by FERC on the NYISO-TO Agreement Revenue Manual, NYDPS on the 16 NYCRR Part 92, 
FERC on the NERC MOD 31, FERC: PJM Manual 28; and NJ BPU. 
The vendor software will perform the NYISO and PJM Metering Authority functions while still allowing for oversight 
by the user. It will eliminate some manual operations and allow the Company to adapt the reporting process to meet 
market and internal  needs. This, in turn, will benefit market participants by improving the accuracy of financial 
settlements, since transactions will be more transparent and will allow for Company personnel to readily troubleshoot 
and resolve metering issues reported by generating companies and neighboring utilities. The vendor software will 
provide an enterprise solution across both CECONY and O&R that will allow for synergies across Company's and allow 
for business continuity. In addition, will enable the analysts to focus on other issues that arise related to this function, 
for example: follow-up on repairs, investigate meter challenges, transmission loss estimations, and work on new 
interconnections.  
Forecasting Services will purchase  off-the-shelf software that will require input/output data from EDAP, EDNA, 
MAMS, MDMS, MV90, TODRS, NYISO WBS, and OSI PI existing systems. The new software’s interfaces with the 
existing systems will be developed by Con Edison IT. Server hardware or a cloud based user interface will be required 
to host the new software. This new software along with the interfaces will be used to calculate and report power 
generation and transmission tie feeder information to the NYISO and PJM for market participant billing settlement.    
CECONY and O&R are responsible for approximately 45% of the load in New York State's Control Area (NYCA).  Con 
Edison's and O&R revenue class metering is submitted next day to the NYISO and PJM to provide accuracy in the 
financial settlements of energy purchased and generated. Because the process is manual and tedious, it is highly 
susceptible to errors due equipment malfunctions or human error. Thus, the current process poses a risk of non-
compliance to the Company from a functional and regulatory standpoint.  
When no adjustment is required, Energy Management releases the information to the NYISO. If the file needs to be 
adjusted, Energy Management manually adjusts the information and then releases the information to the NYISO.   This 
process is completed daily to comply with NYISO Metering Manual 25 Requirements. With the system enhancements 
and upgrade, Energy Management can streamline the existing process and account for future upgrades to internal and 
external systems. 
The decision to incorporate vendor software will allow us to eliminate Excel spreadsheets with embedded coding that is 
not accessible to the end user to determine if it collects the correct data, or if it's being modified through calculations. 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 128 of 185


--- Page 327 ---
This presents an issue when employees leave the Company or department because the developers of these Excel 
spreadsheets are not around to troubleshoot when there are problems.   
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
With the onset of the Automated Metering Infrastructure initiative, we recognize the need to upgrade our meter data 
collection, validation, and submission capabilities. As mentioned, legacy programs are being phased out or no longer in 
service.  The energy landscape across the utility industry is changing, specifically impacting Con Edison infrastructure is 
the addition of Energy Storage and Demand Energy Response devices.  The metering authority will be responsible for 
the accurate submission of load data for billing and reconciliation of these new systems. By adopting these technologies, 
we will more fully integrate clean energy into our delivery system so that we can continue meeting our customers' 
energy needs. IT will be a critical partner in this effort by helping to adopt technology and automation solutions that can 
handle rules-based and repetitive tasks without human intervention.  This will go on to enhance relationships with 
external customers and minimizes risks inaccurate record keeping and counterparty data.  
 
Risk 1 Name: Department.Energy Management.Fraud 
Risk 1 Description:  
Currently daily report submissions are not recorded and are 
assembled in an Excel sheet. An analyst could agree with a 
generating company on a kickback in the amounts reported. 1 
MW difference per hour is equivalent to $20,000 a month. 
 
Risk 2 Name: Department.Energy 
Management.Compliance 
Risk 2 Description:  
Con Edison must submit daily revenue class metering 
information, failing to do so for more than 90 days on one 
meter, results in a non-compliance with the NYISO-TO FERC 
regulated agreement, affects financial settlements, and accuracy 
in reporting for NERC MOD 31. 
 
Risk 3 Name: Department.Energy 
Management.Inaccurate demand forecasts related to 
Electric/Steam/Gas 
Risk 3 Description: Failing to account and report correctly for 
all the energy leads to inaccuracy in the forecast. The same data 
that is sent to the NYISO and balanced, it is the same data used 
to calculate the weather adjusted peak and produce the 
forecast. Analyst should have more time to analyze 
NYISO calculated losses for Con Edison and large 
hourly deviations.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
1) The Company can hire a third-party metering service provider or MSP. This company will need access to all our metering 
data and will independently report directly to NYISO and PJM. It could be challenging to keep our metering data confidential 
and potentially increase our vulnerability to third party risk. It may be difficult to implement this option since the MSP will 
need to have intrinsic knowledge of our electric system and details of our substations.  
 
2) Increase the number of people performing this function to allow rotational responsibilities. It needs additional 2 FTE, 
one for O&R and one for CECONY. The disadvantage is that reporting errors may still occur and it is hard to keep the 
continuity. Initially the two FTEs should be electrical engineers and with a good knowledge of a programming 
language.

Immediate non-compliance and financial losses.   
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
Retention of employees, improved accuracy and timing of reporting, and more efficient use of employee time, and 
improve regulatory compliance.

Work Description: 
 
The Transmission Owner Data Reporting System (TODRS) liaises between wholesale and retail 
markets reconciling small retail meters with market settlements at the ISOs (NYISO and PJM). Because 
the markets (NYISO, PJM, and CECONY and ORU retail programs) change continuously, these 
changes trigger modifications on the existing code, requires building of new TODRS SQL code, and the 
addition of new interfaces with all billing and customer information systems around the Company and 
external ISOs.  
 
With this in mind, it is challenging to anticipate the markets next changes and how it will directly 
impact TODRS. In the last few years alone the following changes were required to be made to TODRS: 
- 
Value Stack or Value of Distributed Energy Resources (VDER) program 
- 
NYSERDA report requirements to calculate Zero-Emissions Credits (ZEC) 
- 
Street Lighting software interface 
- 
Use of new AMI metering data 
- 
Changes in reconciliation of Unaccounted for Energy (UFE) in PJM by New Jersey Bureau of 
Public Utilities (BPU) 
- 
Adding Multiple peak days to Installed Capacity Calculations 
- 
Adoption of Company’s SDPID 
- 
New CC&B customer information system integration created by special accounts system 
changes to accommodate Net Metering program 
- 
ESCOs communications improvements 
- 
Changes in the NYISO Cyber-security protocols 
- 
Microsoft upgrades of Visual Studio 2013 to 2015 
- 
Enable Community Solar 
 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 134 of 185


--- Page 333 ---
2 
 
This white paper requests funding for 2023 – 2026+ to address anticipated market changes, regulatory 
policies, and system needs that will require enhancements to TODRS, they TODRS application 
software upgrades include:  
 
- 
Policy to incentivize Electric Vehicles 
- 
Moving energy aggregation to either CC&B or EDAP systems to handle AMI metering volume 
- 
Implement load shapes, not in accordance to PSC service class definitions, to increase the 
accuracy of the reports when AMI information is not available 
- 
Community Solar data interface 
- 
Policy incentivizing the electrification of the gas system 
- 
Enable community wind and create data interface  
- 
Implementation of Reforming the Energy Vision (REV) 
- 
Reconciliation of retail meters at the feeder level 
- 
Improve fraud detection and prevention at the time of reports submission 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
As the NYISO, PJM, and NYSERDA reporting requirements change to accommodate our clean energy 
future, it is essential to upgrade the system. The Company will not be able to manage these changes 
without hiring additional employees and increasing other resources to manually comply with new 
requirements.  Without the foregoing TODRS upgrades, the Company will be forced to make daily ad-
hoc manual changes to keep up with the evolving markets. As such, the Company would need to hire 
three employees to compile and manage manually customer consumption data and input these data 
into TODRS.   
  
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
 
This software reports monthly to the NYISO on large amounts of energy data in the wholesale market.  
Therefore, continuous improvement enhances the Company’s ability to better mitigate controllability 
for multiple department risks as follows:  
• 
Inaccurate Record Keeping and Counterparty Data  
o 
Because TODRS reports involve a large amount of monthly energy data and data from 
more than 150 ESCOs, the risk of misreporting is high if small errors are made. For 
example, three years ago, a small code error resulted in an $8 million overcharge to 
some ESCOs. At the wholesale level these types of issues can only be resolved with 
FERC approval after the NYISO market settles;a process that will  take several months. 
The financial cost of the amounts not settled is paid by customers until the issue is 
resolved.  As such, the Company needs to be proactive and ensure the market 
participants are served properly and timely. 
o 
AMI data Aggregation using EDAP or CC&B: This task is a process improvement 
using Company’s exiting IT infrastructure and may increase the reliability of the 
calculations. 
• 
Fraud 
o 
Implementing additional approval processes and peer verification to enhance fraud 
detection and prevention. 
• 
Compliance (Federal and State orders and market changes)  
o 
Implementing the aforementioned proposed enhancements will permit the Company 
to quickly address the market changes in TODRS architecture and capabilities. It will 
help maintain the current levels of reliability on the calculations and will avoid adding 
FTEs to the group to perform such calculations manually for the merging markets.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
The alternative would be to delay the necessary upgrades and to manually adjust the input data and 
perform only essential activities to continue to support evolving regulatory reporting requirements.  
Additional FTEs will depend on the complexity of the report and calculation changes. 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
 
The risk of no action is that manual processes will be required to extract and modify data from systems 
that have been changed and/or modified, to accommodate market participants’ requests, and to 
continue support evolving regulatory reporting requirements. The manual processes will be labor 
intensive, requiring the need for three more full-time employees, and manual processes increases the 
risk of human error. 
 
 
Non-Financial Benefits 
 
The non-financial benefits of this project are to assist the Company in meeting evolving regulatory 
reporting requirements, and market changes to improve market transparency and accuracy with Retail 
Access participants/ESCO and other market participants, and to continuously improve forecasting 
performance.

Work Description: 
The Consolidated Edison Enterprise Estimating Software HeavyBid, and P6 Loader software is currently located on a third-
party private cloud software.  The intent of this project is to move these applications to the Oracle Cloud already in use by 
other Con Edison Oracle products.  This approach is in line with the strategic approach of the Oracle Enterprise wide PULA 
agreement’s objective to streamline the number of applications and cloud services providers.  This consolidation provides 
increased cyber security, simplification of integrations and interfaces with currently used Oracle Primavera SaaS / Unifier 
applications, and significant cost savings.  
 
The process will require creating multiple instances for development, test, and production environments to support end user application 
usage and periodic upgrades due to releases, as required by the Oracle PULA agreement.  Infrastructure will be built in the cloud 
environment to support installation of the applications.  Citrix and terminal user licenses will be purchased to support secured access to 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 139 of 185


--- Page 338 ---
cloud applications. There will be an upfront maintenance cost associated with purchase of the applications that constitutes the 
subscription of the services with the vendor. This includes implementation cost, licensing and negotiated upfront subscription costs for 5 
years with the vendor.  Approved Property Records Account Ruling CE-2020-AR-000156-RO. 
 
Justification Summary: 
The HeavyBid and P6Loader applications will be installed in the Oracle Cloud to integrate with Oracle Primavera SaaS 
cloud applications already in use. This implementation will streamline the use of cloud applications by using the same 
cloud for all project management applications to increase performance and security. Eliminating the need to coordinate with 
various vendors for integrations, and operations provides increased leverage of Oracle Service Provider (OSP).  
For cost reduction and avoidance, deletion of the separate cloud host (LoadSpring) provides $87,000 (23%) savings of annual 
O&M costs, totaling over $434K by 2026.   
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation)

occur. 
 
Non-financial Benefits: 
All project management applications (Primavera P6, Unifier, P6 Loader and HeavyBid) will be housed with one Cloud 
vendor. Integrations will reside with one cloud vendor. Eliminating the need to coordinate with various vendors for 
integrations and operations provides increased leverage of OSP.

Work Description: 
  
Central Engineering has several remote monitoring systems that reside either on the Con Edison corporate network or their own 
standalone networks. Most of these applications are not using the current established Verizon Wireless VPN communication over 
SCADANet. Con Edison have established the Operational Technology Network (OTN) for housing data acquisition applications on 
a secure and dedicated infrastructure environment. This project is continuing the effort to build out the alternate OTN data center 
and to migrate existing systems, not limited to Transmission Operations and Substations applications onto a secure, dedicated 
network segment with secured communications on SCADANet. 
 
The company also has the Enterprise OSISoft’s PI expansion effort which can leverage this OTN environment to house it.  
OSISoft’s PI System is used for the real-time monitoring and visualization of critical operations in Electric, Gas and Steam that 
makes critical time sensitive decisions every day.  Currently, OTN is already housing the Pump House data from the substation used 
by the Central Engineering group. 
 
High-level implementation:  
• 
Build out the alternate data center site  
• 
Procure hardware & software for OTN  
• 
Setup hardware & software  
• 
Migrate application 
 
This OTN will continue to grow as more business systems are added to this network.  Per company’s direction on data center 
consolidation at Worth Street, this OTN infrastructure environment requires to be part of the consolidation planning and migration.  
OTN is currently using DELL and will need to migrate to the Nutanix hardware which is the company’s new standard.  This 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 146 of 185


--- Page 345 ---
includes the firewalls and switches upgrade as well. 
Justification Summary: 
 
To align with company’s data center consolidation and standards and to avoid risk of building evacuation of the OTN primary 
infrastructure site located at 30 Flatbush, and 4 IP DR site, OTN must be included in the consolidation effort and infrastructure 
upgrade.

Work Description: 
 
Information Technology adopted an Information Technology Service Management (“ITSM”) framework, 
outsourced IT activities to a Managed Service Provider and implemented an ITSM platform, ServiceNow, in 
2020. This framework requires continued operational improvements which are achieved through the 
maturation of our ITSM platform, ServiceNow.  This project calls for the implementation of ServiceNow’s 
supplemental modules: Automated Service Mapping and Application Portfolio Management.  
 
The Automated Service Mapping module provides IT with visibility into the relationship between 
infrastructure components and applications, and the services they provide to the company. This service 
visibility will allow IT to resolve service outages, optimize service architecture, and assess the service impact of 
infrastructure changes.   
 
Application Portfolio Management builds a comprehensive inventory of IT applications and allows IT to 
perform the following: business capability planning; application rationalization and technology risk 
management. IT will use the data gathered by this module to make decisions aligning technology solutions 
with business strategy.   
 
These modules will enhance IT’s ability to provide reliable services that fuel nearly every aspect of the 
business, promote operational efficiencies and support strategic decision making regarding the Company’s IT 
technologies and data.  The modules also play a key role in the Company assessing IT assets impacted by cyber 
related vulnerabilities and remediating those vulnerabilities more efficiently. 
 
O&M 
 
The implementation of ServiceNow modules will result in additional O&M increases for ServiceNow license 
costs and costs for new resources to provide ongoing support. 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 151 of 185


--- Page 350 ---
2 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
The implementation of Automated Service Mapping and Application Portfolio Management is the next step in 
IT’s roadmap for increasing visibility into IT’s entire operations.  It will ensure business continuity, 
infrastructure, and application compliance, and expand operational agility. Additional benefits are below:  
 
1. Reduce restoration times for IT system outages by quickly understanding the affected service(s) and 
component(s)  
2. Drive operational resilience by quickly determining systems status (availability and performance) 
3. Enhance our security posture by providing Cyber Security teams the ability to quickly identify critical 
infrastructure, services and applications affected by a security vulnerability  
4. Visibility of applications that pose security and support risks due to obsolescent technology 
5. Ability to identify relationships and dependencies between applications and infrastructure 
components  
6. Automated normalization and reconciliation of data across multiple sources to create service mappings 
(currently a manual effort) 
7. Improved data accuracy and broader identification of infrastructure and application attributes that can 
be leveraged by IT teams 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
• 
Alternative processes to this effort include the current model of manual data collection and 
maintenance of application and infrastructure data in the ServiceNow database 
• 
Siloed strategic decision making and technology road map planning using potentially inaccurate, 
outdated data, which can result in service outages and increased security risk 
• 
Customization and implementation of static fields in the ServiceNow platform to store manually 
maintained data 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
Risks of not implementing ServiceNow Automated Service Mapping and Application Portfolio Management 
include: 
• 
Increased costs associated with the manual collection and maintenance of application and 
infrastructure attributes 
• 
Manual collection of data leads to unreliable and inaccurate data, such as duplicates and 
misclassification 
• 
Extensive manual work to enable visibility into the organization’s application portfolio landscape and 
into infrastructure changes, affecting strategic decision making and application rationalization 
• 
Inability to leverage process and automation capabilities of the ServiceNow platform 
• 
Decreased customer satisfaction when inaccurate data triggers redundant approval requests, and 
failure to obtain required approvals for infrastructure or application changes 
• 
Inaccurate risk and impact assessments for changes where the IT components affected are not related 
to a business service 
• 
Risks of increased troubleshooting efforts and delayed issue resolution for impacted business services 
where service-affecting infrastructure components must be manually and physically identified 
• 
Increased complexity and cost of future ServiceNow upgrades due to customizations 
 
Non-Financial Benefits

Work Description: 
 
Electric, Gas and Steam Forecasting (together, referred to as “EGS Forecasting”) currently uses multiple sources to 
obtain the information required to perform monthly variance analysis of volumes and revenues and to generate 
forecasts.  ESG Forecasting employees reach out to several departments and manually pull data from many different 
Company systems. These processes are time-consuming, and are potentially prone to error, since some of the steps are 
manual. The proposed solution is to the develop a single and complete source of enterprise data used to support 
customer, sales, and revenue analytics that is housed in a user-friendly system that can automate the pull of critical data 
from across the Company’s systems, automate the reconciliation process, and simplify and expedite the forecasting 
process. This project will also include exploring the potential use of AMI data to improve forecasting accuracy. 
 
Currently, EGS Forecasting obtains data on a monthly basis using Microsoft Access, which queries the point-in-time 
data-extract pulled from the company’s billing system. Access is a tool generally used for small databases with limited 
users. A key source system is REVSTAT, a revenue statistics reporting system that houses summarized data for electric 
and gas. REVSTAT only allows for data to be obtained by service code. However, an enterprise scale reporting 
repository that obtains more detailed information, for example, by account number, is needed for breaking down 
revenue data into smaller sub-categories to better analyze the data and its components.   
 
We are looking for the product to provide the following capabilities:  
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 156 of 185


--- Page 355 ---
• 
Act as a repository of volume and revenue data that can be queried to extract customer usage information / 
patterns across multiple dimensions (e.g., time range, frequency, service classification, geographical location, 
other available AMI data)  
• 
Automate data gathering, monthly variance analysis and reporting.   
• 
Research monthly billing and provide a listing of accounts and the energy billed when the number of days 
exceed 34 days (bulk billing on one bill). For example, if a bill is for the period from Jan 2021 to Sept 2021, the 
system should flag that a multiple billing has occurred.  Similarly, the system should also flag when multiple 
bills occur in a month.  The system should also have the ability to capture and include the original billing in its 
adjustment of monthly billing if a cancelation resulted in the multi or bulk billing.  
• 
Gas Accounts - The system needs to review the daily actual HDD, the heating slope, and base usage factors that 
are provided to the billing system, to properly adjust historical usage when bulk billing occurs. 
• 
Electric Accounts - Same issue with bulk and multi bills as with gas, but over both heating and cooling seasons.  
The system would be required to provide information on the actual HDD and CDD from the billing system to 
match the period of the bulk billing. The system should also have the heating and cooling slopes that the 
econometric models have determined for each service class.  Additionally, it should provide the adjustment that 
should be made to the monthly volumes so the historical usage in the econometric models is corrected. 
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
The current manual process is not sustainable and will challenge our agility in addressing the ever evolving regulatory 
and technology landscape and to meet our customers expectation.  The proposed solution is to the develop a single and 
complete source of enterprise data used to support customer, sales, and revenue analytics that is housed in a user-
friendly system that can automate the pull of critical data from across the Company’s systems, automate the 
reconciliation process, and simplify and expedite the forecasting process. This project will also include exploring the 
potential use of AMI data to improve forecasting accuracy. 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation)

controllability of this risk event.

Non-financial Benefits: 
 
The goal of this project is to create one single source of enterprise data that will result in the following: 
• 
Customer Benefits – A more in-depth understanding of customer usage patterns and better impact analysis 
reporting for making decisions at the service class and customer level. 
• 
Organizational Improvements – Enhancing data flow and analytics transparency across the Company and 
developing new insights from time spent more on analytics as opposed to data gathering.  
• 
Financial and Regulatory Risk Reduction – Improve tracking and reporting of bill components and the accuracy 
and timeliness of monthly, quarterly, and annual revenue reporting process. 
• 
Value-added Analysis: Reduce administrative tasks to allow more time to be spent performing greater value data analytics, 
and to improve forecasting models. 
• 
Improved Forecast Accuracy: Reduced data error will lead to greater forecast accuracy that will have downstream positive 
benefits for finance, accounting, and operations.  A more accurate forecast will lead to less under purchasing or over 
purchasing of commodities on same-day energy needs.  
• 
Improved Analytical Capabilities:  Easier access to customer usage data across more dimensions allow more granular 
analysis to determine potential impact of certain scenarios (e.g., covid, network issues) 
• 
Improved ability to have agile forecasting capabilities to meet the growing expectations of our regulators, customers, and 
stakeholders.  A more accurate energy forecast will provide better hedging on future energy needs which will reduce costs 
on future energy needs to meet our customers' needs.

Work Description: 
 
Technology Currency and Sustainability is a recurring program that constitutes upgrading of the technologies across 
servers, databases, desktop operating systems and underlying technology stack of the application. Technologies must be 
upgraded to be compliant with manfucturer's support and receive security/vulnerability patches.  
Through this capital investment, there are 4 main initiatives. 
1. Con Edison IT is working on significant upgrade of its server Operating Systems to the minimum OEM 
supported O/S. This will provide continued compatibility with the latest implementation of server Operating 
Systems deployed at Con Edison.  
2.  Databases – Scope of activities: The objective of this project is to purchase and install the latest databases, test, 
and remediate Con Edison software applications on these databases. This will provide continued compatibility 
with the latest implementation of Microsoft’s SQL and Oracle databases deployed at Con Edison.  
3. Desktop – Scope of activities: The intent of this project is to purchase and install Windows 10 Enterprise 2016 
LTSB to be installed on all desktops and laptops at Con Edison. This includes efforts to identify, test, and 
remediate Con Edison applications to provide continued compatibility on the latest implementation of 
Microsoft’s Operating System.  
4. Underlying Technology Stack The intent of this project is to enhance/upgrade the underlying technology of the 
application for shelf life sustainability. This includes efforts to identify, configure, develop, implement, test, and 
remediate Con Edison applications to provide continued compatibility on the latest implementation of 
technology.  
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 161 of 185


--- Page 360 ---
Justification Summary: 
 
The software that runs on the servers must be compatible with the operating system running on that server for it to 
operate successfully. If the server application software is not compatible with the new server, the operating system must 
be upgraded or replaced to keep applications in production. Upgrading the software to the latest version increases the 
useful life of the system, supports the energy commodity operations and therefore helps support the safe and reliable 
service to customers. 
Con Edison's server and database platform relies on the core software that enables it to be functional. The underlying 
software must be maintained and kept currency to sustain a secure environment, protect customer information and 
prevent authorized access. This program is critical to maintaining the security of the server environment and continued 
availability of the business system portfolio and allows us to better protect customer information.    
Con Edison's standard windows platform. The efforts of the program will allow Con Edison to meet the Windows 10 
deployments and replace the devices with obsolete OS versions. In addition, remediating business applications to utilize 
the platform will allowprovide our applications to remain functional and maintained in the event of future changes.

Work Description: 
 
Con Edison’s IT department manages a portfolio of approximately 500 applications in support of our Electric, Gas, 
Steam and Shared Services organizations.  Over the next 3 years, IT is investing in capital projects to modernize, 
upgrade, replace, consolidate, and retire applications within this portfolio.   
 
IT’s leadership is focusing on: 
• 
Standardize, rationalize, consolidate, and modernize the application portfolio  
• 
Migrate on premise applications that traditionally require upgrades every 1 to 3 years, to cloud based 
applications that typically get upgrades quarterly as applicable  
• 
Automate support processes, such as patching, monitoring, testing and production promotions     
• 
Keep applications current in terms of their technology stack to avoid potential cyber threats 
  
Through this capital investment, there are 2 main initiatives. 
1. Retire and/or replace approximately 150-200 of the 500 applications over the next 3 years.  We expect the 
remaining portfolio of approximately 300 applications to be our revised long-term baseline/steady state 
portfolio of applications.  IT has completed a technical currency analysis on the remaining 300 steady state 
applications.  Technology currency is the ongoing process of understanding how current an item of hardware 
or software is, compared to the latest available version. Managing technology currency is a vital part of 
Exhibit___(IT-2)
Page 167 of 185


--- Page 366 ---
operational resilience as organizations attempt to balance the cost associated with maintaining technology 
currency versus the risk posed.  Technical currency includes versions of servers, databases, desktop operating 
systems, as well as application upgrades and consolidation that are necessary to comply with technology 
standards, cyber compliance, vendor compliance and PSC mandated requests.  We estimate that approximately 
50% (150) require modernization and technical upgrades to keep the applications functionally viable and 
technically safe.  Many of the applications have underlying technologies that are more than several versions 
behind current.   
We estimate a 3-year effort with approximately 50 applications per year being upgraded.  The main drivers of 
the technology upgrades/enhancements effort are:  
1. Increase operational efficiencies by keeping applications functionally current 
2. Reduce technology obsolescence to mitigate Cyber risks  
3. Avoid losing vendor/software support for obsolete technologies 
  
2. We will also evaluate if standardization or consolidation to a single enterprise technology is needed.  
Duplicative platforms result in increased license, maintenance, and support costs.  For example, with 
application modernization newer tools like Azure Dev Ops and Git Hub are the new standard.  A project to 
migrate all IT code from Team Foundation Server to Azure Dev Ops is included in this program.  In addition, 
we have various tools that perform customer related functions.  As an integrated project to larger customer 
related initiatives, we have included the consolidation of these technologies to a new standard.     
 
 
   
 
Justification Summary: 
 
The objective of this project is to enforce enterprise application standards through consolidation and reduction of 
obsolete technology.   Duplicative platforms and obsolete technology results in increased costs for licenses, maintenance 
and support.  In addition, obsolete technology leads to cyber risk and falling behind from a functionality perspective 
leads to inefficient use of software and ultimately leads to increased support costs.  These upgrades are required as 
systems vendors keep phasing out support for the existing operating systems, databases, and applications and release 
new versions to provide enhanced security and increased functionality. 
The main drivers of this effort are:  
• 
Increase operational efficiencies by keeping applications functionally current 
• 
Consolidate and rationalize various applications 
• 
Reduce technology obsolescence to mitigate risks  
• 
Avoid losing vendor/software support 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
Our long-range plan is to have a rationalized, and technically current set of steady state applications to support the 
enterprise.  This strategy includes modernization, retirements and consolidation of the application portfolio as well as 
maintaining technical currency to avoid cyber threat and functionality decline.

Technology currency is the ongoing process of understanding how current an item of hardware or software is, 
compared to the latest available version. Managing technology currency is a vital part of operational resilience as 
organizations attempt to balance the cost associated with maintaining technology currency versus the risk posed.  
Servers, databases, desktop operating systems, as well as application upgrades and consolidation are necessary to 
comply with technology standards, cyber compliance, vendor compliance and PSC mandated requests.   
 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Risk 1 
Cyber Risk:  Not keeping technologies up to current versions lead to cyber security vulnerabilities.  Key applications 
remain on an unsupported technology requiring separate support resources, technologies, and infrastructure and leave 
the systems vulnerable for cyberattacks.  In addition, security updates are not provided and vendor support ends after a 
certain point, increasing the cyber risk on existing code if not migrated to a new standard. 
 
Risk 2 
Increased Cost: Higher incremental support costs from hardware and software vendors.  Older version maintenance 
eventually leads to incremental support costs.  
  
Risk 3 
Reduced availability of critical business applications. Software code must be upgraded or rewritten to meet business 
SLA’s.  
 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
Upgrading to the new standards will keep the applications and technologies current, operational and secure.

4. Basis for estimate 
 
There are 2 main components are included in the estimate. 
• 
IT MSP Cognizant has conducted an assessment on our current technologies that need to be upgraded based on 
obsolescence.  Using that as a guideline, IT will partner will Cognizant to establish forecasting and then refine 
estimates based on specific applications that require remediation. IT will establish a three-year plan to ensure 
completion of this important effort.  Cognizant infrastructure support costs are approximately 30% of the total 
costs.  A total cost of $39M for outsourced and insourced applications has been estimated.  As mentioned above our goal is 
to modernize 50 applications per year. 
o 
$24M for outsourced applications over the three-year period.  This includes $6M per year to Cognizant and $2M 
per year internal labor.   
o 
$15M for the insourced applications.  This includes $5M per year for internal labor.  
• 
A total of $50M has been estimated for enterprise application rationalization and consolidation for technologies 
such as customer facing tools, messaging tools, mobility platforms and Azure Dev Ops, Git Hub and Code QL.  
Specialized skill sets and resources are warranted to develop and rewrite application code pipelines or migrate, 
test, and implement. 
o 
An estimate for the migration of an application like TFS is ~$5M dollars per year.  This is inclusive of a 
project manager, development team (3 resources) as well as the IT and Cognizant resources to test the 
applications.  
o 
We assumed 3-4 application consolidations per year at $5M per application.

The project is critical for supporting daily business operations and moving to the latest software and hardware 
technologies and environment will help improve cyber compliance, application software management costs and 
reliability.
