Work Description: 
Items in XM-10 are critical computing components that support the infrastructure necessary to provide reliable and resilient data centers, 
networks and devices that support employees and applications.  Device refreshes are required to support newer applications and the 
demand for computing resources is continually increasing due to the complexity of applications and cyber security scanning tools.  XM10 
supports all devices such as desktops, tablets, laptops, MDTs and printers.  In addition to devices, XM10 supports infrastructure 
equipment, data centers and networks.   
 
The cost of running state of the art data centers continues to grow.  Many applications specifically related to storm or event management 
require the appropriate redundancy and resiliency in place.  It is essential that we continue to harden these environments with the appropriate 
investments and upgrades in server and storage infrastructure, mainframe, Internet facing technologies and networks (Local Area Networks 
(LANs), Wide Area Networks (WANs), wireless and fiber channel networks).

In addition to providing reliable and resilient access to corporate systems, as the threat landscape continues to increase these investments 
are required to stay on current technologies to prevent against cyber concerns.  
Key initiatives in 2023- 2025 include: 
• 
Yearly refresh of devices including the desktop, laptop, tablet, printer, plotter, and MDT inventory  
• 
LAN switches upgrades

Justification Summary: 
 
Without the equipment in XM10, Con Edison's ability to provide reliable access to Company computing systems would be adversely 
impacted. This equipment is essential to the operation of the Company's daily business activities and is integral to all Company 
organizations.  XM10 equips employees with technology and devices to access information and systems in the office, field, and remotely 
and ensures the core IT infrastructure is supportable, reliable, and accessible.   
With the increased focus on technology modernization and N-1 versioning we need to efficiently manage various upgrades for devices and 
infrastructure. 
The programs under the XM-10 budget support: 
• 
Safety – private communications which provide isolation from public sources of vulnerability and enable Con Edison to 
respond rapidly to emergency situations and critical incidents over secure and segmented channels.  These private 
communication systems provide reliable performance and highest priority for life-sustaining alerting and feeder relay 
protection.  The equipment will be maintained in a vendor-supportable state and refreshed prior to its end-of-life cycle, 
which includes periodic security patches and hardware upgrades through our purchasing channels. 
• 
Operational Efficiency – the communication, data computing, and networking infrastructure provides a stable and efficient 
platform for the applications and processes used by the various operating businesses to achieve and maintain high levels of

• 
Customer Enablement - the customer-centric applications used in the customer contact centers depend on the capital

and reliable experience.  This program addresses the need to meet current customer expectations for more information 
delivered in a variety of easily consumable formats such as mobile platforms, while also maintaining the security, integrity, 
and confidentiality of sensitive customer information. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation)

expansion of the telecommunications equipment to support Company wireless and telephone 
networks, end user customized telecom solutions and subscriber equipment upgrades.  This 
telecommunication technology enables employees to communicate and access business systems 
including the various process management systems: electric, gas, steam operations work 
processes, monitoring, and control systems, as well as a number of other systems like financial, 
human resources, and legal. Information Technology’s Communications Operations 
Department is the control agent for XM8. The following equipment is covered under XM8:  
 
• Telephony and video equipment replacements and upgrades 
• Capacity increases and monitoring of various telephony and radio communications 
systems 
• Radio System capacity upgrades and technology refreshes 
• Handheld radio replacements 
• Antenna installations and replacements at Company cell sites  
• Voice over IP (VOIP) equipment 
• Conference room audio/video equipment 
• End user subscriber telephony equipment and terminals 
• Customized end-user telecom solutions

for newly built command trailers 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
The XM8 general equipment category upgrades, expands and implements voice and telephony 
telecommunications tools that leverage both wireless and wired technology. This includes 
telephones, radios, antennas, and associated electronic components necessary to provide private 
voice and data services as needed by operating areas. It also encompasses special custom designs 
to provide backup tactical communications to support restoration associated with major events 
like storms.   
 
Equipment covered in XM8 is essential in enabling critical communications for the different 
operating units (electric, gas, steam) during normal operations and more importantly during 
storm events for customer restorations.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
Alternatives include increased reliance on carriers and expense increases for ongoing lease costs 
for telephony and field communications. Yet even under that scenario, telephones including 
desk phones, wall phones, console phones and cell phones would need to be purchased. 
Telecommunications equipment is purchased in bulk and competitively bid to take advantage of 
volume discounts. Information Technology has initiated programs, such as equipment 
standardization, to optimize these costs. Using the same manufacturer (i.e., Motorola, Ericsson) 
has allowed the Company to obtain larger discounts. Information Technology has been utilizing 
contract negotiation best practices for price and duration of contracts.  
 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
No action would likely result in multiple communications equipment failures including 
telephone systems, data circuits, radio systems, and protection circuits as a result of the inability 
to purchase spare parts and maintain supportability of the communication systems. In that case, 
availability of critical communications systems would be severely reduced. Reliable 
communications systems and distribution automation systems are required to support field 
customer restoration activities and the automation of the distribution system to maintain electric, 
gas, and steam services.  This equipment is essential to provide both system reliability, customer 
service as well as employee safety. 
 
Non-Financial Benefits

o Provides carrier diversity to critical communication circuits

o Scales capacity over time through card replacements

Project Risks and Mitigation Plan 
 
The major risks to XM8 equipment and systems are the unavailability of direct replacement for 
some of the older technologies and appliances that have been migrated to purely software-based 
solutions, middleware and cloud services which do not provide the resilience and durability and 
mission critical performance under challenging circumstances. There is also the risk of greater 
cyber vulnerability as the end devices depend more and more on code. These risks are managed 
by careful, early, and thorough evaluation of the replacement technologies and more emphasis 
on cyber risk assessment as opposed to focus on raw performance. Custom solutions must 
balance cost and long-term supportability by shortening the life cycle of the new systems by 
more frequent technology assessments. 
 
 
Technical Evaluation / Analysis 
 
XM8 equipment has an extended life and is replaced in 10–15-year increments. This equipment 
is mostly carrier grade communications equipment to support voice and other communication 
requirements. Information Technology performs planning and analysis on all technologies 
introduced. Solutions are investigated in conjunction with the IT strategy and vision planning 
process. Collaboration between IT advisors, carriers, vendors, and Company employees helps to 
ensure the selection of optimal solutions.

Work Description: 
This project represents an ongoing investment in the continuation of the Company’s move from the legacy Hyperion 
Planning (HP) suite of planning and budgeting applications to the newer Enterprise Planning and Budgeting Cloud 
Service (EPBCS) technology platform.  EPBCS was successfully implemented in 2020 and utilized for the 2020 planning 
cycle for the first time.  Through implementation and based on user experience we continue to implement 
enhancements to the tool to provide additional reporting capability, better integration of actuals and forecasting 
processes, data maps and data governance processes.  The enhancement work is expected to continue through 2023.  
Starting in 2024 funding is earmarked to integrate updates and processes that result from the Oracle Human Capital 
Management (HCM) project and Oracle EBS cloud migration project.   
Data integration, inputting data once, and a single source of the true are core tenants of cloud based financial systems. 
In order to enable this single input and single source of the truth, all systems (financial and non-financial) must be 
integrated.  To enable this integration, each system must have common data definitions for things like Account, 
Geography, Management Unit, Legal Entity, etc. For ePBCS specifically the following integrations will be critical to 
meet the requirement of FP&A and the business: 
1.
HCM to Workforce planning:  Headcount, salary, title, department, user permissions and other data fields will
be pulled directly from HCM rather than re-input into ePBCS.  This will be used not only to support production
of plans (head count and labor costs) but will also be supported for access provision and validation rules within
ePBCS.  As such, we need to make sure the inbound data can be integrated with or mapped into the current
structures which are in ePBCS today.
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 2 of 64


--- Page 386 ---
2.
Fusion Cloud to ePBCS: Both the projects module, as well as other GL data (Revenue, other expenses, equity,
other items, statistical accounts, etc.) will be integrated into ePBCS.  This enables all plan to actuals analysis to
occur in the planning application.  It’s critical that the source of actuals data (projects and the GL) be of a
complementary structure to how plans and forecasts are produced in ePBCS.  This will enable less effort in the
production of forecasts and plans, and easier interpretations of variances between actual and plan.
The integrations of these two systems, aside from technology and data considerations, will have upstream and 
downstream impacts on timing and process (e.g., timing of Manual journal entries in Cloud EBS need to be considered 
in the consolidated plan (ePBCS) and actual (FCCS) tools.  Due to these close linkages of process, data, and technology, 
it is critical that the current ePBCS application configuration is updated in sync with the changes in those source 
applications.   
Justification Summary: 
This program will ensure the planning and budgeting tools at the Company are maintained and enhanced to allow for 
efficient and effective budgeting and planning processes.  The system is critical in providing accurate planning forecasts 
for internal budget reviews and approvals and regulatory proceedings such as rate cases.

Work Description:
The objective of this project is to implement a software solution (i.e., Archer a Governance Risk and Compliance (GRC) 
Software) to automate, standardize, and centralize the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) and Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) 
framework and workflows. This will require the procurement of four ERM/SOX related modules (i.e., Control 
Monitoring Program Management, Top-Down Risk Assessment, Bottom-Up Risk Assessment, and Key Indicator 
Management) and the hiring of a consultant to gather requirements, design, implement, test, and deploy the software 
solution. This project is driven by recommendations derived from the following: 1) Audit of ERM framework and 
management of risks, 2) an external consultants review of assurance functions for fit and alignment to Archer’s use 
cases and capabilities, and 3) ERM key stakeholder feedback sessions. 
Justification Summary: 
ERM's framework is a manual process that uses Microsoft Office to interact with over 250 employees and manage 
hundreds of documents. Similarly, SOX's framework also employs Microsoft Office to interact with over 200 employees 
throughout the Company. ERM and SOX are looking to procure a software to electronically support their respective 
processes and have a direct user interface for inputting and collecting risk and control information, including a database 
to retain historic data with easy extraction and version control, and that has customizable reports and dashboards. 
The benefit realized from a SOX perspective will be a centralized repository of controls with automated workflows for 
approval. This will greatly reduce the burden of manual sign off by business and improve the stakeholder experience.  
Additionally, the tool will assist with tracking material changes within our control environment. 
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 7 of 64


--- Page 391 ---
This software will help address ERM's current challenge of having poor visibility into the interrelationships between 
risks and their associated attributes, which is an integral part of monitoring and reporting the Company's risk exposure. 
Additionally, these attributes are not currently tracked in real-time, are not easily accessible, and are allocated across 
various software (i.e., Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Word).  The procurement and deployment of these modules are 
in response to the recommendations of external parties, which include:   
1) This year the ERM program was audited, by Internal Audit, to determine the adequacy and effectiveness of the 
ERM framework design and management of corporate and department risks. Auditing deemed the ERM 
controls sufficient, however they advised on the following observations and solutions: 
Recommendation: Leverage GRC Tool 
• 
Observations 
o 
Documentation is shared manually through a shared network drive and emails 
o 
ERM requirements are not always updated in a timely manner nor systematically tracked 
o 
ERM activities are reliant on key people and institutional knowledge to perform responsibilities 
• 
Proposed Solution 
o 
Utilize a GRC tool to centralize documentation and increase visibility across the organization 
o 
Allows for continuous improvement opportunities across workstreams, reduces the amount of manual 
labor in ERM activities, and increases visibility across internal stakeholders 
Recommendation: Automate KRI Monitoring Process 
• 
Observations 
o 
There is a defined foundation for monitoring and reporting while looking for improvement 
opportunities 
o 
Few automation tools are being used, leading to processes that are manual and time-consuming 
o 
Current KRI monitoring is more reactive than proactive in nature 
• 
Proposed solution 
o 
Begin adoption of continuous monitoring processes with an automation roadmap 
o 
Leverage an RPA or ETL tool to support KRI monitoring and reporting 
o 
Adopting automaton will encourage a more proactive risk management mindset throughout the 
enterprise 
2) This year, an external consultant assessed SOX, ERM, and other assurance functions fit and alignment to 
Archer's use case and capabilities and developed an Archer Roadmap.  ERM and SOX reviewed the consultant's 
recommendations and has decided to action those that are appropriate and align with Audit's observations.  
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation)

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
ERM and SOX researched alternative software solutions (e.g., CURA, Workiva, and Service Now, Navex) to ensure it 
aligned with IT’s principles of Promoting One Enterprise, Excel at the Basics, Foster/Promote Innovation, and 
Implementation Methodology Ensures Speed, Flexibility & Simple Design. In particular, the Oracle suite was analyzed 
and that system does not currently house the capabilities that is needed by ERM/SOX. The Company—via Compliance 
Management—has already made a significant investment in utilizing RSA Archer as its enterprise compliance 
management and action tracking software. ERM, in collaboration with Compliance Management, has also made an 
initial investment of $143,000 in 2018 procuring a pilot prototype in RSA Archer for risk management and, in 2020, made 
another investment of $199,000 to hire a consultant to perform an assessment of assurance functions fit and alignment to 
Archer’s use cases and capabilities and to perform an in-depth ERM Program Assessment. The consultants were also 
tasked with advising if there were better software options than Archer to perform assurance related tasks. They 
recommended the best option is to build out functionality to support the ERM and SOX process within the Company’s 
existing platform. RSA Archer has the potential to be expanded in the future to support other Governance Risk and 
Compliance (GRC) functions across the enterprise, including operations risk management, quality management, 
supplier relationship management and audit functions 
Risk of No Action: 
 
The ERM program is currently excessively manual in nature, which may result in delays in collecting risk information 
and reporting and managing the Company’s level of risk exposure to its most material risk. These risks should leverage 
real-time data and permit the Company to identify, mitigate, monitor and report risks in a timely manner. Without 
proceeding with this project, the Company would continue to utilize current manual processes using Microsoft Office. 
Current processes are not standardized, are manual in nature, have poor visibility into the interrelationships between 
risk and associated attributes, and do not support efficient information sharing across the Company thereby increasing 
the risk of process fatigue, human error, and not leveraging the real-time data to reduce and manage risk.

Work Description: 
This project will provide the necessary innovation and technology to transform and improve our employees 
learning experience and performance. To achieve this, we must:  
•
Assess current training methodologies and curriculum inventory
•
Create training governance process and policies by:
o
Benchmarking across major industries including the Utility industry
o
Stakeholder assessments
•
Develop a digital learning platform consisting of :
o
Replacement of the existing Learning Management System (LMS)
o
Integration of multiple technology solutions to provide an efficient mix of systems, hardware, software,
and process development for the enterprise.
o
Use of corporate IT integrated solutions that cross organization needs, e.g., Cloud based Video and life
cast training.
•
Implement new the learning strategy to:
o
Deliver the enhanced employee learning experience to the employee, improving engagement and
retention o Improve employee performance in the work place
o
Meet organizational training needs, optimize training hours, and comply with regulatory training
requirements.
The project team will develop a learning strategy that will transform how we prepare our employees to meet the 
challenges of a rapidly changing work environment as technology and innovation shape the future of the utility 
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 14 of 64


--- Page 398 ---
 
business. The objective is to create a learning platform that embraces employee development, has the ability to address 
new technology and training methods and provides the best training experience at the right time and place. Using 
design principles and a data-driven approach, we will redesign and or replace key processes and systems over multiple 
years. This includes the replacement of the current LMS system and integration of a Cloud based platform to support a 
mobile learning philosophy that will place training tools into field for the employees use. This process will enable us to 
manage the entire learner experience benefiting our learners, the organizations we support, our stakeholders and 
ultimately the company's performance.  
 
The goal is to establish and sustain an excellent training culture through innovative learning solutions by: 
 
• 
Creating dynamic learning experiences that build on our strong foundation using state of the art 
technology.  
• 
Developing the scope, approach and design of each element of the project, cognizant of the 
interrelationships between them. 
• 
Identifying activities, processes, and systems for improvement 
o 
Establish a governance Process.  
o 
Evaluating training proficiency and cost effectiveness 
o 
Establishing performance measurement, control plans and reporting around training 
• 
Delivering optimal learning strategies to meet changing business needs. 
• 
Promoting and growing a strong learning culture. 
• 
Expanding the learning beyond the classroom. 
• 
Enhancing and modeling Diversity and Inclusion as an integral part of the learning experience. 
• 
Collaborating with our Stakeholder to respond to changing or developing needs such as the current 
AMI project and future BCO initiatives. 
• 
Realizing O&M costs savings implemented in phases throughout the project, e.g., reduce reproduction 
costs, resources and optimized training curriculum  
 
These projects form the cornerstone of L&I’s Business Cost Optimization (BCO) initiative and provide the core 
learning foundation successfully meet future enterprise needs.  
 
Justification Summary: 
 
• 
Justification:  
Today's learners' expectations, the changing utility landscape, the external pressure of innovation and technology 
combined with an enterprise need to have a flexible work force are driving this initiative.  The adoption of online 
and digital learning models continue to accelerate at a rapid pace, changing the way individuals learn and how 
training is delivered. This shift is transforming traditional learning. 
Integrating new learning technologies and instructional design is an effective way of training today's 
workforce.  The speed and flexibility of mixed learning is imperative to enhancing the learning experience and 
productivity of the modern workforce, as training continues beyond the classroom.   
To maximize the benefits of training it is imperative the training goals of the company are in alignment with the 
Company's top priorities: safety, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and the customer experience.   
Starting in 2019 and continuing over the next five years, we will transform the delivery and absorption of training 
material from an instructor-led walled classroom to one where an SME utilizes mix of digital material and physical, 
mobile and virtual environments.   
The goal of implementing targeted cognitive learning strategies is to: 
 
• 
Increase technical proficiency, employee safety, operational excellence, a measurable impact to the 
business and the ability to react dynamically in a technical environment with a compressed learning 
curve.

• 
Infuse and reinforce a motivation toward continuous learning and the ability to gather and analyze 
situations and data to support business and customer needs.  
• 
Prepare the workforce for a rapidly changing environment by enabling them to learn and process 
information from digitally available resources that are updated in real time not subject to publication 
dates.  
• 
Set in place a series of evolving steps to reach the digital learning vision.  
Tactics include, but are not limited to:   
• 
Integrating a mix of learning tools and approaches utilizing technology e.g., e-Books, Mobile content, 
Virtual/Augmented Reality.   
• 
Providing various delivery channels for training content to enable greater access and improved/same 
proficiency e.g., Mobile devices, enhanced learning spaces. Distance learning. 
• 
Optimizing the level of training per employee for safety, job requirements, promotions, advancement, 
etc. 
• 
Ensuring the cost effectiveness of learning.  
• 
Acting as a standard and resource for good pedagogy for the enterprise and the center of learning. 
• 
Reviewing, updating and creating policies and procedures for training governance. 
• 
Responding to the speed of business and ensuring agility to respond to events and changing customer 
needs e.g. Just in Time training. 
• 
Benchmarking to ensure continuous improvement and effectiveness of learning e.g. Training hours per 
employee. 
• 
Improving employee-learning Journey to attract, develop and retain qualified employees. 
•

Work Description: 
Develop a Mobile Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Subject Matter Expert (SME) system that uses 
technology to allow field personnel to communicate by use of a personal body camera and microphone with 
EHS SME personnel 24 by 7. The system would also be used to communicate with various commodity 
Operations SME personnel for complicated work tasks that may require additional or enhance Job Briefings 
Justification Summary: 
Typical overhead work involves working on live cable in various voltage classifications (4 kV, 13 kV, 27 kV). 
Company procedures govern most of these work tasks but often the choice made by the employee on the work 
location dictates the protective devices that are actually used. Typical gas leak repairs also are governed by 
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 21 of 64


--- Page 405 ---
Company procedures but field decisions are required to be made by the mechanic at the location. The ability 
to have an SME review the conditions in real time mitigates risk of serious injury for these types of situations. 
The use of body-cams that link to a cloud type environment will allow both control room personnel, field 
supervisors and EHS personnel to view in real time the work that is being done on energized lines. This body-
cam would also have a person down feature for emergency crews that work without a second person. 
The body-cam would also allow a real time recording to be stored in the cloud environment for lessons 
learned and teachable moments. 
Con Edison has reduced the number of injuries to employees, but the Company still experiences  High Hazard 
Injuries.  Con Edison has implemented a number of safety programs to reduce these injuries, however, the 
Company continues to seek further reductions in injuries.  High Hazard Injuries are often life altering for the 
individual or individuals involved in the event.  These injuries include arc flash burns, gas ignition burns, 
fractures and other serious life altering injuries.  In many cases these individuals are not able to return to work 
or can no longer perform the tasks and duties that they were trained to perform.   
  
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
 
Risk 1 Name: Safety 
Risk 1 Description:  
Ability to use technology for real time discussions relating 
to safety, environmental, "just in time" training and 
technical issues.

Physically presence of the field supervisor or EHS SME required at site of event. 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Field crew making an error involving risk to safety or environment 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
 
Reduction in safety injury incidents, operating errors, “Rules We Live By” incidents, video and audio record 
Exhibit___(IT-3)

of a “close call”. Ability to dial up by the EHS SME to ensure 100% compliance

Project/Program Title: Obsolete Oracle GRC Software Replacement

24626913

Work Description: 
Current Oracle Governance, Risk Management, Compliance (GRC) on-premises software will 
be unsupported by Oracle as of 5/31/23. Additionally, GRC will lose functionality when the 
company moves to Oracle cloud-based services as the two applications are incompatible. The 
expected timeline for the Oracle cloud conversion is 2024, with the project anticipated to 
commence in 2023. Based on the aforementioned timeline, funding for implementation is 
needed in 2023. 
The objectives of implementing the GRC software replacement include: streamlining ERP 
Cloud role design for security and segregation of duties, automating the internal controls and 
compliance processes that ensure financial reporting integrity, and continuously monitoring 
for insider threats and policy violations.  
This will require the procurement of modules to cover the existing functionality of Oracle 
GRC which includes Transaction Controls Governor, Configuration Controls Governor and 
Applications Access Controls Governor.  Additionally a consultant will be required to gather 
requirements, design, implement, test, and deploy the software solution.   
Justification Summary: 
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 26 of 64


--- Page 410 ---
SOX is looking to replace Oracle GRC on-premises and procure a software to electronically 
support its segregation of duties analysis on the Company’s General Ledger (GL) platform 
(Oracle) and transaction monitoring across Consolidated Edison Company of New York and 
Orange and Rockland Utilities in the cloud platform, to be compatible with the Oracle ERP 
cloud implementation .  The software will ideally have the future capability of being integrated 
with other applications, such as the Treasury Management System, PowerPlan, ServiceNow, 
and our GL platform, in addition to providing access provisioning capability.    
 
The benefit realized from a SOX perspective will be a centralized internal control monitoring 
tool with automated prompting for resolution of issues identified.   
 
Recommendation: Leverage GRC Tool 
• Observations 
o SOX transactional controls are not systematically monitored in a tool. 
o SOX activities are reliant on key people and institutional knowledge to perform 
responsibilities 
o SOX documentation is manually prepared and updated . 
• Proposed Solution 
o Allow for continuous improvement opportunities across workstreams 
o Reduce the amount of manual labor in SOX activities 
o Increase visibility across internal stakeholders 
Recommendation: Automate Transaction Monitoring Process 
• Observations 
o There is a defined foundation for monitoring and reporting while looking for 
improvement opportunities 
o Few automation tools are being used, leading to processes that are manual and 
time-consuming 
o Current monitoring is more reactive than proactive in nature 
• Proposed solution 
o Begin adoption of continuous monitoring processes with an automation 
roadmap 
o Adopting automaton will encourage a more proactive risk management mindset 
throughout the enterprise 
 
• Benefits of GRC Tool 
o GRC Tool supports current SOX controls (segregation of duties analysis, 
transaction controls within Purchasing) 
o GRC Tool will drive automatic action and issue information sharing as required 
and designed. through the identification of access conflicts and transaction 
anomalies 
o Tool can be leveraged to automate additional SOX Controls in the future which 
are currently performed manually providing opportunity for cost savings  
Strategic Driver Alignment: Reducing and managing financial misstatement risk, strengthen

The purpose of the SOX organization is to provide guidance for and oversight of the 
continuing design, documentation, review, results of testing, and updating of internal controls 
over financial reporting for compliance with Section 404 and Section 302 of the Sarbanes-
Oxley Act of 2002 (SOX). The Company has the obligation to meet these regulatory 
requirements. The SOX program impacts the identification, assessment, mitigation, 
monitoring, and reporting of financial misstatement risks.  
 
This software solution will improve the Company’s ability to better mitigate/improve 
controllability for the risk of financial misstatement and adhere to regulatory requirements 
through continuous transaction monitoring and automated notifications of issues requiring 
resolution. For information regarding the benefits of the solution, please see above.

retirement.

Work Description: 
The Law Department is seeking to take a phased approach to the replacement of old and obsolete legal technology that 
is critical to the running of the Department. The Department is undergoing a significant transformation project and 
upgrading this vital technology project will provide the support that is critical to the successful implementation of 
various departmental transformation initiatives 
Phase 1: Enterprise Legal Management Implementation: 
Con Edison is seeking to implement a solution that is a “system of engagement” to help the Law Department provide 
better service while improving operational efficiency. Matter management and e-billing, though they make up a fraction 
of the legal department’s responsibilities, are critical pieces of this provision of services. Phase 1 starts with the 
implementation of cloud-based matter management and e-billing systems, most of which now come with built-in 
workflow capabilities, and sophisticated reporting and analytics systems to manage and track Law matters and projects. 
This necessarily includes the conversion of data from the existing obsolete systems to the new systems and the creation 
and recreation of interfaces to other systems. These system integrations are vital to achieve the necessary efficiencies in 
processes between Company, Department, and third-party systems including HR, Oracle (AP and AR), e-billing, the 
federal government, our document management system, document scanning processes, workflow automation systems 
and document assembly systems, to name a few.  
The new system will include native data analytic tools and the ability to create and track metrics for strategic decision-
making, resource management and accountability. Con Edison would issue an RFP for the products with the work 
beginning in 2023 and completing in 2025.  
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 32 of 64


--- Page 416 ---
 
 
Phase 2: Document Management Implementation:  
The implementation of a cloud-based document management system will provide a secure, centralized repository for 
documents, images and other media related to the business of the Law Department and will include the conversion of 
data from the existing out of date document management system to the new system. The new system will interface with 
Law’s enterprise legal management solutions, document scanning, and workflow automation systems and third-party 
applications like document assembly products. In addition, a cloud-based system offers a range of solutions for record 
management, email management, content searching, and SharePoint integration. Phase 2 would begin toward the end 
of Phase 1 with an RFP in 2025 and completing in 2026. 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
The Law Department is undergoing an organizational transformation to improve efficiency.  Updating the basic, 
obsolete, and out-of-date legal technologies in use by the Department is critical to the success of several of the 
transformation plan initiatives that commenced in January 2021 under the leadership of the General Counsel and the 
senior leadership team. The transformation plan involves a multi-year restructuring of the Law Department to achieve 
greater organizational efficiency. There are twelve specific competency models, based on the Corporate Legal 
Operations Consortium (CLOC) “Core 12” functional competencies, are in the final stages of refinement before 
presentation to the SLT. These models outline plans for Law Department reorganization, team realignment, process 
improvements, and a new service delivery model. Functions include firm/vendor management, eDiscovery, business 
intelligence, financial management, contract management, information governance, legal operations technology, and 
program management. As part of the transformation initiative, a new Litigation Center of Excellence has been created to 
provide standardized litigation services across multiple practice groups, serving as a model of efficiency and agility. 
The Law Department has formed roadmap plans and teams to implement these transformation initiatives, all of which 
rely heavily on legal technology. To achieve the objectives set forth in these initiative plans, it is imperative that the Law 
Department is enabled to embrace innovations in technology, thereby making strategic transformative changes. The 
exciting opportunity to use legal operations for increased operational and cost efficiencies, as well as driving value for 
the business, relies on an investment in technology. Most importantly, workflow automation tools and 
analytics/metrics are critical. 
The Law Department has identified two essential phases as critical to its short-term and long-term objectives: 
Phase 1: Replacement of End-of-Life Enterprise Legal Matter Management System: The matter management system is 
used to manage and track the work done in the various sections of the Law Department. The Law Department's existing 
matter management system. LawManager, does not meet current departmental and Company needs for several 
important reasons  LawManager lacks the capability to create and track metrics for strategic decision-making, resource 
management, and accountability.  Most importantly, the system is obsolete, having been sunset by the vendor in 2017. 
There are functional, technical, and security risks to continued reliance on outdated, obsolete software, which is no 
longer supported or updated to keep up with changing business requirements. The Cloud-based matter management 
system includes reporting, analytics and remote capabilities, all current legal industry standards. Unlike LawManager, 
current matter management systems also offer workflow automation and integration with other Law Department and 
Company applications (from Office 365 to e-billing systems). Transition to a new matter management system will 
increase productivity and efficiency by enabling collaboration and streamlining tasks.  
Reporting capabilities will finally provide the Law Department with tools to track metrics, analyze data, create reports, 
utilize dashboard, and do other types of analysis necessary for strategic planning and for measuring the value of its 
services. A robust matter management system would allow the Law Department to standardize matter intake, add 
approval workflows to its matters, and track and report on different custom attributes. Matters would be captured in 
detail for tracking purposes. The system would integrate with the Company’s accounts payable system so that we could 
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 33 of 64


--- Page 417 ---
 
track and analyze spend by practice area (log spend, enforce billing guidelines, perform spend analysis) and available 
opportunities to reduce costs. We could also explore alternative arrangements and discounts on outside counsel rates. 
Phase 2: Replacement of End-of-Life Document Management System:  The existing document management system, 
eDOCS OPENTEXT, has existed in some iteration within the Law Department for over 15 years. eDOCS is no longer 
considered a market leader in the industry. The Law Department’s current software, like LawManager, is outdated, 
does not integrate with other Company applications such as Office 365, and lacks remote functionality. The technology 
is three versions out of date and no longer meets the needs of the Department or the Company. The current system has 
limited functionality, and there are many features lacking in comparison to newer document management applications. 
As with LawManager, eDOCS presents technical and security concerns. The Law Department invests time and 
resources, along with IT, in maintenance and troubleshooting, from overseeing end-user problems to managing 
operational issues. Many Law Department staff do not utilize the document management system for work products due 
to its unreliability and slowness.  
 
The benefits of cloud-based systems are well known to this audience, and the Company has been moving towards 
cloud-based systems for a few years. Cloud-based systems are secure and cost-efficient. There are no capital expenses, 
data can be backed up regularly, and there is instant provisioning. We are seeking cloud computing solutions with 
optimized performance, security, and control for both phases of this project. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
Funding this request is critical to the Department's five-year and long-range plans. Gartner notes that developing a 
multiyear legal technology strategy that can evolve with changes in the corporate environment and advancements in the 
technology market is critical to success. (Gartner Insights – Legal & Compliance, “5 Legal Technology Trends Changing 
In-House Legal Departments,” Feb. 9, 2021) 
The Law Department's transformation plan is a forward-thinking long-range plan.  The Department is reorganizing to 
improve service delivery and optimize process improvements. As we move through transformation and beyond, it is 
critical that we have functional legal technologies.  These technologies allow for sophisticated insight into our work for 
service delivery, transparency in reporting to our internal and external stakeholders and predictive analytics that would 
enhance our strategic and tactical decision making.  Our current technologies are years out of date and insufficient to 
meet our needs.  New cloud-based technologies can evolve with the Department as it transforms, and these technologies 
are integral, critical support to the success of Law's various transformation initiatives. 
Law's current applications are on-premises and require substantial time and effort from Law and various groups in IT to 
manage daily.  Cloud applications allow complete and efficient access from any device and any location.  Law's matter 
management system, the life blood of its day-to-day operations, has been obsolete for four years.  The vendor has not 
sold or invested in the product since 2017.  The product does not meet our needs and its utility to the Department during 
a business continuity event, as demonstrated throughout the pandemic by our inability to readily make workflow and 
process changes in the system, is reduced and increases the severity of risk of significant loss.  We are seeking systems 
that improve our interface capabilities and include bi-directional exchange of information with, for example, the courts 
that enable us to more efficiently ensure that we do not miss deadlines, including deadlines for regulatory filings and 
court documents. 
We continue to invest significant amounts of time, dollars, and internal and external resources, to fix and change out-of-
date systems, just to keep up with basic functions.  Implementing innovative technology solutions requires an initial 
investment, but the internal IT and Law Department resources currently dedicated to this work can then focus their 
attention where they are otherwise needed.  Cloud-based solutions maximize availability and performance because 
maintenance and support, including regular software and security updates, are managed by the vendor with little to no 
IT involvement, saving the Company time and money. Moving these applications to the cloud will also save over 
$20k/year of IT maintenance of these on-premises applications. 
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 34 of 64


--- Page 418 ---
 
The newly created Litigation Center of Excellence, one of the products of our transformation initiatives, is now 
supporting litigating sections across the Department.  The ability to provide internal and external stakeholders, 
including regulators, the courts and insurance companies, with reports and analytics (predictive and otherwise) 
regarding the work of the Department is essential.  Providing data and information increases transparency, which 
increases trust and decreases the risk of eroding relationships.  More robust, advanced, and reliable tools will enable 
transparent collaboration with the exchange of detailed information that in turn allows for better business and strategic 
decision-making, improving relationships among all stakeholders. 
 
Risk 1: Records Management 
Risk 1 Description: The controllability of the Records 
Management risk is increased as all data and documents are 
subject to the Company's records retention policies.  Up-to-date 
systems allow for the appropriate classification of documents 
and data and thus allow for compliance with the policy. Over-
retention of records beyond records management policies and 
legal hold requirements can result in increased exposure to the 
Company and higher litigation costs.  This is a known issue that 
the Law Department is actively working to mitigate. 
Risk 2: Cybersecurity 
Risk 2 Description: Funding this project would decrease the 
Cybersecurity risk, as the risk of shutdown would be 
mitigated.  If the Company systems are compromised, the 
Cloud applications would still be available, and the Law 
Department could continue its critical work without 
interruption and without fear of missing regulatory or litigation 
deadlines.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
An alternative would be to fund only one of two phases now.  This alternative was rejected, as the systems in these 
phases are tightly integrated. Replacing and upgrading only one of the two obsolete systems will not provide the overall 
efficiency process envisioned in the transformation initiatives. This project should be implemented in a phased approach 
over time.  As noted above, the current matter management system is obsolete – so the alternative of not replacing the 
systems associated with that application is rejected.  The document management system uses old technology and is 
three versions out-of-date.  It does not meet today's needs for access via remote access or offer much of the Office 365 
integration and other functionality widely available in other document management systems.  A legal enterprise 
management system would be hobbled without a new document management system behind it, and vice versa.  The 
systems in these two phases are intricately linked.  As documents are scanned into the Department, they are associated 
with a matter in the matter management system, routed and filed in the document management system with the other 
documents associated with that matter.  The matter management system is updated with reference to the document that 
was filed.  When a new document is created it is saved in the document management system in a folder structure 
associated with the matter to which the document belongs.  One without the other decreases its respective utility.  This 
alternative is unacceptable if the Law Department is to continue to be a leader in legal operations. 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Risk 1: 
If Law is unable to move forward on its technology roadmap it will fall behind in its ability to properly defend and 
support the Company.  The inability to utilize up-to-date technology in conducting its business directly impacts the 
Department's ability to effectively manage its matters, budget, and resources.  The result will be a loss of productivity 
and efficiency in an organization that greatly values its high performance.  Data allows insight into business trends and 
assists in our partnerships with the organizations across the Company that we advise and represent.  Currently, there is 
no ability to effectively forecast budgets and analyze outside legal spend, though we continue to increase the use of 
outside counsel. There is a huge reliance on manual workflows, which can and should be replaced by automation and 
digitized processes. Resources are devoted to IT to maintain and troubleshoot outdated software and systems.  Law will 
continue to require assistance from multiple IT resources to address fixes and apply patches to on-premises systems in 
three environments (development, test, and production).  Client software deployments and updates will continue to 
require the IT Lab to create scripts that push the changes.  
 Risk 2: The lack of metrics and the inability to objectively quantify, analyze and report data on matter and resource 
management is detrimental to the overall functioning of the Department.  Benchmarking is critical to promoting 
efficiency, productivity, and value. The current matter management system is rich with data about where, why, how, 
and when the circumstances that give rise to litigation occur.  Enterprise legal management allows for matter 
management coupled with many other capabilities including analytics that allow mining of data for potential risk 
identification.  Our systems contain information on organizations we serve and what legal needs they have.  This data 
should be analyzed to provide insights and trends that Law and the Company can use for strategic decision-making.  We 
receive requests from the PSC and other external agents for reports and data that we are not able to satisfy efficiently due 
to the limitations of our systems.  New legal enterprise management systems would allow us to make forward-thinking 
strategic decisions based on data. 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
 
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 36 of 64


--- Page 420 ---
 
This project will increase the productivity of the department by providing the ability to create workflows between 
departments and strengthen relationships by providing the ability to provide factual detailed insights about the matters 
we handle for the organizations of the Company.  The matter management system is rich with data about where, why, 
how, and when circumstances occur which give rise to litigation.  It can also collect data relating to the transactions 
reviewed and negotiated by Law, as well as regulatory and environmental information.  This data should be analyzed to 
provide insights and trends which can be used for strategic decision-making by Law and the Company.  The systems 
together will improve communication among departments by enabling interfaces that do not currently exist for the 
exchange of information about Company structures, incidents and claims which impact the health and safety of our 
employees and the communities we serve.  It will also enhance existing interfaces and allow for increased collaboration 
with other departments to maximize the use of innovative Company automation tools.  Transitioning to cloud-based 
systems will reduce the time spent searching for or re-creating information.  It will also improve productivity and make 
content accessible to users at anytime and anywhere.  New matter management and document management systems 
can connect with document assembly systems that further enhance efficiency by taking data from one system and 
routing it to a variety of templates and forms.  Flexibility and mobility with better access to more complete, reliable 
information enables users to make critical decisions faster.  Cloud-based systems will provide greater integration with 
Office 365 tools and the ability to share documents securely on mobile devices and with other departments and external 
stakeholders to increase transparency, efficiency and reduce reliance on exchanging documents via email, FTPs or 
portable media.  This will enhance users' ability to comply with governmental regulations and internal company 
policies involving PII, cybersecurity and safeguarding company, customer, and employee information. 
Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup) 
1. Cost-benefit analysis (if required) 
 
A robust, capable enterprise legal management system includes, in part, matter management and electronic billing for 
outside counsel matters. Data analytics will enable Law to identify metrics and create dashboards to track compliance 
with billing guidelines, predict litigation budgets, reduce redundancies, share engagement data across the Department, 
and track the diversity of counsel assigned to our matters.  Transition to a cloud-based enterprise legal management and 
document management system will reduce ongoing costs associated with reliance on  IT resources, purchasing, and 
maintaining server space, power consumption, and the physical real estate footprint required to run in-house 
servers.  With the ability to access data and metrics, we can analyze and manage outside counsel by managing cost per 
hour and the cost of handling and resolving claims and cases, which will then provide better insight into settlement 
values and the right point of settlement.   
2. Major financial benefits 
 
The financial benefits are associated with mitigating risk and financial exposure to the Company, enhancing external 
relationships and strengthening Company processes. 
There are two areas where these benefits can be identified: reporting and business process improvements.  Law's ability 
to provide information and metrics to its constituents is paramount. The current level of need for reports far outpaces its 
ability to create them.  The effort necessary to create reports severely limits the number of reports we can produce.  New 
systems, with built in reporting and dashboard capabilities can provide rea- time data and will reduce the time spent 
creating reports by at least 50%. Law conducted an analysis and determined that it currently spends nearly 3,000 hours 
and $360,000 in labor annually in these two areas due to the intense manual nature of obtaining the required data and 
information.  For example, to create the annual reports for the Board of Directors and President, up to 20 hours of Vice 
President time and 20 hours of Section Manager time are utilized unnecessarily each year. In addition, many hours of 
attorney time are spent on bi-monthly reports for the General Counsel, plus additional versions of the report that are 
tailored for O&R and Construction.  This level of manual effort to obtain the basic or threshold business information 
necessary to report on is not an efficient use of anyone’s time.  Reducing this effort by 50% will save the Department 
$180,000 in labor cost annually that could be shifted to more productive endeavors.  
Automating and improving business processes in cloud systems is another area where substantial benefits can be 
found.  The business processes that are currently done manually in e-billing, template creation in an enterprise legal 
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 37 of 64


--- Page 421 ---
 
management and document management systems and eliminating most technical problems with on-premises matter 
and document management solutions would reduce time spent on those activities and result in labor savings of 65% per 
year for those processes.  Current process time for just these 3 business processes is 1,068 hours and $136,000 labor 
dollars per year.  New systems would cut the process time on these 3 by 690 hours, saving over $91,000 labor dollars 
annually in the Law Department alone.  The current on-premises systems require regular internal maintenance and 
support by Law Department employees, IT personnel and the vendor.  The maintenance and troubleshooting require 
daily communication and follow-up to identify and resolve problems.  There will still be a need for some level of IT 
support, but the time would be greatly reduced if the product were in the cloud.   As noted above, transition to the cloud 
promises flexibility, everything from saving time, money to improving agility and scalability.  As noted above there 
would also be savings of over $20k/year for IT maintenance of these on-premises applications. 
In the report and business process areas, we would anticipate cost reduction in the amount of $271,000 in the first year in 
known savings.  That reduction will allow us to turn those resources to work to expand our reporting capabilities and 
the number of organizations to whom we report.

5. Conclusion 
 
As noted above, the Law Department's transformation plan is a forward-thinking long-range plan.  The Department is 
being re-envisioned to accomplish the objectives of the multi-year transformation initiatives to right-size work and 
improve service delivery to the Company.  To ensure the success of the transformation and beyond, it is critical that the 
Law Department has access to adaptable, innovative, and agile technologies that allow for sophisticated insight into our 
work for service delivery, transparency in reporting to our internal and external stakeholders and predictive analytics 
that will enhance our strategic decision making.  New cloud-based technologies can elevate the Department, support 
sustainable best in class practices and ensure our continued leadership in legal operations.

Work Description: 
The Rate Case Enhancements Project is a project to continue to streamline, enhance, and add functionality to Rate 
Engineering’s Customer Usage System (CUS). CUS is a strategic data warehouse and analysis system that is used to 
centralize and summarize electric and gas data necessary for Rate Engineering to report on or develop various rate 
structures, and to analyze load research and develop load shapes. To be effective, CUS must be an integrated and 
complete snapshot sales reporting system.  
Over the last several years, Rate Engineering has worked to replace and integrate the data and functionality of four 
disparate and obsolete mainframe systems into the CUS. This integration has eliminated the need to manually query 
multiple systems and facilitate more thorough and timely rate case analyses. As we work on new components of the 
integration of the CUS, a need has surfaced for additional functional enhancements to support electric and gas demand 
analysis, rate design, and rate impact activities and to expand functionality to improve efficiency and decrease the need 
for manual processes.  
There is also need for enhancements, particularly to accommodate the growing population of customers with bills not 
calculated in CSS (manual or off-system billing). These populations of customers often have complex billing structures, 
or characteristics that require separate treatment outside of CSS. Expanding CUS’s linkage to the Off-System Billing 
platforms will address billing changes for growing populations of customers with no alternative bill impact reporting 
design or capability and, in so doing, enhance the Company’s ability to more efficiently develop bill impact analyses. 
Specifically, with the Rate Case Enhancements Program, the Company plans to:  
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 42 of 64


--- Page 426 ---
 
• 
Develop and implement system requirements associated with billing changes not included in original scope of 
the CUS integration (e.g., capacity tag billing, net metering or value stack options, standby billing, incentive rate 
designs, REV proceeding outcomes, reactive power billing, updates to reflect changes in rate structures and 
future rate cases) 
• 
Implement technology and software enhancements, including developing additional fields and derivations, and 
data mining for additional customer usage and interval data information available from other data collection 
and storage software 
• 
Obtain additional data storage capacity for customer billing and interval data 
• 
Implement further automation related to the creation and storage of load shapes in the CUS. These load shapes 
include New York Independent System Operator (NYISO) and market support activities, including wholesale 
energy reconciliation and retail supply pricing, and enhancements to the Company’s existing Load Shape 
library.  
Justification Summary: 
 
Rate Engineering continues to support the growing trend of evaluating and developing new rate structures that follow 
different models from existing rate structures.  Future rate impact programming will not only need to assess the effect of 
a change in existing rate structure but also to evaluate the effect of completely different rate forms.  Expanded 
functionality will be required to support other PSC-mandated activities as well.  For example, Rate Engineering must 
update load shapes used for energy settlement and market supply-pricing for customers without interval metering. 
Additionally, automated and streamlined access to current and historical billing and interval data is critical to respond 
to the needs and initiatives of various Company and PSC efforts including distribution analyses, energy efficiency, and 
electric vehicle initiatives.  Cross-functional training of Company staff on the use of available data storage and analytic 
tools will allow each individual user to focus their inquiries in a targeted way, allowing for improved automation and 
efficiency.

Work Description: 
Vertex, TaxWare and Sabrix (OneSource) are sales tax engines that make sales and 
use tax a seamless part of every transaction, connecting with our source system 
(Oracle). Vertex, TaxWare and Sabrix provides expertise, collaboration, training, and 
support needed throughout the sales and use tax process. The objective of this project 
is to add either Vertex, TaxWare or Sabrix as an add on to the Oracle ledger and 
purchasing system currently in place at Con Edison. With the addition of one the 
three sales tax software programs to the Oracle system, the process of calculating, 
collecting, and reporting Sales and Use Tax will improve, promoting the Company’s 
goal of data-driven decision making, operational excellence, and customer 
experience. 
The Sales Tax Engine has the following primary objectives: 
•
Implement a cloud-based solution that integrates with Oracle enterprise
resource planning (ERP)
•
Connect to Oracle’s financial, billing, and other systems through pre-built
and custom integrations
•
Calculate correct sales and use tax amounts automatically
•
Accuracy through automation
•
Reduction of compliance costs, potential penalties and interest, and errors
associated with over or under assessing sales and use tax.
•
Produce reports for high level data analytics analysis
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 48 of 64


--- Page 432 ---
2 
 
To meet these objectives, Tax requires software implementation support from 
additional software and tax consultants along with the software and support 
provided by the chosen vendor. This request includes staffing for the addition of 2-3 
programmers and management roles to assist in the implementation of the sales and 
use tax engine. Tax will need assistance from various departments throughout the 
company’s footprint including, but not limited to, Accounts Payable, Supply Chain 
Management, Information Technologies, Corporate Accounting and Oracle Support. 
To complete the project these roles will require competencies in project management, 
data science, business analysis, and application development and implementation.  
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
Since the company’s deployment of the Oracle enterprise resource planning (ERP) 
systems, over and under accruals of sales and use tax have significantly increased.  
The investment of a sales tax engine offers an opportunity for the company to reduce 
these accruals. Over and under accruals ultimately cost the company money in 
consultant costs as hired consultants take a percentage of the refunds received as part 
of the reverse audit process of the three-year audit cycle. Additionally, this prevents 
proper data analytics since costs of purchased items do not properly reflect the 
addition cost of sales tax.  
 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives,

approved refund, which has resulted in millions of dollars in contingency fees. 
 
A Tax Engine will implement various processes that will reduce Sales and Use tax over-accruals. By 
implementing a more efficient Tax Engine, reduced Sales and Use Tax refunds will reduce the Reverse 
Audit consultant’s contingency fees.

Work Description: 
Material handling-related soft tissue injuries are a significant contributor to the Company’s annual injuries. These 
ergonomics related injuries include cumulative trauma disease (CTD), musculoskeletal disorder (MSD) or damage to 
nerves, ligaments, tendons or muscles causing disabling injuries or pain and discomfort of various body parts such as 
back, neck, thoracic spine, wrist, shoulder, ankle, knee, hip, and upper/lower extremities. The basic event mechanism is 
overload of one or more body parts either through handling of an overweight load, or by handling an otherwise 
manageable weight in an awkward body posture. The former mechanism can be avoided through assessment of the 
load before handling, but the latter requires self-awareness on the part of the user. During work, such self-awareness 
may diminish, leading to increased potential for awkward body positions or postures. Wearable sensor and interface 
such as Kinetic REFLEX increase self-awareness by delivering feedback in the form of vibration alert upon detection of 
at-risk body positions or postures. Initially, the user will wear the device for up to a month to create a baseline. Once the 
baseline is established, the device will detect a high-risk posture and the worker will receive real time feedback in the 
form of vibration to identify and correct the positioning. The Company anticipates developing capability to equip and 
support approximately 500 employees. This technology adds an immediate and regular oversight mechanism for at risk 
behavior that might otherwise produce soft tissue injuries. The Company will aggregated and analyzed the data from 
this program. The project schedule initiates in early 2020, anticipating continued positive outcomes from a current R&D 
project.  
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 53 of 64


--- Page 437 ---
Justification Summary: 
 
This technology application adds an immediate and regular oversight mechanism to engage the target employees on at 
risk behavior that might otherwise produce soft tissue injuries.  
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
 
Existing supervisory oversight and peer to peer coaching are alternatives to this project.  However, these mechanisms 
provide only intermittent feedback for individual employees.  Sensor application provides means for constant data 
analysis, oversight/coaching, increasing the potential to quickly and sustainably change at-risk behaviors through 
constructive feedback and individualized training. 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Taking no action leaves the Company at risk for an ongoing trend in the referenced injury type, or a trend that improves 
slowly over time through existing means. 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
 
Primary benefit is injury prevention, with morale improvement also likely due to employee perception of technology as 
a direct personal benefit.

2. Major financial benefits

Recordable injuries and illnesses from 2017 to 2021.  Soft tissue injuries or ergonomics related injuries have resulted in 
152 recordable injuries in the past five years.

Technical Evaluation/ Analysis 
 
R&D has studied the application and viability of wearable sensors/interfaces for preventing injuries.  The Company 
deployed 26 Kinetic REFLEX devices as a STIPP pilot program on three workgroups for approximately 3 – 6 month 
period during November 2016 to February 2018.  Three work groups were selected (Construction Services at Van Nest 
Yard, Astoria Store Operations at Astoria Yard and Store Operations at East 16th Street Yard) for the pilot program 
based on their materials handling and other physically challenging activities. The preliminary data shows that at Van 
Nest Deployment (10 devices), the wearers on average performed 15 high-risk postures per day during the feedback 
phase, compared to 28 high-risk postures during baseline period, which is a 45% reduction in high-risk posture behavior. 
 Similarly, 77% reduction and 31% reduction in high-risk posture behavior was observed in the pilot programs at Astoria 
Yard Deployment (6 devices) and East 16th Street Yard Deployment (10 devices) respectively. 
  
Data generated to date has positively indicated potential to prevent injuries through detection of awkward body 
postures.

Work Description: 
Objectives: 
Con Edison is targeting a roll-out of a Supply Chain Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) program in the first quarter 
of 2023 to drive efficiencies and enhance its ability to identify, monitor, and manage the risks of doing business with 
third parties.  
Through this program, Con Edison will expand its current third-party risk assessment review to include additional risk 
categories including: business resiliency, fourth party management, fraud, geopolitical, human capital, physical 
security, compliance, reputational, and operational risks.  The program will also enhance the Company’s risk program 
by automating and aggregating all third party risk review information for ease of understanding and use. 
Assessments completed by third parties will be reviewed and evaluated by the Company’s new TPRM employees. If the 
Company identifies risks, it will develop a risk treatment plan that will be tracked, managed, and approved by the 
appropriate internal party (e.g. the contract end-user) as part of Con Edison’s third party selection management.   
During contract negotiations, the Company will also consider risk profile information to determine whether to negotiate 
special contract terms, including regarding onboarding.   
The enhancements that result from the TPRM program will also inform contract reassessment and monitoring cycles. In 
addition, the Company will establish more robust vendor performance reviews (scorecards) which will provide 
increased insight into third party vendor risk to the Company.    
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 58 of 64


--- Page 442 ---
 
In 2024, Supply Chain will partner with a consulting firm to assist with the expansion of the design, build, and 
deployment of a Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) program to all other third parties managed outside of Supply 
Chain managed spend including but not limited to Law and non-procured type relationships (e.g. regulators, 
consortiums) to continue to drive efficiencies as well as identify, monitor, and manage the risk(s) of doing business with 
all of the Company’s third parties. Additionally, the program expansion will look to address continued enhancements 
of its existing program through additional automation opportunities with the procure-to-pay processes. 
 
This proposal is to leverage its existing Oracle and RSA Archer platforms for CECONY and O&R (collectively the 
Company) to implement consistent and standardized processes of onboarding, assessing, monitoring, and managing 
the identified risk of its third parties. This implementation will involve the enhancement of four (4) TPRM Archer 
modules and build into the existing Issues Management solution leveraged by Compliance. Additionally, the solution 
will be integrated with the Vendor Portal for secure data sharing with third parties, third party risk monitoring tool(s), 
and linkages to payment and contract management systems. The integrations with internal tools include the Contractor 
Oversight System (COS), Discovery SAS, ServiceNow, Oracle’s payment and contract management solutions, and the 
Company’s big-data reporting tool(s) (e.g. Tableau, Power BI).  
Justification Summary: 
 
In February 2020, Con Edison hired a program manager to develop the business case and project manage its TPRM 
program.  The TPRM program charter was developed to meet the Company’s priority to provide a direct line of sight 
into risks of its third parties. The Company’s TPRM Steering Committee approved the charter in Q1 2020.  
In December 2020, Supply Chain onboarded KPMG LLP to partner in driving a, complex, cross-functional project with 
over 70 stakeholders from across the Company to design, build, and deploy a TPRM program. An investment into the 
Company’s existing on-premises Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform, RSA Archer, was selected as part 
of the Company’s strategic initiative to build functionality with IT partners already used by the company, rather than 
increasing our portfolio of software partners.  
 
The major elements of work for this project in 2022 include:  
(1) create a TPRM Oversight Committee and a single function within Supply Chain to oversee implementation and 
operation of program;  
(2) incorporate all 12 risk domains and applying TPRM processes consistently across all third parties; 
(3) adopt a risk-based methodology to assess and monitor third parties;  
(4) document a formal TPRM policy and procedure;  
(5) create training and awareness to drive change and facilitate adoption of program enhancements;  
(6) develop a single, dynamic due diligence (control-based) questionnaire that incorporates all applicable risk domains;  
(7) define a risk treatment process to track identified issues to closure;  
(8) assess third party risk at an engagement and third party level respectively to better identify and manage new 
potential risks;  
(9) implement technology that supports the end-to-end TPRM Framework and workflows, which includes:  
i. 
onboarding of third parties, procurement process/lifecycle, risk domain subject matter experts (e.g. 
EH&S, Law, Information Security), and business requestors throughout the enterprise  
ii. centralizing third party profile data to capture comprehensive risk profiles   
iii. embedded and traceable workflows (internally and externally with third parties) 
iv. real-time risk metrics and end user work queues for workflow management 
v. ease of QA reviews with embedded audit trails (internally and externally)  
vi. document repository

Outer years (2024-2026), will help the company mature its overall program maturity by extending beyond Supply Chain 
and making this an enterprise program (for CECONY and O&R). 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
This program will improve the Company’s ability to develop risk treatment plans.   
 
 
 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Alternative 1 description and reason for rejection 
An alternative to this project would be the development of standardized processes and instructions that could be 
followed by employees so that one method is used to manually record and track onboarding and templates can be 
developed and leveraged to consistently risk rate third parties in the existing non-electronic, decentralized, and 
duplicative manner currently used. This would not provide efficient or timely sharing of information, and continue the 
current practices disparate electronic inherent risk, due diligence assessments, and action tracking from the respective 
third party risk profiles.  
  
Alternative 2 description and reason for rejection 
Another alternative could be to build a home-grown solution that supports the TPRM framework instead of purchasing 
a system solution from a vendor.  Building a system is not an efficient solution in comparison with a fully functional 
vendor-provided system that remains dynamic and current with the latest technology and industry frameworks as 
competition drives system improvements and will be supported by a maintenance contract. 
  
Alternative 3 description and reason for rejection 
Another alternative is to select a TPRM solution by an alternative vendor.  From the Gartner report that rates existing 
platforms, RSA Archer is the preferred option due to its dynamic abilities to integrate and its ease of configuration to 
support this evolving landscape.  Additionally, it is already being used by other areas of the company. 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Risk 1 
By not proceeding with this project, the Company will not fully address internal audit findings, will continue to fall 
behind industry TPRM program maturity, and not be able to support the increasing Corporate Risks of Cyber and Fraud 
or the Organizational Risks of Third Party Risk Management, Supply Chain Disruption, or Emergency Preparedness & 
Response. The expanding risk landscape and an inability to identify and mitigate risks in real-time operational impacts, 
financial loss, regulatory exposure, public embarrassment could result in reputational damage to the Company.   
  
Exhibit___(IT-3)
Page 60 of 64


--- Page 444 ---
Risk 2 
By not proceeding with this project, the Company would continue to utilize current processes to manage third 
parties.  Current processes are not standardized, are manual in nature, decentralized, duplicative and do not support 
efficient information sharing across the Company thereby increasing exposure to risks that cannot be identified or 
managed in a timely fashion.  Thus, making it increasingly difficult for Supply Chain to address its departmental risk of 
Supply Chain Disruption and Third Party Risk Management.   
  
Risk 3 
By not proceeding with this project, this could lead to low employee morale and retention due to a lack of centralized 
technology that supports Supply Chain's ability to make faster and smarter decisions regarding third party selections 
from a risk evaluation perspective and its ability to support effectively managing risks as they arise.
