Work Description:  
  
Autodesk is t maker of Computer-Aided Design software. Company engineers and designers rely almost exclusively on 
these products for CAD work The CAD (Computer-Aided Design) Program requires periodic upgrades of software and 
hardware to keep up to date with current technology. Autodesk’s licensing schema follows a subscription format that 
entitles its clients to all future releases of their software for a determined period. The funding requested in the five-year 
capital plan includes the upgrade and replacement of wide format plotters, 3D scanners, CAD laptops, and various 
other hardware needed to fully leverage the capability of Autodesk’s collection of CAD software.  
Justification Summary: 
 
The CENG Management Administrative and IT Support section of Central Engineering Services Department is 
responsible for supporting over 200 CAD laptops/workstations used by designers and engineers throughout the 
company for CAD work. In 2019, Central Engineering completed an initiative that consolidated all Autodesk licenses 
under Con Edison. We must renew the contract with Autodesk to support our customers. Upgrading the Autodesk 
collection of products will increase the designers’ productivity, maintain Autodesk support of the software and 3D 
platform, and maintain file compatibility.   
 
Productivity improvements are expected to be achieved through the implementation of Autodesk’s Building 
Information Modeling (BIM) or 3D Design. In addition, upgrades provide for links to Excel spreadsheets with dynamic 
updates – making data extraction more powerful.  The new applications allow for smaller file sizes which conserve

Work Description: 
 
Central Operations uses over 250 battery banks for emergency DC power for the control, operation, and indication of 
critical assets. These batteries are currently maintained in accordance with Engineering specifications and NERC 
requirements when applicable. The required battery maintenance is time consuming and battery health data is only 
collected during maintenance activities. A battery monitoring R&D project completed in 2021 demonstrated that battery 
monitoring systems eliminate periodic maintenance requirements and real-time battery health data can be instrumental 
in avoiding failures of the DC system. This project will install battery monitoring systems on selected batteries along 
with a centralized monitoring software system that can be utilized to access and monitor battery condition data and 
generate automated alerts.  
Justification Summary: 
 
Installation of battery monitoring systems will lower O&M costs associated with time-based battery inspections and 
proactively identify degrading battery conditions thereby improving reliability of these critical assets.  In addition, 
condition monitoring systems meet all NERC requirements thereby eliminating the risk of non-compliance. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
This project will lower O&M costs, improve reliability, and lower the risk of regulatory non-compliance

Work Description: 
  
This project is to configure and create asset condition monitoring functions and asset health dashboards for Central 
Operation equipment utilizing the enterprise OSi PI software. Currently, condition monitoring and asset health is 
managed in 3rd party software products limited exclusively to a type of equipment or monitoring device and/or in 
Excel spreadsheets where information from multiple data sources is manually compiled. Due to these limitations, 
condition monitoring and asset health assessment can be improved. In addition, it is time-consuming to manage and 
update all the different tools being used. Condition monitoring and asset health assessments involve the compilation 
and analysis of data using a multitude of algorithms and calculations usually unique to the type of asset. This project 
will consolidate all the equipment health-related data for currently monitored assets into a centralized database (OSi PI) 
and then build all functionality (algorithms, calculations, alert set-points) needed to monitor equipment performance 
and health in the form of dashboards in OSi PI.. Once the project is complete, as new IoT devices are installed in the 
field, the data will be routed to this centralized platform and algorithms and displays updated accordingly.  
Justification Summary: 
 
Robust asset condition monitoring and health assessment is critical to safely, reliably, and cost effectively, manage our 
equipment.  Condition-based monitoring enables minimization of more costly time-based maintenance and ensures 
assets receive maintenance when they need maintenance before they fail.  Asset health enables better capital 
replacement planning and highlights potential programmatic maintenance and/or equipment performance 
deficiencies.  This system will provide information for making asset-related decisions.

Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
This project promotes the use of an enterprise software system to achieve Company goals of reducing the risk of 
reliability related events, the safety of Company personnel, and environmental events.  In addition, it would help lower 
operating and maintenance costs within Central Operations.

Risk of No Action:

is not sustainable to manage condition monitoring and asset health data as is currently done when we continue to add 
IoT devices in the field.    
 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
Improved safety, reliability, and environmental performance due to automation asset performance monitoring that 
enables intervention prior to catastrophic equipment failure.

Work Description: 
  
The Contingency Analysis Program (CAP) assists control center operators in making operating decisions during system 
contingencies. CAP consolidates data from multiple systems and implements decision algorithms which provide 
guidance to operators on next actions. The broad goals of this initiative are to: - Extract and combine vital information 
from different systems, such as General Electric’s Extensible Architecture for 21st Century (XA/21) - Integrate data 
across separate applications and provide this critical information to operators in a way that they can interpret and act 
upon quickly. Decision aid tools help operators analyze data from a multitude of systems quickly enough to implement 
corrective actions. - Provide this critical information to operators in a single, actionable view. In the early module of 
CAP, we integrated key elements from different critical attributes from over 40 applications into CAP, during the last 
few years we were focusing on the Network system contingency and how to reduce the Control Center SME processing 
time to address ongoing system challenges and coming system contingency. The ongoing challenge is the non-network 
system, OH and 4kv, where the design is less reliable and takes longer duration to restore. To reduce this impact, CAP 
needs to further extend to provide this analytical design to the non-network system, which are outline in module 7-17 
below. Modules 1-6 have previously been completed.  
Below are the high level modules of CAP to be developed between 2022 and 2025: 
Module Description  
Module 7 Integrate to 4kv load flow contingency analysis  
Module 8 Integrate to Auto-loop load flow contingency analysis  
Module 9 Include Underground loop system in CAP  
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 23 of 97


--- Page 471 ---
Module 10 Correlate multibank contingency with secondary status for operator awareness 
Module 11 Provide Seamless capability to run test cases from the main display for "what if" scenarios in NNW (similar 
to Manual Cap for NW)  
Module 12 Calculate and display now and next worst contingency for secondary cable overloads 
Module 13 Provide interface with HTV Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)  
Module 14 Provide capability/logic to trigger to run contingency on any combination of equipment and feeders (other 
than from feeder OA)  
Module 15 Incorporate automatic status update of overhead utilizing OMS and overhead switching 
Module 16 Incorporate Area Substation Over load  
Module 17 Decision Aid Action Engine    
Justification Summary: 
 
 
CAP is a decision aid for control center operators to help them analyze system contingencies. System contingency 
analysis and response by operators in our control centers is a labor-intensive process.  CAP presents operators with the 
most vital information on current system status and providing guidance on next actions. CAP works to address the 
following concerns: 
• 
What is the current abnormal state of the distribution system? 
 
• 
What is the current impact? 
• 
What is the impact and severity of the next event? 
• 
What are the best options for getting the system back to a normal state? 
Historically, operators had to gather information that is contained in over ten applications.  This is a laborious process 
and often each application typically requires a separate login with a user ID and password.  While this provides a 
picture of the current status, the resulting view is not dynamic and needs to be manually constructed after an event. 
We need to continue to enhance this tool with the improved capabilities to assist operators. 
 
 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
Risk 1 Network Shutdown 
Risk 1 Description:  
PSC Penalty and financial implication to the company

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
The main alternative to consolidating data from multiple systems and providing decision tools to operators, as 
implemented by CAP, is to continue manually accessing multiple data sources to piece together vital information. 
Contingency analysis requires an integrated view of the condition of the distribution system which CAP provides. 
CAP's ability to push vital system information to operators in the form of current conditions and subsequent scenarios is 
a beneficial feature for control center operations. 
 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Operator efficiency will be impacted without the further enhancements offered through the CAP initiatives. Control 
operators will have to rely on the current disparate group of applications to collect relevant information.  For example, to 
determine which customers are impacted in either high tension, multi-bank, or non-network systems, operators must 
combine SCADA information from numerous 4 kV auto loop systems by sorting through many pages of reports. 
  
 
 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
 
The Company has developed and implemented a display for operating personnel that provides an integrated view of 
network and/or load area system conditions.  The application allows the operators to navigate between the various 
applications as though they are all part of a single tailored application.  The application facilitates the processing of 
primary distribution feeders from outage to restoration, and analyzes the network or load area contingency for the 
“now" case and the “next worst" cases.  
The importance of having a complete and integrated knowledge of system conditions during contingencies is essential 
to successfully bringing the system back to normal status in a timely manner. The current process involves pulling out a 
feeder map, manually identifying the automatic transfer switches and high tension customers.  Targeting the auto loop 
and 4KV primary grid will complete the loop by providing operators with the ability to quickly analyze system 
contingencies and assess next  
 
Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup) 
1. Cost-benefit analysis (if required) 
 
 
2. Major financial benefits 
 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 25 of 97


--- Page 473 ---
 
A five minute reduction per outage corresponds to a 0.08 reduction in Customer Average Interruption Duration Index 
(CAIDI), equivalent to an average reduction of eight customer outage hours per 100 customers interrupted.   
Regarding customer cost savings, a study conducted by Berkley National Laboratory and sponsored by the US 
Department of Energy entitled Framework and Review of Customer Outage Costs, computes potential costs of power 
interruptions to U.S. electricity customers.  The report estimates outage costs at $8,200 per hour for large commercial 
customers, $1,200 per hour for small commercial customers and $3.00 per hour for residential customers.  Adjusted for 
inflation and locality, these costs are $13,722 per hour for large commercial customers, $2,008 per hour for small 
commercial customers and $5 per hour for residential customers. 
A reduction of five minutes per interruption due to CAP has the potential to save impacted electric customers 
approximately $10.6 million.    
The basis for the estimate is based on a study conducted by Berkley National Laboratory and sponsored by the US 
Department of Energy entitled Framework and Review of Customer Outage Costs as described in the Major financial benefits 
section of this document.

Work Description:   
The three year program described in this roadmap applies emerging technologies to enhance the 
customer experience, encourage self-service, increase Energy Services Representative productivity, 
reduce costly errors, and shorten case lifecycles.  These benefits would be achieved by predicting and 
delivering contextual and enabling information during appropriate stages of the case in the preferred 
communications channel to ESD customer and contractors.  In addition, critical information would be 
added to ESD cases to help ESD reps streamline case progression .  
 
This goal will require restructuring, capturing and delivering the data associated with our 
business processes  (Unified Data Structure).  New data models would be created to deliver customer 
and business intelligence to ESD and all other departments involved in the ESD case progression 
workflow.  Once these new data models are created and ESD is able to capture and access this data, the 
project team would improve workflows across the various Con Edison systems to leverage the new 
data in order to optimize business processes . The technology group plans to create a road map and 
phase these initiatives in over the next four years beginning in 2023, with various releases throughout 
that time.  
 
This business intelligence is not available to ESD and associated departments today due to inconsistent 
and insufficient data across multiple systems.  The current data structure prevents a shared 
understanding of customers, contractors, employees and cases – as well as external factors such as 
geographical location, etc. – to allow service teams across Con Edison to become better equipped to 
add value throughout the case lifecycle, especially with a projected growth in demand.  
 
The Unified Data Structure would consist of the following models: 
 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 29 of 97


--- Page 477 ---
2 
 
• 
Contractor Unified Model – Global model for collection, distribution, and management of 
contractor data along with data quality guidelines and stewardship responsibilities for 
handling contractor data.  Data on case history and past experience will provide information 
on contractors with repeated issues in the case life cycle. Examples: 
o 
Inspection failures 
o 
Missed appointments  
o 
Frequent case inquires  
o 
Late document uploads/changes   
• 
End- Customer Unified Model – Global model for collection, distribution, and management of 
customer data along with data quality guidelines and stewardship responsibilities for 
handling customer and contractor data.  Data includes case history, case types, experience, and 
risks to gain insight into customer behaviors and Con Edison’s relationship with end-
customers. For example, this functionality will track and identify when in the case life cycle 
customers are having issues/ submitting inquiries. This information will provide the 
opportunity to be proactive in the case life cycle by providing guidance and information before 
it is requested by the customer.  
• 
Case Unified Model – Global model for collection, distribution, and management of Energy 
Services case data to allow comprehensive case visibility between Con Edison groups such as 
ESD, Engineering, Meter and Test, Construction Planning, Field Services, etc. and external 
customers. This functionality would provide transparency between the internal groups 
displaying case information which is not currently visible across internal applications. Adding 
this functionality will create greater visibility for our reps to better communicate relevant case 
information directly to customers. This functionality would assist the various groups Energy 
Services collaborates with listed above by eliminating the current need and use of manually 
prepared and tracked spreadsheets. Therefore this initiative would derive benefits for these 
various departments other than ESD as well. These benefits are not calculated in our cost 
justification below.   
• 
Location (Place) Unified Model – Global model for collection, distribution, and management 
of location data to make accessible all useful information about a geographical area, as context 
for providing service in specific locations.  This will allow ESD to anticipate, avoid, and/or 
better respond to case-related decisions, customer inquiries, and location-oriented problems, 
and to predict and prepare for zone- and city-level conditions that could affect schedules and 
service. This functionality would also allow ESD to inform customers about situations that 
may impact or interfere with case progression, including design and construction. Examples: 
o 
Embargoes 
o 
Paving 
o 
Festivals 
 
• 
Failed Inspection Model – This model would enhance the data surrounding customer 
inspections. Data captured in this model would identify the root causes of failed inspections. 
Together with the case unified model, ESD would gain visibility to determine, for example, 
whether an inspection failed by field services was due to a customer or ESD error. The model 
could further reveal if  the failure was unique or repetitive. This enhancement would allow 
ESD to identify and assist our customers, contractors and representatives who have repeated 
failures. This would also allow ESD to employ a more proactive and targeted approach 
towards training our representatives.     
 
This new data platform would achieve the ability to “look backwards” to identify process breakdowns 
and to anticipate them in the future.  Once structured, the project team would establish “baseline 
scores” to identify and measure case lifecycle risks, errors, and pain points using the captured historic 
data.  The project team would apply this business intelligence to streamline future cases; for example, 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 30 of 97


--- Page 478 ---
3 
 
to identify high risk cases and potentially route them to more experience reps, and/or alert the rep that 
the case contains elements that have historically caused delays or additional, avoidable work.  
 
The technology enhancements include: 
• 
Enterprise Taxonomies (Controlled Vocabularies/Data Tagging/Metadata) to standardize 
data collection across platforms and applications. 
• 
AI and Machine Learning to better and more quickly recognize key events, behaviors, 
anomalies, and risks in case management.  From this we can refine processes to more 
accurately respond to case conditions and customer inquiries, and to provide continuous-
improvement opportunities for day-to-day case management and customer communications. 
This would allow the ability to take a proactive approach with our customers.  
• 
Intelligent Notifications – Identifying when and how much information to push to customers 
to reduce customer inquiries, questions, and confusion. By leverage predictive analytics, ESD 
could proactively communicate critical information to customers at the right moment based on 
historic risk analysis. 
• 
Task Automation and Self Service to improve day-to-day case management operations, by 
leveraging chat, Virtual Assistants, RPA (Robotic Process Automation), data input validation 
in both the customer portal (Project Center) and internal systems (e.g., CPMS), etc.   Examples:  
1. Reading data from documents:  identify and confirm that information supplied by the 
Customer/Contractor in the Application for Service meets ESD requirements, eliminating 
manual review.  
2. Integrating with NYC regulatory websites:  e.g., confirm validity of Electric or Gas 
Certificates supplied by the Customer/Contractor.  
3. Customer appointment /Field Services Technology: Self Scheduling, Auto 
notifications, Mapping functionality, Arrival time notification. Rep 
identification/authentication. 
3. Validating customer-submitted work description in the initial service request filing to 
identify missing or inaccurate information leading to case cancellation and resubmittal.

Justification Summary: 
The goal of this initiative is to decrease the overall case lifecycle, reduce case errors, increase customer 
satisfaction, and reduce ESD representative time required to progress the majority of ESD cases.  These 
benefits would be derived from data collection and analytics that would allow case management to be 
more proactive vs reactive and improving resource management.   
 
Examples of tangible business benefits include:  
 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 31 of 97


--- Page 479 ---
4 
 
Reduction in failed Inspections: Identifying recurring/predictable causes for failed inspections 
and identifying contractors that typically fail inspection.   
 
Through predictive analytics, the system would generate discreet, targeted information assets 
to communicate ways to avoid recurring failure points and suggest ways to ensure successful 
inspections.   
 
Intelligent Appointments:  Identifying recurring causes for inspection ‘no-shows’ and 
‘reschedules’ to .   
 
The goal is to reduce ‘no-shows’ and ‘reschedules’ by identifying communication gaps that 
cause the ‘no-show’/’reschedule’ and reuse the slots caused by  last minute changes for 
another inspection (for example, offering an earlier inspection time to customers in the same 
area when there is a cancellation).    
 
Case Progression Exception Handling:  Identifying average timeframes between critical case 
milestones.  
 
When the timeframe exceeds a specific threshold, the system notifies users to 
investigate  possible bottleneck or process delay  (e.g., pending engineering approval, 
construction scheduling, customer payment, document submission, etc.).  An example includes 
Gas Booster cases which typically have delays due to the large amount of required 
documentation not being completed properly.  At the macro level, a spike in exceptions can be 
analyzed for system or process improvement.    
 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
This project is aligned with the Corporate Digital Customer Experience (DCX) initiative to improve the 
external customer’s experience by streamlining and leveraging web technologies.   
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
Alternative 1 description and reason for rejection 
The goal of the program would be to leverage technology to streamline the end-to-end process for 
resolving electric and gas new business requests by using captured business intelligence, predictive 
analytics and decisioning capabilities to make corrective actions proactively and avoid pain 
points.  The same goal can be achieved by hiring database experts and paring them with ESD reps to 
perform frequent case reviews in order to manually identify case risk points.  The team would 
document common and chronic failure points and communicate case attributes leading to those failure 
points to ESD case owners.   The case owners would then monitor their cases to identify high risk cases 
and act appropriately to avoid case problems.   
 
With approximately 60,000 cases filed annually, this alternative would be costly, difficult to manage, 
and would produce lower quality output. 
 
Alternative 2 description and reason for rejection 
Some of these goals could conceivably be achieved through alternative methods including manual 
spreadsheet analysis and visual analytics technologies available today within ESD.  This method 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 32 of 97


--- Page 480 ---
5 
 
would require an investment in database and reporting human resources to manually obtain the 
business intelligence describe above and perform the analysis to identify corrective actions.   Given the 
large number of cases received annually, this would be an expensive and inefficient activity. Energy 
Services would require an investment in data analysis in order to achieve a limited result.  
 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
Risk 1 
Potential for errors with increased case volume and manual entries. 
 
Risk 2 
Declining customer satisfaction due to increasing expectations as customers get used to new customer 
services with other companies, especially as regards increased case transparency, increased customer 
self service functions, quicker problem resolution, and decreased case lifecycle.   
 
Risk 3 
Increasing Representative  and Clerical Staff headcount to maintain existing levels of service. 
 
Risk 4  
Energy Services would continue to rely on manual efforts from other departments that supply the 
limited information we currently get on customers cases.  
 
Non-Financial Benefits 
 
Implementation of the program described above is expected to provide substantial increases in customer 
satisfaction by avoiding case errors and decreasing case lifecycle time. 
  
Customers will have more transparency and self-service into case status, and control over case 
progression (Customer Empowerment).  
  
All technologies will be designed within the guidelines of IT and the DCX initiative.  This initiative 
would leverage and reuse any existing technologies already implemented in Con Edison.  
  
The design will allow scalability.  Any new implemented technology would scale from a department  
to an enterprise solution.

Work Description: 
  
The Distribution Equipment Management System (DEMS) is an IMS Transactional System written in an unsupported 
legacy code allowing for no improvements. This system is in a mainframe environment that is scheduled to be retired 
by 2024. Both the code and database have reached obsolescence. This obsolescence results in an increase in maintenance 
and leads to redundant manual data entry. Manual data entry in multiple systems contributes to human error and 
inaccurate inventory. This inaccuracy and obsolescence increase operational risk. DEMS has rigid functionality that can 
no longer be maintained with current IT resources. The broad user base struggles with navigation requiring command 
prompts and free-form character entry. Continual training and support requirements are extensive. The DEMS database 
was implemented in 1985 to provide a central database to track the cradle-to-grave life of the transformer. This includes 
receiving equipment in Oracle, manual data entry into DEMS, storeroom-to-storeroom transfers, issuance to field for 
installation, and removal from the field for consideration for retirement. The information managed in DEMS is vital to 
Distribution Engineering (DE), Regional Engineering, Electric Operations, Stores, EHS, Finance, and other groups for 
reporting, regulatory agencies, legal entities, taxing agencies, planning and financial forecasting. This solution is to 
enhance functionalities of Oracle EBS and the Maximo work management system, which will require some level of 
integration and process improvements. These enhancements would replace the legacy DEMS system and allow for 
better automation and data accuracy. A high-level schedule of the project is as follows: Design: 2021 Development/Test: 
2022 Q1 – 2022 Q3 Implementation: 2022 Q4 – 2023 Q3  
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 37 of 97


--- Page 485 ---
Justification Summary: 
 
The DEMS system's functions are managing inventory and usage of distribution equipment. The core justifications are 
enumerated below for the functionality described in the above table.  
1. The mainframe environment is scheduled to be retired by 2024. The functionality in the current DEMS system 
needs to be transferred or rebuilt prior to 2024 to continue to support business requirements.  
2. Integrations between systems will create synergies, streamline processes, eliminate duplicate data entry efforts 
and potential subsequent errors. For example, storerooms are heavily space-constrained, yet equipment must be 
on-hand for field installation and remain prepared for emergency events.  
3. The integration between systems would improve accuracy and enable common reporting. 
4. Transfer of functionality from DEMS into Maximo WMS will eliminate the duplicate data between those two 
systems and the need for a reconciliation process. This will substitute the reliance on various manual 
transactions including paper forms and spreadsheets between operations and Stores personnel. 
5. Using newer technologies enables the potential to add automation to the data collection process. 
This project will also improve inventory representation and tracking, both of which are is essential 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Replacement of DEMS with a new, standalone application with intuitive process and Inventory Management System 
solution that will potentially include automation to eliminate the redundancies and misalignment between physical 
inventory and what is entered into the database.  There should be an intuitive user interface to minimize input errors 
and provide real-time, and accurate inventory. 
This is a more extensive solution which would require more resources and funding. 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Risk 1 
DEMS is an IMS Transactional System written in an unsupported legacy code allowing for no improvements. Both the 
code and database have reached obsolescence. If data restore procedures fail, this could lead to catastrophic operational 
failure. 
Risk 2 
Existing process and systems require duplicate data entry which leads to human error.  
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
 
 Non-financial benefits include Consolidated Enterprise Platform support and maintenance, streamlined business

4. Basis for estimate 
 
Basis for Estimate 
To accomplish this first step of improving DEMS our team has met with CFS storekeepers, OST, IT and work 
management resources in order to gather various perspectives and thoughts on how to precisely go about this new 
interface approach.  
The team has recommended an enhancement of existing systems with a rough duration estimate of about 18-24 months 
for one developer. This can be cut down if additional developers are added. To estimate labor, we used $220K per FTE 
annually (this does not include contingency). In terms of hardware costs, there are no servers required to host these 
enhancements to existing systems. We used estimates per location and field-user to determine the automation costs. We 
used a bottom-up approach based on the configuration, integration, conversion, and reporting.

Work Description: 
  
The objective is to create a module that will allow Distribution Control Center Operators to learn remotely and practice 
in a simulated and controlled environment. The virtual environment will reconcile information from various sources 
including Reactance to Fault, substation relays, FMS Fault Correlation, and reports of manhole fires, and Contingency 
Analysis. The testing simulator needs to be continuously expanded to include lessons learned, projected spending for 
2020 was $60k, the process and procedure changes as well as new technology required to deploy remotely will cost 
$115k and expanding the training material, reporting and scoring capabilities will cost $125k in 2022 and $145k in 2023. 
The simulator results will be used to analyze an operator’s performance, and for qualification and requalification of new 
and experienced users. This tool has been ruled as a capital tool that will require new features not maintenance. The 
training material has been vetted with a Vendor, gamified and is available on the learning management system in the 
TLC without voice over. Voice over and sequencing will be completed in 2020. Scoring and evaluation will be 
implemented in 2021. 
Justification Summary: 
 
System Simulation significantly enhances operator understanding of system complexity. It provides a powerful 
addition augmenting the integrated the use of new and existing tools in processing events occurring on the system.  
This increases efficiency through the development of greater expertise using Human Performance Improvement (HPI) 
Program. skills.  Through the development of scoring criteria this application provides an objective mechanism that can 
determine skill levels before operators can be considered qualified.  With the increasing shortage of expertise through 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 43 of 97


--- Page 491 ---
 
retirement and the increasing complexity of our distribution design, it is critical that we have a new technological tool to 
stimulate learning and assess readiness for our operators. This application will be available in the Control Center on a 
designated computer for the purpose of making remote learning, moderating and scoring possible.  
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
Risk 1 Operator Errors 
Risk 1 Description:  
 
We decided to test the technical skills of feeder processing and 
ability to observe HPI traps rather than focus on the current 
applications used to conduct the process. The training model 
has a built-in mitigation plan, we will not encounter the need to 
revise the training model based on applications that have been 
retired. 
  
 
  
 
 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Hands on training - Desk-readiness is dependent on staff available to train, materials covered and individual 
training style.  Errors made by trainees will be made in real-time with a real-world impact.  Hands on 
training does not provide the equivalent conditioning of operators and an objective qualification process 
based on dynamic operator response.  Through the development of objective scoring criteria and training 
content, this application provides a training mechanism that can determine skill levels before operators can 
be considered qualified.   
Risk of No Action: 
. 
Maintaining operator expertise becomes increasingly challenging given changes in the technological 
landscape in each Control Center and the training requirements required to sustain the current business 
process. Control Centers require a singular enterprise application that can be used to reduce human error and 
is consistent with Electric Operations Human Performance Improvement (HPI) Program. If the risk of 
committing operating errors as a result of human error are not mitigated the consequences will be equipment 
damage, and injury to employees and the possibly the public.  
 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
• 
Targeting the auto loop and 4KV primary grid will provide operators with the ability to quickly analyze system 
contingencies respond more efficiently.  
• 
Increased reliability of service by quickly restoring a feeder back in service, ensuring customer satisfaction.

• 
A stronger relationship with field operators, Control room operators will have a more accurate representation of 
the customer outages related to the system contingency and the next worse event providing a safer working 
environment for field employees and the public.

Technical Evaluation/ Analysis

Work Description: 
  
The new software functionality includes computerized warnings and other indications that will contribute to timely 
processing and error free environment. New operator consoles will be added to support these new applications. The 
new 3G Feeder Networks will be modeled and integrated into the electronic order flow. The interfaces with Rapid 
Restore, FeederBoard and Visual Electronic Distribution Information System (VDIS) will be updated to reflect the 
changes in 3G field conditions and connections. 
Justification Summary: 
 
The District Operators coordinate and direct all switching operations on Con Edison's distribution and 
transmission systems using multiple computer systems including the energy management system (EMS), Feeder 
Management System (FMS), Transmission Operation Management System (TOMS), Telephone Line System (TLS), 
and other corporate systems such as Rapid Restore, DO (District Operators) Direct, Outage Scheduling System 
(OSS). Each of these systems has different user interface and operates on different vendor platforms and 
operating systems.

Work Description: 
  
This effort seeks to conduct a phase 0 assessment to determine the feasibility, scope, and estimate to migrate the Electric 
WMS (Work and Asset Management) system to the enterprise Maximo WMS platform. This is in keeping with IT’s 
strategy of moving to a “One Enterprise” Work and Asset Management solution for all of Con Edison’s business areas, 
to realize the full benefits of a true enterprise solution across all business areas. Electric WMS is now on the CGI ARMS 
platform and is experiencing severe limitations in the product line to meet the current and growing needs of the 
business. Significant investments have to be made to enhance the current functionalities of the Con Ed CGI ARMS 
implementation which can be met with Maximo out of the box capability. Maximo has been successfully implemented 
and has been in use in several business areas at Con Ed for many years: Central Operations, Steam, and Transmission 
Ops. In 2021 the platform was upgraded and the Controlled Enterprise license, which had some limitations in terms of 
the number of Maximo products licensed and the business areas covered, was re-negotiated to a true enterprise model 
which gives Con Edison and its affiliates use of any/all modules within the Maximo work and asset management suite 
of products on a subscription basis. A roadmap has been established to migrate over 45 disparate legacy WMS systems 
over the next decade. The Steam Job Tracking System migration to Maximo is now underway and Constructions WMS 
will be migrated starting the fourth quarter of 2021. With this unrestricted use of the product line and total user base 
coverage, Electric Operation can now access and use all of Maximo’s Work and Asset Mgt modules under the current 
enterprise license. 
The current Electric WMS system manages and tracks all work done by Electric Operations including: 
• 
Emergency repairs 
• 
Maintenance and inspection 
• 
New construction and customer connections 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 53 of 97


--- Page 501 ---
• 
System performance/reliability programs  
 
This phase 0 assessment will encompass all major categories of work and asset management currently tracked in CGI 
ARMs, understand the limitations of the existing solution to meet the current and future needs of the business, and fill 
in the gaps. It will look at a cross section of, but not limited to:  
• 
Work Initiation – initiate work from various sources  
• 
Design and Estimating - The use of Compatible Units (CU) to define the labor, material and associated 
accounting  
• 
Prerequisite and Materials Management – Prerequisites, such as parking data, is asset part of an embargo area, 
is a permit required to work on the asset or any special equipment needed, are set up for the work prior to the 
clerical effort required for dispatch. The materials are defined in the compatible units (CU’s) of work to be 
performed  
• 
Scheduling - The scheduling process starts with planning and forecasting the work, then scheduling. 
• 
Dispatching and Resource Management – Dispatching is an extension of the scheduling process where the work 
is dispatched to field forces and resources around this are managed. Mobile, Work Closure and Time Reporting  
Justification Summary: 
. 
In  keeping with IT's strategy of establishing a true “one enterprise” WMS platform for all operating areas, all legacy 
WMS systems are roadmapped to be migrated to the Maximo Platform including Electric WMS. In addition, potential 
risks associated with limitations in CGI’s capabilities to continue meeting Electric Operations’ changing needs with their 
ARM suite will be mitigated. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
 
Risk 1 Name: None 
Risk 1 Description:  
 
 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Do not migrate to Maximo but keep the limited WMS Logica implementation. This is not in keeping IT's strategy for 
establishing a state of the art enterprise Work and Asset Mgt solution for all of Con Edison which fully meets/exceeds 
the current and growing needs of the business. 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Electric WMS has work management capability limitations. The product line cannot support the growing needs of the 
business.  
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
• 
Increased efficiency and customer satisfaction 
• 
Improved workflows and streamlined business processes 
• 
Enhanced business capabilities in areas of asset life-cycle management and asset performance management.

5. Conclusion 
 
The current system's platform vendor, CGI, is not investing in their technology roadmap and do not have a vision for

(e.g.,  Powerbuilder) 
In addition, ARM WMS for Electric is functionally limited and may not meet the current and growing needs of the 
business. Migrating to a "One Enterprise" WMS system will bring new and greater efficiencies, consolidated platform 
and system support, and the ability for the business to leverage new and innovative functionalities to meet its current 
and future needs.

Work Description: 
  
The Electronic Feeder Sign On (FSO) system has been developed by IT using the business case, scope and detailed user 
requirements developed by the Edison Project with all operating regions to interface with Rapid Restore to allow 
qualified employees to sign on to feeders effectively and safely, this will reduce the phone call traffic to the Control 
Centers and accelerate the current "call in" sign on process. The FSO application interfaces with the existing Rapid 
Restore application.  Initial development work done by our corporate IT were three Sign On modules incorporated into 
this application: Crews signing on to perform spearing/clantech & cutting, pulling, and splicing of cable.  
The application requires continued operational improvements. Therefore, the project calls for the implementation of 
other modules.  
 
We are requesting additional funding to cover the following work:  
• 
Addition of Transformer Replacement scope of work  
• 
Addition of Local Grounds scope of work to move this type of work from paper tracking to digital 
 
 
These additional modules will provide the operational benefit and add value to the existing product and platform in 
which Electric Operations and IT have already invested.

Justification Summary: 
 
The FSO system allows crews to electronically sign-on to feeders and to reduce the sign-on/sign off traffic at the Feeder 
Control Desk in the regional control centers.  This technology builds in a sequence of safety checks and balances to 
electronically verify the critical element of signing on to work locations via a more efficient process then the current 
manual system.  Supervisors, Cable Mechanics, Distribution Splicers and Feeder Control Representatives (FCRs) 
significantly benefit when signing on to a feeder electronically.  In addition to the efficiency, the electronic process has 
built in electronic hard matches for safety precautions through the use of standardized templates with a variety of 
confirmation and verification functionalities. By allowing our field personnel to sign on more basic work through the 
use of FSO, it will allow the FCRs to focus on more complex jobs. FSO will streamline the process by improving our 
schedule attainment by eliminating delays and improve on safety as a result of the checks and balances built into the 
system through hard matches. 
 
Technological obsolescence is another driver for this project.  This upgrade will include new servers, database servers, 
and changes needed to run with the latest browser.   From a business perspective, if the current system stops 
functioning, all field crew work would have to use pen and paper to keep logs.  This will lead to increased paperwork 
and make it more difficult for mangers to keep track of the history of daily tasks going on at each work location.  In 
addition, there is a greater likelihood that paper instructions could be misinterpreted which will put our employees and 
equipment at risk. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation)

FCR or field crew to update the current location details if a crew wants to issue a verbal scope of work change 
after electronically signing on.  ~2022-2023 
 
  
3. Attach the layout for a job to the location in the Crew Management module in FSO. The layout provides 
additional technical details and verification to eliminate operating incidents and enforce operating practice.  
~2023 
 
   
4. Further integration with other Company application such as GIS, WMS (Work Management System) for work

Human Performance Tool.  ~2025

Work Description: 
  
The objective of this program is to develop and deploy a series of Grid Modernization Analytics (GMA) use cases to 
convert operational data into actionable operations intelligence using advanced analytics and best in class technology. 
GMA uses Con Edison’s Enterprise Data Analytics Platform (EDAP), which is managed and maintained by the 
Company’s Analytics Center of Excellence (ACE). ACE oversees the prioritization and governance standards needed for 
successful implementation of Grid Modernization Analytics use cases. 
 
The Grid Modernization Analytics program began with discovery and the initial prioritization of use cases in May 2020 
and is scheduled to be in service by the end of 2025. The project utilizes the Agile project management methodology, 
with developers, data engineers, and data scientists from ACE working with product owners from Electric Operations 
(i.e., Distribution Engineering) to align on priorities and deliver value. To date, the Grid Modernization Analytics team 
has implemented several use cases to improve processes and create efficiencies for the business. These efforts have 
included the development and implementation of use cases to identify efficiencies in open main design and work 
prioritization process, machine-learning-driven identification of potential open neutral conditions, and automation of 
data validation aiding in SAIFI/CAIDI reporting. 
 
The program will deliver more advanced analytics use cases, leveraging the data integrated from previous phases. 
Work will continue to develop a comprehensive data layer to build a holistic view of distribution assets and related use 
cases to improve visibility, as well as work on higher-value, higher-effort use cases to enable asset health analytics. Use 
cases for the program have been scoped across a variety of business domains, including, but not limited to, safety, work 
prioritization, transformer health, outage management, power quality, and cable systems.  
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 64 of 97


--- Page 512 ---
 
For each use case, the Company will procure the additional storage or computer capacity necessary to store the 
additional data that is integrated and run the algorithms to perform the analysis. 
 
The Company will use a standardized prioritization framework to evaluate use cases and guide decisions on how to 
apply the program budget. The prioritization framework accounts for key value and complexity attributes of the use 
case, such as financial value, impacts to reliability and safety, customer experience impact, as well as analytic and data 
complexity (i.e., availability and quality), use case maturity, process change requirements, and organizational impacts, 
among others. 
Justification Summary: 
. 
Advanced data analytics is an essential tool to leverage data from additional sensors and communications technology 
delivered through other Grid Innovation and Distributed System Platform (“DSP”) investments.  Machine learning and 
artificial intelligence offer the ability to process the increasing volume of data being produced at the grid edge. These 
advanced capabilities are existing functionalities of EDAP that Con Edison has already implemented as part of the AMI 
rollout and in earlier phases of the Gird Modernization Analytics program.  EDAP, as a cloud-based big data platform, 
is well-suited to scale and add data as required for additional, more-advanced GMA use cases. 
As additional data sources are modeled and integrated into EDAP, the Company realizes economies of scale and 
synergies through reduced incremental costs for each future use case that can leverage the same data sources. For 
instance, many of the use cases under the GMA program leverage customer or usage data that is already modeled on 
EDAP with no additional data integration work required.  The same will be true of future use cases that will leverage 
the additional data that will be integrated as part of this program.  
As demonstrated throughout this whitepaper, the Grid Modernization Analytics program also has various financial and 
non-financial benefits. Financial benefits of the program include improved capital asset planning and operational 
savings. In additional to these financial benefits, the execution of GMA use cases will increase public and employee 
safety, mitigate operational risks, improve grid reliability, increase customer satisfaction, enable a unified view of 
distribution electric assets, and enhance regulatory compliance. 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
The Grid Modernization Analytics program will help the Company improve grid reliability by converting operational 
data into actionable intelligence through advanced analytics. The insights derived from such analytics will help the 
Company improve capital asset planning and achieve operational savings. Furthermore, the program will increase 
regulatory compliance, reduce risks, and improve employee and public safety through programs driven by analytic 
insights. 
As an example of the benefits described above, an early use case executed as part of the GMA program uses machine 
learning to identify open neutral conditions, which present safety risks to the public and have associated costs to the 
Company. The earlier identification of such conditions, enabled through this program, reduces such safety risks as well 
as the risk of incurring increased costs.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives: 
 
Alternative 1 description and reason for rejection 
An alternative to leveraging the enterprise analytics platform to model data and analyze business problems is to 
develop analytic applications in individual business areas.  Failure to use an enterprise analytics platform could result in 
non-IT supported application development by individual departments that provide very limited scope and may not use 
the appropriate resources, data, and technology. These departmental projects consume capital funds, create new “silos" 
of data, may have redundant data and functionality, and ultimately require additional support personnel for 
administrative and maintenance activities.  Furthermore, if the data is not integrated to the enterprise analytics platform, 
it cannot enable future use cases for and correlation of that data, forgoing the network benefits of the platform. 
 
Risk of No Action: 
 
Risk 1 
Not building advanced analytics capabilities to support Grid Modernization would prevent the Company from 
optimizing rules to run the business more efficiently and expand the visibility of engineers and operators. This would 
restrict the Company to using the existing toolset which will not keep pace with the rapid expansion of grid edge data. 
The Company would continue to manage by business rules and programmatic replacements and would not fully utilize 
the other advanced sensing and communications assets it is deploying. 
Risk 2 
If the Company does not continue to pursue Grid Modernization analytics use cases it will forgo the benefits associated 
with their execution. Without the implementation of these analytics use cases, the Company risks missing out on benefits 
associated with their implementation, including, but not limited to, increased public and employee safety and improved 
reliability.  
 
Non-financial Benefits: 
 
The implementation of Grid Modernization Analytics use cases on EDAP offers additional non-financial benefits, 
including: 
• 
Increased safety—Grid Modernization Analytics use cases increase public and employee safety by analyzing 
grid and operational data to develop analytic insights and identify potential safety conditions that can be more 
quickly addressed. 
• 
Risk reduction—By making use of additional grid edge data, the Company anticipates that it will be able to 
reduce public safety events and better maintain its equipment, resulting in improved safety and enhanced 
reliability for its customers. 
• 
Improved customer experience—The reduction of public safety events and improved reliability will lead to 
increased customer satisfaction. 
• 
Regulatory compliance–The work management and asset maintenance enhancements will provide efficiencies 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 66 of 97


--- Page 514 ---
in maintaining regulatory PSC compliance. 
• 
Improved workflows/communication among departments—Rather than implementing siloed solutions and 
programmatic replacements, the implementation of grid and operational data analytics on an enterprise 
platform allows for synergies and information/insight sharing across departments.   
 
Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup) 
1. Cost-benefit analysis (if required) 
 
The Grid Modernization Analytics program has demonstrated financial and non-financial benefits. GMA provides 
financial benefits through improved capital asset planning and operational savings generated by automation and 
increased efficiencies. Each use case under the umbrella program has unique financial and non-financial benefits. For 
example: 
• 
Identifying Protected Streets use case—Automatically flags work being done on streets with protected status, 
which allows for the delay of low priority work to create operational savings from reduced paving costs. 
• 
Automating the Identification of Open Neutrals—Automatically the identifies of open neutral conditions. This 
led to the optimization of personnel resources through process automation; mitigated fire and shock risks, which 
decreases the likelihood of associated legal expenditure and oversight costs; and improved power quality. 
Furthermore, the network effects present from using an enterprise solution lessens the costs associated with 
development work for the program as this work will also enable future analytics initiatives at lower costs. 
 
2. Major financial benefits 
 
As illustrated above, major financial benefits associated with the GMA program include improved capital asset planning 
and operational savings associated with back-office labor optimization, automation of processes, and increased 
efficiencies. Such operational efficiencies (e.g., back-office labor optimization, process automation, etc.), enabled by 
analytic insights derived from Grid Modernization use cases, will generate costs savings and avoidances. 
 
 
3. Total Cost ($000) 
 
The total cost of the Grid Modernization Analytics program for 2022-2025 is approximately $20.64 million. Of this total, 
approximately $19.59 million accounts for capital expenditure, while the remaining approximately $1.05M represents 
ongoing O&M maintenance. 
 
Consistent with the detailed funding breakdown below, planned capital expenditure, without contingency, is 
approximately $1.65M 2022, followed by roughly $4.48M each in the rate years 2023, 2024, and 2025. In addition to this 
capital funding, additional O&M maintenance ($150,000 in 2022 and $225,000 in 2023-2025) is required for the program 
annually. 
4. Basis for estimate 
 
As of May 2021, the Grid Modernization Analytics program has identified a total of 44 use cases, eight of which have 
minimum viable products (MVPs) delivered, leaving 37 remaining use cases in the backlog. Use cases are classified 
based on complexity into a “Low," “Medium," or “High" complexity group per the table below. Based on executed GMA 
use cases, we can estimate the average time required to deliver an MVP for each complexity group:

Based on its size and complexity, it would be infeasible to execute the backlog at current workforce capacity. To deliver 
these use cases during the rate years 2023-2025, the labor and contract resources available will be increased in order to 
handle the volume of work anticipated for the GMA project.  
The estimate provided in this whitepaper increases the available developer, data engineer, and data scientist resources 
by 150%.  The majority of the increase falls in Labor and the associated Capital Overheads, with the remaining increase 
in Contract Services.  Transitioning the work from largely Contract Services to largely Labor will establish a more 
sustainable model – using Company employees vs. external contractors will both provide increased value in terms of 
hourly rate and ensure more consistent resourcing across the duration of the project and different use cases.   
This resourcing strategy will increase the benefits retained by the Company through increased knowledge retention and 
allow for the completion of the GMA program within the specified timeline. 
 
5. Conclusion 
 
There are significant financial and non-financial benefits to be gained through the continued implementation of the Grid 
Modernization Analytics program. Early use cases have demonstrated the potential for success of the program. GMA 
increases public and employee safety, increases grid reliability, enhances regulatory compliance, improves capital asset 
planning, and provides operational savings for the business groups leveraging the tool. These benefits justify the 
continued implementation of Grid Modernization Analytics use cases.

Project Relationships (if applicable) 
 
The Grid Modernization data analytics use cases are dependent on several other investments to source, transfer, store, 
model, and analyze data. Smart sensors and transformers with PTO sensors collect additional operational data from the 
field to analyze. Communications infrastructure is required to transmit the data back to receive systems for processing.  
Distribution Engineering is currently undergoing a related effort with the “Emerging IT Projects Initiative for Enhanced 
Distribution System Analysis." This program is meant to improve Distribution Engineering systems and applications; 
data from several of these systems will ultimately be used for analytics under the GMA program. Under the Emerging IT 
Projects Initiative, Distribution Engineering is looking to enhance the Outage Management System and the PVL 
application. These are just two examples of systems from which Grid Modernization Analytics is currently or plans to 
leverage data for analytics.  
In addition, several use cases in the Grid Modernization Analytics backlog are dependent upon the replacement of the 
Distribution Equipment Management System (DEMS). This is an IMS Transaction System in a mainframe environment 
that provides information on electric assets. Use cases in which historical asset data is required, such as the development 
of asset health scores, will require data from the new system that will replace DEMS.

Work Description: 
  
Substation Operations is planning to enhance the Rapid Restore system for operating orders and work permits issued 
on the electrical system by System Operations personnel to interface with Augmented Reality tablet application. The 
significant improvements that could be realized by building a new communication interfaces that will allow the District 
Operator to utilize the current Rapid Restore system to create the Work Order and to the Augmented Reality tablet 
application. The Rapid Restore application, with a new data interface supporting XML or similar will send and receive 
data from the Augmented Reality tablet application. This will allow the District Operator to add indirectly any items via 
the Content Management system to the Work Order and send the Work Order to the Station Operators and also receive 
any orders manually entered by the Substation Operator or supporting staff.  
Justification Summary: 
 
The opportunity exists to significantly reduce the likelihood of equipment switching errors by leveraging commercially 
available technology integrated with our operating orders and rapid restore systems.  The proposed project will help 
ensure with validation that Operators are at the right equipment when performing switching moves.  Operating errors 
result in unplanned disturbances on the transmission system as well as pose a safety threat to personnel.   
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation) 
This project leverages commercially available technology and integrates with existing Con Edison software platforms 
resulting a significant reduction in the likelihood of equipment switching errors.  This reduces the risk of personnel 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 72 of 97


--- Page 520 ---
injury, system disturbance, and costly equipment damage.

Work Description: 
  
Presently, Energy Management uses nMarket, which is an electricity nomination and scheduling system. It provides functionality to 
manage a participant’s transactions, public settlements, and invoices with the Independent Market Operator, Independent System 
Operator or Regional Transmission Organization. These functions typically represent in excess of billion dollars in transactions 
annually, but can be much higher depending on the market price of energy. Originally a Ventyx product, nMarket was once the 
industry leading software for ISO communications. However, after multiple acquisitions and corporate restructuring the product is 
no longer the focus of the parent company and is failing to keep in step with the needs of a rapidly changing energy marketplace. At 
the same time, Energy Managements needs are growing, and a product which can support the bidding of grid scale batteries and 
other distributed energy resources is needed in the near term for proper implementation of regulatory mandated programs, which the 
current system is not capable to address. These developments will add complexity to Electricity Supply's Physical Wholesale 
business requirements, creating the need to replace the existing nMarket System. The CEBs have already transitioned away from 
nMarket due to similar concerns with the product’s inability to keep up with up with changing market rules and the transition to 
renewable energy.  They have implemented Adapt 2 in its place. Adapt 2 is the premier ISO bid-to-bill platform for all North 
American ISO markets enabled with AI and Big Data technologies. The core components of Adapt 2 include Market Link, Front 
Office, Back Office and Plant Portal with over 2,500 market participants. 
This project is looking to replace the nMarket System and utilize an alternative software solution (i.e., Adapt 2) to support 
Electricity Supply’s Physical Wholesale business requirements, which consists of the following:  
• 
Electricity purchasing, scheduling and invoicing  
• 
Using and monetize electric storage assets in ISO energy, capacity and ancillary markets. 
• 
Regulatory and SOX compliance  
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 77 of 97


--- Page 525 ---
• 
Interfacing with other internal systems  
• 
Implementing the NYS PSC Reforming the Energy Vision (REV) Imitative  
Justification Summary: 
 
The implementation of REV expands the participation of DERs (especially electric storage) in the wholesale energy 
markets as well as extend the electricity markets down to the network and distribution levels. This will add complexity 
to Electricity Supply's Physical Wholesale business requirements, creating the need to upgrade or replace the existing 
nMarket System. The NYISO requirements for the operating parameters for a storage asset differ than that of a 
generator (i.e., new parameters, such as state of charge). nMarket is not configured for these new parameters. Without a 
replacement for nMarket, manual entry of operating parameters will be required.  
This project will help Con Edison: 
• 
Improve Energy Management processing of over $1 billion in wholesale electricity supply transactions, which 
requires state-of-the-art software to assist in managing the energy portfolio. 
• 
Interact with NYISO with more complex granularity than currently available. 
• 
Keep up with any regulatory changes which could impact how we do business. 
• 
Increase efficiencies by making data and results available in a standardized format that can be used to generate 
reports automatically for internal use, settlements, and regulatory reporting 
• 
Decrease the possibility for errors by automating processes as appropriate and interfacing with other internal 
systems on a corporate and organizational level 
• 
Maintain strict SOX controls and audit capabilities 
• 
This current system interfaces with an in-house system, ePortfolio,  NYISO – MIS, Con Edison's Pricing 
Database System (PDS), and once implemented, Energy Management's Data Analytics Tool, and the Enterprise 
Data Analytics Platform .

schedulers are given access

the company's customers.  The application maintains security 
over users and reduces the risk that fraudulent activities occur. 
Risk 3 Inaccurate record keeping and counterparty data Risk 3 Description:  
This application records our scheduling of electricity.  It 
provides the basis of reconciliation and verification of the 
electricity we purchase. 
Risk 4  Full recovery of all fuel costs 
Risk 4 Description:  
As the scheduling program for electricity, any inaccuracies in 
recording or reconciling of our purchases will limit our ability 
to fully recover fuel costs.

Work Description: 
  
This project will address upgrades to the Operations Management Systems (OMS) computer systems and provides for 
expansion of these systems to better support the needs of the operators and field services. This work will also support 
infrastructure needed for replication of systems at the Alternate Energy Control Center (AECC) for disaster 
recoverability. This project will include the replacement of the current replication system used by the Feeder 
Management System (FMS) with Virtual Machine platforms in order to improve the reliability and disaster 
recoverability of FMS. The new Virtual environment will upgrade the OMS computer systems with new servers, storage 
units and virtual infrastructure software to facilitate the operation of multiple virtual machines on fewer physical 
servers. Complete duplication of the production database functionality will be built in parallel with the current 
production database, allowing a cutover with a minimal system outage. The new architecture will build local and 
remote duplication into every aspect of the OMS, thus creating fault tolerant dual redundant systems.  
Justification Summary: 
 
This project is needed to maintain OMS computer system hardware and operating systems current with 
industry levels in order to maintain high system performance, better reliable systems and databases, strong 
cybersecurity posture and dual redundant, fully independent backup systems at the AECC.

Project/Program Title:  CECONY REV/DER/EEDM Forecasting Tool 
Project/Program Manager: Berna Falay Ok 
Project/Program Number (Level 1): 25546223 
Status:  ☒ Initiation  ☐ Planning  ☐ Execution  ☐ On-going  ☐  ☐ Other: ___________

Work Description: 
In 2020, McKinsey designed, built, and deployed the Con Edison Distributed Energy Resource (DER) 
forecasting application, containing forecasting modules for storage and for electrification of heat. They 
also developed the theoretical approach to the electric vehicle forecasting module. The application was 
used live in the Con Edison winter peak forecast this fall.  
 
With this project, the Company is looking to continue its engagement with McKinsey to enhance the 
analytics and tools used to forecast four more electric load modifiers that are undergoing significant 
changes in the coming years. The modules covered in this proposal are: 
• 
Electric Vehicles (“EV”); 
• 
Combined Heat and Power Distributed Generation installations (“DG/CHP”); 
• 
Solar photovoltaic installations (“PV”).  
 
The application will cover the 20-year electric forecasts for EV, DG/CHP, and PV; and will be 
performed for Con Edison’s electric service territory, specifying the DER effects on: 
• 
Electric System Annual Delivered Volume; 
• 
Electric System Annual Billable Demand; 
• 
Peak load at Electric System Summer and Winter Peak Hours; 
• 
Peak load at Electric System Summer and Winter Network and Radial Feeder Independent 
Peak Hours. 
 
Justification Summary: 
The uncertainty of the energy landscape has increased with its evolving complexity. This application 
software will reduce this uncertainty and provide a higher level of confidence in the summer peak 
demand, winter peak demand, and annual delivered volume forecasts for Con Edison electric. Such 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 88 of 97


--- Page 536 ---
2 
 
forecasts are essential for reliability planning, capital planning, budget management and bill impact 
modeling, and rate design. 
 
McKinsey has developed versions of this application software for two of the DERs in Con Edison.  The 
Company currently is using this application software to develop Electric System Peak, Network/Load 
Area Peak, and Delivered Volume Forecasts.  
 
This application software provides a higher-level of confidence due to its stock and flow approach 
through gaging the potential/universe of several load modifiers and maintaining the best available 
data while the framework and mechanics of achieving a future carbon neutral economy evolves.  
 
This application software will allow for the management of the aforementioned load modifiers, in 
order to avoid overlap through balancing of their potential, and so that there is reasonability in the 
stock and flow of each load modifier. 
 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
This project is in response to the ever-evolving energy market, dynamic policy, innovative 
configurations, renewables, and advancing the Company’s commitment to a clean energy future. This 
tool looks to effectively reduce demand and manage energy and predict where loads will go under 
policy measures such as PV, EE, and Electrification, which are policy driven to mitigate climate change 
and promote decarbonization. 
 
The Company’s Long Range Plans, from Strategic Planning, will rely heavily on the outputs of this tool 
and will apply them to the sensitivities assigned. This tool predicts how electric peak demand and 
volume will evolve in an already uncertain and risky energy landscape.  
 
Supporting the project is in alignment with the Company’s goals to provide safe and reliable services 
to the local community and to support NYS CLCPA and NYC LL97 goals. 
 
Lastly, this tool will be used to reduce Energy Management’s organizational risk called Inaccurate 
Demand Forecast Related to Electric, Gas, or Steam. 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
Alternative description and reason for rejection 
 
The alternative would be to continue to perform manual and independent forecasts for DG/CHP, PV, 
and EV. Such forecasts are not balanced against one another to the level that the new software 
application performs, and the forecasts are not organized and fed from updated data sources and stock 
and flow. 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
The primary risk associated with not completing this project is that the uncertainty in Energy 
Management’s forecasts will increase under evolving policy and electric load modifiers that are 
undergoing significant changes in the coming years. Forecast error can lead to diminished reliability, 
Exhibit___(IT-4)
Page 89 of 97


--- Page 537 ---
3 
 
higher supply costs, and increased O&M. Lastly, not developing this tool could increase the likelihood 
and severity of Energy Management’s organizational risk called Inaccurate Demand Forecast Related 
to Electric, Gas, or Steam. 
 
Non-Financial Benefits 
 
This project will improve the Company’s ability to predict electric peak demand and volume, comply 
with regulatory requirements, improve supply plans, improve energy scheduling, and improve the 
efficiency of the overall forecasting process. Additionally, this project further demonstrates the 
Company’s commitment to improve its predicting and planning capabilities to support a clean energy 
future for its customers, regulators, and stakeholders. 
 
Summary of Financial Benefits and Costs (attach backup) 
1. Cost-benefit analysis (if required) 
N/A 
 
2. Major financial benefits 
 
This project will indirectly result in financial benefits for the customer.  This tool is likely to improve 
forecast accuracy by an estimated 10% (2% for organization, 2% for balancing across load modifiers, 
3% for improved algorithm, and 3% for improved data streams). Such improvements could lead to: 
 
• 
For reduction in an over-forecast - Avoid supply costs, having to purchase the next 
incremental MW, as well as avoid load relief at certain substations. 
• 
For reduction in an under-forecast - Avoid last-minute, surprise day-ahead supply costs, 
which are higher than planning in advance, unforeseen outages/load shedding, and enhanced 
ability to comply with electric performance metrics. 
 
3. Total cost 
 
The estimate for this capital project is $2.7 million.  
 
4. Basis for estimate 
 
This estimate was prepared in partnership with an external consultant and using historic corporate 
estimates.  
 
The estimated work required includes the following: 
• 
60% user interface, middleware, and back-end model integration (including testing); 
• 
30% core algorithm development (including some due diligence on existing forecasting 
methods and processes through interviews and documentation assessment for PV and 
DG/CHP, plus user testing); 
• 
5% methodology and process development, mainly focused on PV module; and 
• 
5% user training. 
 
 
5. Conclusion 
 
The Con Edison REV/DER Forecasting Tool must be developed in order to continue to increase the 
accuracy and granularity of load modifier forecasts, to facilitate more prudent planning and support 
the achievement of NYC LL97 and NYS CLCPA goals.
