Work Description:  
 
Presently, Energy Management is pursuing a capital effort to replace the current Integrated Gas Supply (IGS) 
system with FIS Gas Transaction System (GTS), which is planned to be deployed in 2022. This system acts as the 
operational and accounting system of record, used by gas supply to record and schedule deliveries of natural gas 
purchases to the Companies’ service territory. In addition, it identifies, assembles, analyzes and reports the 
organization’s transactions for accrual purposes, accounts for the related assets and liabilities and allocates the 
various costs of natural gas purchases to the various end uses. 
 
From 2025 -2027, Energy Management plans to upgrade and enhance the system. Major outputs of this effort 
include: 
• 
Upgrading the FIS GTS application to a newer version, resulting in the consolidation of the product two 
versions /clients installed: Aligne 3 (A3) - locally saved version and Aligne 5 (A5) – web-based version, 
into one single upgraded version. The upgraded version consolidates the following screens, features, and 
functionality: Master Contract Management, Static / Reference data entry and configs (locations, IAs, 
Data Mapping and Pricing formula), Variable Commodity Rates, Exercising Call Options (deals), 
Capacity Releases entry (manual and loader), GDO and EDI Inbound data retrieval and processing 
(Actualization), Actualization Marketers (measurements), Inventory Management - balancing and 
adjustments entry, Valuation Process (cost allocation), Power generators Cashout Settlement 
• 
Implementing enhanced and/or new application features and capabilities to eliminate in-system 
workarounds: workflow sequence and data entry; full utilization of the planning and mobile capabilities. 
Examples include: 
o 
Screen and process consolidation for scheduling and invoicing functions 
o 
Full implementation of the data reporting, graphs, and analytics feature  
o 
Extension of FIS GTS Loader functionality to include other manually intense tasks such as 
Contract Demand Rates and Fuel and variable rates entries/ updates (in bulk) 
Exhibit___(IT-6)
Page 8 of 24


--- Page 596 ---
2 
 
o 
New planning feature / functionality to look ahead and simulate/plow various scenarios for 
portfolio Optimization. This will entail Integration of the FIS GTS various modules to the 
planning for the exchange of data 
o 
Implement No Notice functionality to automate the manual process of entering rankings, 
thresholds, allocations, and daily results for the agreed upon daily imbalances with the pipeline 
as part of the system balancing for the CE and ORU service territory 
o 
Enhancement of the EDI interface to include non-EDI pipelines  
o 
Notification information postings, restrictions, and pipeline conditions through EDI or through 
integration with S&P 
o 
Integration of the FIS GTS and the FUELS standalone module for the exchange of data 
• 
Enhance existing tools / interfaces to automate applicable business activities  
• 
Modernization of FIS GTS Application to the Cloud  
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
The FIS GTS system is scheduled to go-live in 2022 with the goal of consolidating every facet of the gas lifecycle 
to a single product and to integrate with Gas Daily Operations (GDO) system, Interstate Pipelines Electronic 
Bullets and Boards (EBBs), PDS, the ICE trading platform and Oracle AP/AR. While this project is realizing 
many of its planned benefits, the incorporation of many other business processes and work streams into the FIS 
GTS system has presented challenges and are likely not be realized. For example, automation and/or streamlining 
of the middle and back-office tasks/activities were not fully realized and the need for additional product 
development for some features is necessary. The latest version of the FIS GTS product has the necessary 
enhanced features and functionality in response to some of these recognized constraints and limitations identified 
in the previous versions (e.g., Power Plant module). Implementing these along with full expansion of the of the 
enhanced data reporting, graphs, and analytics tool, will allow the Company to fully realize the benefits of FIS 
GTS.   
 
Upgrading FIS GTS to a newest version will require the current application to migrate to the cloud. Modernizing 
this software platform will enable users to access all functionality and perform all activities using the web-based 
interface version of the application (A5), resulting in increased accessibility, faster system response and 
application performance, and increase in productive time as they will no longer need to log into two system to 
perform their daily activities. Additionally, this is in alignment with our business continuity plan and will help 
alleviate the substantial effort to support and maintain two versions of the product. The gas industry is changing 
rapidly and migration to the cloud provides increased flexibility and the ability to innovate faster while 
simplifying IT. Similarly, the workforce is changing and expects their interactions with systems to be intuitive 
and similar to their consumer experience.  
 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
 
This project will help sustain or improve the current risk assessment and the likelihood and 
controllability of the following Energy Management department risks: 
 
• 
Inability to Transact with Counterparties – FIS GTS enables recording and transfer of 
information with counter parties. It also helps maintain adequate pipeline capacity that 
enables the Company to access a broad spectrum of suppliers in different geographic locations 
• 
Full Recovery of All Fuel Costs – FIS GTS helps accurately record and reconcile gas supply and 
pipeline transactions to recover costs. 
• 
Inaccurate Record Keeping and Counterparty Data – The proposed project enhancements help 
mitigate the reliance on manual data input, processing, and reporting.

2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
The alternative to this project is to not update the system which would mean not addressing the 
inefficiencies and limitations of the current system. 
 
 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
The risk of no action would be the inability to provide a flexible gas transaction processing platform to 
meet the growing needs of our gas customers, regulators, and stakeholders. Additional risks include:   
 
• 
Current A3 version is not user friendly or intuitive, increasing time required to perform 
workarounds  
• 
Older FIS GTS versions may no longer be supported by FIS 
• 
Maintaining and patching 2 client versions 
• 
In case of hardware equipment failure, operations and back office may be unable to perform 
essential functions in the A3 version  
 
 
 
 
Non-Financial Benefits 
 
General benefits include simplified vendor support, efficient management of energy portfolio, reduced 
errors, and enhanced reports (internal & external), improved user experience, reduced training 
complexity, improved security, improved workflows and data integration / consistency among 
departments, and improved data visibility and traceably across groups and business areas and data 
analytics.  
 
New features such as screen and process consolidation, a planning tool, and no-notice agreements 
functionality can help improve and facilitate automation of business processes. Planning for the 
purchase of gas is currently done in spreadsheets outside the system, using inputs and data from the 
system. No notice functionality will streamline and automate parts of the manual process of entering 
rankings, thresholds, allocations, and daily results for the agreed upon daily imbalances with the 
pipeline as part of the system balancing for the CE and ORU service territory. Incorporating these 
functions into FIS GTS would eliminate the need to transfer data to spreadsheets daily, reduce errors 
leveraging the granularity and visibility of the data to optimize planning and overall operations.  
 
Other manually intense tasks such as Contract Demand Rates and Fuel and variable rates entries/ updates, will be 
streamlined by expanding and leveraging tools such as Loaders (in bulk). In the same way, the original project 
successfully sought the implementation of the functionality to enable the scheduling group to use the FIS GTS to 
send the nominations directly to the EBBs and receive post nomination cycle quantities through EDI for the 4 
Exhibit___(IT-6)

major pipelines. This eliminated the need for the double entry of the nominations in both the system of record and 
the EBBs. This not only resulted in time savings and operational efficiencies, but in a reduction in human errors.  
This new project is seeking to expand that functionality to include the additional non-EDI pipelines and storage 
facilities to maximize the benefits and will also pursue to include informational postings about pipeline 
operational conditions from the EBBs through EDI or integration with S&P.

2. Major financial benefits 
The financial benefits of this project are increased productivity, enhanced functionality, and continued 
ability to support regulatory requirements. 
 
3. Total cost 
  
The total cost of this project is estimated to be $6.9 million. 
 
4. Basis for estimate 
The high-level estimate to complete this project is approximately 36 months. The estimate is based on the 
complexity of the FIS GTS system and expected work related to the existing interfaces with Gas Daily 
Operations (GDO) system, the Interstate Pipelines Electronic Bullets and Boards (EBBs), PDS, the 
InterContinental Exchange (ICE) trading platform and Oracle AP/AR system. Given the complexity of the system 
we expect to engage a system integrator, internal resources, and an increase in the number of contractors required 
to successfully complete the project. 
 
5. Conclusion 
 
The original FIS GTS system initial implementation was the cornerstone and foundation for the consolidation of 
systems covering multiple commodities to reduce maintenance costs and increase efficiency (Application 
Rationalization and Portfolio Optimization). The system facilitates the automatic integration of data and centralized 
data analytics resulting in more effective risk mitigation strategies, increased transparency, more effective trending 
and analytics. 
The expansion of the solution, proposed version upgrade and eventual migration to the cloud, should allow IT to 
eventually reduce the internal support needed for FIS GTS.  Maintenance costs have increased with the FIS 
annual fee, but we expect costs and efficiencies to be realized as subsequent projects incorporate other 
commodities such as oil, financial instruments and electricity onto a single platform and eliminating the separate 
systems currently in place.

Work Description: 
  
Work Description: The current SmartApp system is used to record and monitor field work for gas operations. The 
objective of this project is to migrate and enhance applications from the vendor supported SmartApps platform to a 
mobile platform using approved technology. Some of the use cases include: A form to enter Distribution and 
Transmission Hold Point records A checklist form for Gas Personnel in the field to fill out to make sure they are 
adhering to job specifications. App to post pdf of bill for third party billing to be reviewed by Con Edison for approving 
pay. App to post pdf of weekly billing containing daily hours for third party inspectors. Information such as OT and ST 
pay is included in the pdf. Application used by third party inspectors to include their sketches, fuses included, layout, 
work order forms and joiner qualifications for a job. App to enter gas valves for specific jobs in the field. App to identify 
issues in the field and propose solutions that should be sent to Gas Engineering. App to document potential defects on 
tools used by mechanics so that purchasing can be made aware of this as well. App to propose changes surrounding the 
scope of work that is sent to Gas Engineering for review. App for opening ticket and paving order created.  
Justification Summary: 
 
The apps are operationally required by Gas Operations to adhere to the job specifications and to ensure that the third 
party inspectors capture fuses, layout, work order forms and joiner qualifications for a job. The information 
documented in this app will be used for third party billing to be reviewed by coned before approving payment. 
In addition the app will help identify issues in the field and propose solutions that should be sent to Gas Engineering

Project/Program Title: Utilizing AMI Data for Interruptible Gas Marketer Forecasting and Retail 
Choice Information System ("RCIS”) Migration 
Project/Program Manager: May Cheng and 
Heidi Cinquegrana 
Project/Program Number (Level 1): 21569647

Work Description: 
 
The Transportation Customer Information System (TCIS) is a software used by marketers to 
communicate gas operational information with Con Edison. TCIS has many functions, including the 
ability to communicate gas scheduling information, control access security, generate reports, post 
messages to the internet, store rates, create invoices and vouchers, and track enrollments/de-
enrollments. There have been recent capital projects enhancements to TCIS, which include the 
completion of the TCIS rewrite project and changes to the daily and monthly interruptible marketer 
programs. In 2021, TCIS was enhanced to include the implementation of capacity release, 
implementation of rebill adjustments, and include a display of AMI meter reading data.  
 
This project proposes to enhance TCIS’ capability to leverage AMI data to improve forecasting 
accuracy.  
 
The project should be able to address the following  firm  and interruptible marketer forecast 
requirements: 
• 
Obtain and store AMI data for firm transportation customers in TCIS  
• 
Update the Estimated Load Following report from monthly billing data to AMI data 
• 
Test the integrity of the heat factor and baseload calculation with the new AMI data 
• 
Modify the existing user interface to reflect the forecast 
 
• 
Modify the Estimated Load Following report to use AMI data, in place of monthly billing historical 
data.  
• 
Modify the forecast methodology to reflect the use of AMI data.  
 
Exhibit___(IT-6)
Page 20 of 24


--- Page 608 ---
2 
 
The work will also include the migration of Energy Management functionality from RCIS to TCIS. The 
functionality includes:  
• 
Daily Delivery Service (DDS) Invoicing 
• 
DDS administrative reports 
• 
DDS rates 
• 
Gas ESCO editable fields 
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
MI data will allow the Company to utilize daily information for daily forecasts, improving accuracy. 
The largest variations of forecast compared to actual exist in the shoulder months where citygate 
allocations are the lowest. Providing a more accurate forecast, especially during the shoulder months, 
would decrease the amounts to the citygates, decrease the true up at the end of the month, and 
decrease the imbalance on the system. The financial implications vary by season and market 
conditions. However, the program’s goal is to decrease the cashout because it causes a difference 
between the cost spent to provide the gas and the revenue the Company receives for the gas. 
 
Additionally, DPS Staff and marketers have frequently requested the forecasts to be updated with AMI 
data.  
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
 
This project helps to achieve the Company’s goals by refining its forecasting methodology. The project 
would impact the forecasted usage of transportation customers, which comprises approximately 50% 
of all gas customer load. The implementation of AMI allows for a more granular view of data, which 
allows the Company to improve its forecasts. This would result in more accurate delivery amounts by 
marketers on behalf of their customers and reduce the amount of cashouts. Cashouts have the potential 
to impact all gas customers due to price differentials.  
 
 
 
2. Supplemental Information 
 
Alternatives 
 
Alternative 1 description and reason for rejection 
The alternative would be to continue existing processes without incorporating AMI data into the 
forecasting process. However, this is not recommended as the PSC and marketers have suggested 
changes.   
 
 
 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
Risk 1 
There is a risk that cashout volumes could increase to high levels, resulting in marketers potentially 
filing complaints with the PSC. 
Exhibit___(IT-6)
Page 21 of 24


--- Page 609 ---
3 
 
 
Risk 2 
Marketer deliveries may vary widely from actual consumption, which increases difficulty in 
operations to balance the daily load requirement.  
 
Risk 3 
The Company has been asked by Staff to utilize AMI data in its forecasting methodology. If this is not 
addressed in a timely manner, then this may result in poor relationships with our regulators, 
customers, and other key stakeholders. 
 
 
Non-Financial Benefits 
 
 
This project can improve the experience and satisfaction of marketers who routinely ask questions 
about the existing forecast. Lastly, this could keep customer costs as close to actual spend as possible 
by reducing the volume of marketer cashouts.  
 
The successful migration of the functionality from RCIS to TCIS would result in the retirement of the 
RCIS application. TCIS is better optimized for performance because it is built on newer technology. 
The migration of RCIS functionality to TCIS includes benefits for both IT and Business users, in 
streamlining the number of support applications, and providing a better user experience with TCIS.

3. Total cost 
 
The total capital cost for this project is $1,080k and includes the following:  
 
• 
Hiring a vendor to design, develop, and deploy the software enhancements 
• 
Energy Management and IT employee labor to support this project 
 
Post-project O&M is related to labor to maintain the system (e.g., security scans, triage any defects, 
interface monitoring, service pack deployments, etc.). 
 
4. Basis for estimate 
 
The cost estimate is based on historical expenditures of several contracted software developers and 
discussions with a contracted business analyst and company employees.  
 
 
5. Conclusion 
 
The benefits of this project, as defined above, are pivotal to continue to meet the increasing 
expectations of the Company’s stakeholders (e.g., regulators, customers, etc.) and to improve the 
accuracy and effectiveness of its forecasting capabilities.

Work Description: 
• 
  
With Electric Operations discontinuing use of Bentley Passport products, the Bentley 5013 application license has become cost 
prohibitive for Gas Operations to continue its use. As a result, Gas Operations is partnering with IT to implement a mobile electronic 
drawing tool (EDT) as replacement for the Bentley 5013 solution, to support leaks and other field drawing needs. 
 
In addition to offering all the required Con Edison drawing functionalities provided by the Bentley 5013 solution, EDT will provide 
a device agnostic and user-friendly drawing interface. Leveraging modern technologies and development tools, EDT will be easily 
integrated with other applications such as WMS ARM, and extendable for future Gas Operation drawing needs such as replacing 
SmartApps. 
 
In 2022, implementing the EDT solution, will include but not limited to the following high-level activities: 
• 
Complete development of mobile drawing tool 
• 
Convert existing leak drawings into new EDT format 
• 
Integrate mobile drawing tool with Gas ARM 
• 
Conduct testing (system and user acceptance) of the solution 
• 
Train work force in the use of the new tool 
• 
Deploy solution to Gas Operations by end of Q3 2022 
 
Once deployed, ongoing maintenance support is needed as well. 
Exhibit___(IT-8)
Page 13 of 51


--- Page 625 ---
 
Justification Summary: 
 
Gas Operations’ Emergency Resource Center (GERC) field users leverage an existing vendor software package (Bentley 
5013) to create field sketches for leak migration/tracing.  As the Con Edision eGIS capital project is on-going, and 
eventually replacing the Bentley software suite functionality, the licensing model for the software has become cost 
prohibitive.  The Gas Operations department would be the sole user of this platform, and be required to bear the full 
licensing cost burden, which is estimated at $1.4M annually. An evaluation was performed on the current O&R ELDT 
(Electronic Drawing Tool) software application, as an option for use by CECONY Gas Operations.  With modifications 
along with enhancements to make the tool a native mobile application, the ELDT tool will be implemented in 
CECONY.   
This product is a “home grown” software package.   
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, Risk Mitigation)

Environment.  Gas Distribution Event 
Risk 1 Description:  
Requirement is to provide this level of capability in the new 
software system, to minimize safety risks as a result of incorrect 
tracking of Gas Leak events.  This is a PSC requirement for gas 
leak management

Work Description: 
 
The company relies on innovative ways to keep its network infrastructure operating 
seamlessly with the assistance of various telecommunication, data networks and data centers. 
This program allows for security and support for all networks and major capital programs, projects, 
and initiatives that are implemented under the capital programs for CCTN, Grid Modernization, 
Corporate Data Center Improvements and XM8 critical radio systems.  
 
Technology solutions are purchased through capital investments which include negotiated 
maintenance and warranty periods.  Once that period has expired, the contract becomes an 
expense to the Company, in addition newer solutions may only offer a SaaS model.  During 
the following five years, operating and maintenance costs on the products, applications and 
infrastructure described below will increase and new expenses for maintenance will be 
incurred. 
 
Infrastructure Operations and Maintenance 
 
The O&M activities pertain to the major infrastructure categories below: 
 
1. CCTN/Data Network Infrastructure – Outside plant fiber and network equipment 
including routers, switches, gateways, cybersecurity appliances, multiplexers, 
channel-banks, modems, Fiber Distributed Data systems and various cable 
management and cabling systems and the Stratum clocking infrastructure.

infrastructure and their various subscriber units including portables, mobiles, control 
stations, base stations, repeater stations, broadband data micro & femto cells and 
modems, radio frequency distribution systems, waveguides and antenna systems 
including microwave dishes.  
3. Telephony Infrastructures – The VoIP system, turret system, dispatch console system,

lightning protection systems, HVAC systems, Fire detection and suppression systems, 
equipment rack systems, rooms, cabinet and enclosures, physical security access 
control systems, environmental and application monitoring systems, and lighting 
systems.

Carrier usage rates and expansion of carrier services, fees, and taxes 
 
Apart from the infrastructure implemented and used at Con Edison, communication 
requirements are supplemented by commercial carrier services including various wireline 
and wireless services. These services incur monthly recurring charges (MRC) based on 
monthly usage required to support company operations. These MRC include additional fees 
and taxes. Although the rates are aggressively negotiated to minimize usage cost the actual 
usage varies depending on activity and new deployments. 
 
Infrastructure Support Services 
 
This work is performed by a combination of employee and vendor resources. Con Edison spends about 
$12 million annually for these services that are provided by more than 100 vendors including 
Exhibit___(IT-8)
Page 21 of 51


--- Page 633 ---
3 
 
outsourced services, specialized service providers, managed service providers, systems support 
providers, equipment and hardware providers and telecom software and license providers. 
 
Infrastructure Systems 
 
The network and telecommunications infrastructure consists of the Corporate 
Communications Transmission Network, the Land Mobile Radios systems, the SCADA radio 
systems, the corporate data network, the control operations recorder, turret and dispatch 
console systems, the VoIP telephone system, the multimedia collaboration and 
teleconferencing systems, the monitoring systems, the common support systems, the facilities 
housing the equipment and the outside and inside plant fiber optic and cable systems, the 
software including applications, firmware and middleware and the subscriber units 
associated with these systems. 
 
The objectives of the work are to maintain all critical systems in optimal condition and operate them in 
an efficient, proactive manner that maximizes the life span and utility of the system. To maintain the 
balance between private infrastructure and supplemental services provided by commercial entities 
while minimizing usage cost through economy of scale-based negotiation.  
 
The work entails various preventative maintenance programs across all critical systems executed on a 
schedule that almost eliminates major failures that substantially impact major operations. 
 
Increase in O&M costs: 
 
The increase in equipment through sustained targeted capital investments in the CCTN outside plant 
fiber expansion; and upgrade of equipment through ongoing migration from legacy technologies that 
were in service for the past several decades to the new technology platforms such as MPLS and LTE; 
and expansion of broadband wireless infrastructure to support Grid-Mod (Grid Modernization) 
including significant expansion in sensor networks, and the overall transformation of the telecom 
outside plant infrastructure from copper to fiber to provide more resiliency and survivability from 
super storms like Sandy,  have resulted in increased O&M cost associated with routine maintenance of 
equipment and systems; increases in usage, fees, taxes, warranties and licenses; and preventative 
inspection and remediation and repair services to maintain these infrastructures in an optimal 
operational state.  
 
Some of the equipment systems expanded and upgraded under the capital CCTN, XM8 and Grid-Mod 
programs include the various land mobile radios systems and their subscriber units, the various 
dispatch consoles and repeater systems, the turret and their recorder systems, and the new IP based 
telecollaboration system that facilitate remote worker productivity. These systems are maintained by a 
group of highly specialized vendors like Microchip, Cisco, Nokia, Ericsson, Power Systems, HVAC 
systems, board, card & component level repairs and engineering services contractors. There has also 
been a substantial increase in field support for the hundreds of end points associated with Grid-Mod. 
 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
The value of the Company’s technology investments is maintained through support contracts 
for its various hardware and software platforms. The support is used to assist during issues, as 
well as to keep the software up to date, patch cybersecurity vulnerabilities, replace hardware 
failures, and take advantage of new release features within the products.  IT provides critical 
Exhibit___(IT-8)

services, and these vendor support services contracts allow for sustainability and 
supportability of the environment and increases reliability and availability of the network, 
business applications, infrastructure, and PCs.  These contracts are part of the IT strategy to 
reduce risk and provide sustainability and supportability of the various platforms.  Without 
having these contracts in place, the Company will incur a significant support risk.  
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives,

This program supports future growth, allows for security and support for all networks and major

includes significant training which will be very costly. The vendor services secured via the competitive 
procurement process are more cost effective and in reducing operating costs through economies of 
scale and avoidance of hiring specialized skillsets or re-training for employees. 
 
Risk of No Action 
 
A lapse in these critical support services will result in gradual deterioration of systems that will 
adversely affect operations of all commodity businesses.

Project Risks and Mitigation Plan 
 
The most common risks associated with O&M activity and services are increasing costs, supportability, 
and supply chain delays. Use of the competitive procurements process will help manage costs; timely 
systems platform migrations will address obsolete unsupportable technologies; and upfront bulk 
purchases together with re-prioritization will help manage supply chain delays.

manufacturers to ensure reliable service and protect warranty and sustainability requirements.

Work Description: 
The IT Risk Management & Compliance Section will establish a new section within the Office of the 
Chief Information Officer (OCIO). Core activities that will be performed by the workgroup will 
include:  
• 
Developing a 5-yr Technology Risks and Compliance Roadmap 
• 
Increasing the maturity level of ITs risk and compliance management capabilities and 
implementing a standardized risk framework for technology risk management 
• 
Enhancing IT compliance programs and establishing control standards for the use and 
implementation of new IT systems throughout the Company 
• 
Reducing IT risks to internal, external customers and stakeholders through the systematic 
identification, evaluation and remediation of technology and compliance risks 
• 
Providing risk insights to the IT leadership team about emerging technology risks and 
changes/new compliance requirements 
The scope of activities to be undertaken by this section includes: 
 
• 
Conducting and/or coordinating self-assessments to evaluate compliance with IT controls, 
standards, and policies and procedures 
• 
Enhancing IT risk awareness and conducting risk and compliance training to IT employees 
• 
Supporting IT and working with Auditing and Corporate Compliance in connection with 
audits, compliance, and other reviews performed in the IT Department 
• 
Reporting on the status and timely completion of audit recommendations   
• 
Overseeing Business Continuity Planning (BCP)/Disaster Recovery coordinating activities 
Exhibit___(IT-8)
Page 26 of 51


--- Page 638 ---
2 
 
• 
Maintaining and supporting preparedness for Event/Crisis response (Emergency Response 
Plan, Coastal Storm Plan, Emergency Drills, System Emergency Assignment coordination) 
• 
Overseeing software license management  
• 
Implementing a new Policy and Procedures System that will enable IT to: 
o 
Replace the use of manual spreadsheets with a robust policy and procedures system 
that sends automated reminders to document owners to ensure that all policy and 
procedures documents are reviewed, updated, and approved timely 
o 
Initiate a program to standardize all IT policy and procedures and establish a review 
and update cycle 
o 
Classify and mark sensitive policy and procedures, if not done so already and tag 
documents to ensure conformance with specific compliance requirements (PII, SOX, 
etc.) 
Justification Summary: 
IT Risk Management & Compliance activities are currently performed within each IT section. These 
activities are performed ad-hoc, rely on the use of manual spreadsheets, and may divert IT people 
resources from their core job responsibilities.  The IT Risk Management & Compliance Section will 
centralize ITs risk and compliance management activities, increase functional capabilities, and develop 
risk mitigation plans for emerging technology risks and implement monitoring controls for new 
compliance requirements. 
 
The IT Risk Management & Compliance Section will establish a dedicated workgroup to include 3 
Information Technology Risk and Compliance Analysts who will: 
• 
Coordinate and monitor IT risks and compliance issues; 
• 
implement a robust policy and procedures system with automated workflows to replace the 
processes currently being performed manually 
• 
initiate a 5-yr. plan to standardize all IT policy and procedures (>500 policies, guides, job aids, 
checklists, etc.); 
• 
provide a single point of reference/contact for IT, employees, management, auditors, and 
regulatory bodies. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
The IT Risk Management & Compliance Section is aligned to the risk management strategies, 
establishes a dedicated workgroup with the knowledge, experience, and expertise to address increased 
technology and compliance risks.   
 
The program reduces reputational risks due to early identification of technology risks, compliance 
issues, and lessens impacts to customers through the mitigation of avoidable risks.

Work Description: 
 
Information Technology (IT) seeks to further develop its Portfolio Management Office (PMO) to 
enhance and mature portfolio management capabilities, to include advanced analytics, metrics, 
increased oversight, and controls to provide corporate guidance on IT investments as the portfolio 
continues to grow.  
The IT PMO manages the Company’s IT capital portfolio, provides guidance and a standard approach 
for the management of technology projects.   
 
Over the next 2-5 years the aforementioned items will need to be addressed and/or built out for the 
organization to strategically and effectively drive technology investments across the Company, 
particularly as the IT capital portfolio continues to increase.  This work will require the addition of 
three (3) qualified employees, as outlined in the funding requested below. 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
In 2016, IT created the IT Portfolio Management Office (PMO) to facilitate the execution of a technology 
portfolio of projects that is aligned to Con Edison’s IT strategic goals and guiding principles, and to 
enable the delivery of IT projects that are on time, on scope and on budget, to deliver value to our 
customers.  The IT PMO has made progress toward these goals since its inception: 
 
• 
The consolidation and optimization of a capital portfolio of IT projects taking place across the 
Company during the capital budgeting cycle 
• 
The registration and evaluation of technology projects in accordance with CEI CI-215 
Acquisition, deployment and support of Information Technology 
Exhibit___(IT-8)
Page 31 of 51


--- Page 643 ---
2 
 
• 
Alignment of IT projects with IT’s guiding principles (promote one enterprise, excel at the 
basics, foster/promote innovation, implementation methodology) and long term strategy, and 
improvement of delivery 
• 
The promotion and application of project management best practices across IT 
 
To elevate the abilities of the team, the IT PMO is looking to enhance and mature portfolio 
management capabilities, to include improved analytics, metrics, oversight, and controls. Through 
these initiatives, the IT PMO aims to bring better utilization of funding, a strategic approach to project 
implementation, identification of interdependencies between projects and management thereof, and 
more efficient and timely delivery of projects, scheduling, resources, and cost agility (shifting these 
items quickly, as needed).  Successful execution of these projects will aid in the safe delivery of energy 
services and improved customer experience to our rate payers.  
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
 
5-Year Long-Range Plan: With IT investments needed to support day to day operations, enhance field 
work, and meet the expectations of our customers the trend of an increase in IT investments in the next 
5-years supports the need for Portfolio Management. The IT PMO will enhance policy/procedure 
compliance, better allocate the IT capital budget and provide advanced analysis and metrics to ensure 
the portfolio is adding value as expected.

Con Edison is requesting finding for costs associated with its Oracle Strategic Partnership (OSP).  
OSP facilitates portfolio standardization, and predictable Operations & Maintenance expenditures 
with Oracle. 
 
In May 2018, Con Edison and Oracle established a Perpetual Universal License Agreement (PULA). 
Oracle Corporation is a global provider of mission critical enterprise technology and is one of Con 
Edison’s largest IT vendors supporting:

Customer care, billing, and energy efficiency

Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) including finance and supply chain, human resources 
and payroll, and Business Intelligence (BI)

Outage and distribution system management

Corporate hardware, integration software, and database management systems 
Con Edison has been an Oracle customer since 1990.

Work Description: 
This is a program designed to train developers in secure coding practices.  Auditing has recommended 
that a formal training program be implemented to train all developers annually in secure coding and 
industry best practices. This is required for all employees who are engaged in architecting, designing, 
developing and supporting IT applications.  
  
The scope of this initiative includes the following activities: 
• 
Procure annual subscription licenses from a reputable training provider/platform 
• 
Annually review training curriculum to ensure relevance of training content 
• 
Perform administrative oversight of secure coding training program to ensure awareness and 
compliance 
 
Justification Summary: 
 
 
Due to rapidly changing technology and an increase in cyber-attacks, developers must stay abreast of 
secure coding best practices, including prevalent vulnerabilities, and standards.  This, along with 
centralized code management and built-in cyber scanning capabilities will mitigate/eliminate coding 
issues as code is developed, maintained, and changed over time. 
 
The training program will provide awareness in the following areas: 
• 
Securing Coding Procedure 
• 
Cyber security standards and best practices (OWASP, SANS etc.) in: 
o 
Web and API development 
o 
Mobile Development 
o 
Database designs 
Exhibit___(IT-8)
Page 42 of 51


--- Page 654 ---
2 
 
o 
Cloud Computing 
• 
Source code analysis for software bug detection and vulnerabilities 
• 
Code quality analysis for code maintainability 
• 
Automatic integration with existing DevOps tools to enabled continuous integration and 
deployments (CI/CD). 
• 
Analytics on quality and vulnerability data. 
 
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
The investment in training program aligns with IT’s Journey to Zero.

Work Description: 
The CECONY Mainframe hardware environment supports many critical Applications. has 
been executing ease in operating and maintenance software support costs, for both IBM 
and our 3rd party software vendors, is a result of a recent requirement to increase 
computing resources on the CECONY mainframe.    
  
The CECONY mainframe environment runs critical corporate applications including 
Customer Information System (CIS), Emergency Control System (ECS) production batch 
systems that support Customer Billing (CUBS), Automated Metering 
Infrastructure (AMI), and other processes that support the business of Con Edison.  
  
The CECONY mainframe is also used for testing copies of production state to validate 
application upgrades and changes prior to moving to a live production environment. In the past 
few years, the CECONY mainframe has consistently seen growth in processing on the 
mainframe environments. The current batch billing schedules have caused latent demand with 
critical application testing and impacting both customer and internal processing 
performance.  The demand for additional resources put on the mainframe by critical business 
groups: AMI, with the additional borough creation and daily batch streams, DCX 
has accelerated the need for additional computing resources. This new requirement will in turn 
increase our annual support costs incurred and paid to both IBM and our 3rd party software 
vendors. The CECONY mainframe also functions as the disaster recovery platform for the 
Orange and Rockland mainframe (both mainframe systems can function on the alternate 
machine during a system event impacting mainframe services at one of the locations.)  
 
Exhibit___(IT-8)
Page 47 of 51


--- Page 659 ---
2 
 
 
Justification Summary: 
See above.  The increase in the CECONY annual support costs is directly related to the yearly 
increase in third party software cost that we see every year and to support old hardware 
technology on our CECONY platforms.   
  
In 2020, a mainframe health check assessment was initiated by two outside vendors to assist in 
evaluating the current operational state and provide configuration recommendations to 
potentially improve current state performance. While the vendors did provide technical 
recommendations for system tuning (note all recommendations were implemented, providing 
benefits to specific applications / system functions), through their recommendation, based on 
the analysis and presuming no significant change in operational requirements, normal business 
growth still results in the need for additional computing power.  As per their evaluation, 
there may 
be 
potential 
life 
extension/refinement 
opportunities 
in 
the 
production job/batch universe, but they did not see anything that would lead them to believe 
there will be a significant improvement to the overall health of the computing power. Their 
recommendation is to increase the compute power of the equipment, especially based on our test 
environments workloads over the last few years.   
Relationship to Broader Company Plans and Initiatives (e.g. Long-Range Plans, CLCPA Initiatives, 
Risk Mitigation) 
The project will create a more healthy, robust and secure CECONY Mainframe environment. 
This will allow us to continue to support our legacy application as mandated by legal 
requirements as we achieve our goals to migrate off the mainframe with certain application 
workloads. Executing on outdated mainframe software exposes CECONY to more errors and 
unreliable services. Risks of not maintaining state of the art levels of mainframe software  on 
our CECONY processing environments could result in a reduction in critical system uptime.

Cost Savings: Reductions in costs that are currently being incurred (e.g., reduced annual maintenance 
cost relative to today) 
 
Cost Avoidance: Reductions in anticipated future costs that don’t occur today (e.g., anticipated short-
term fixes/maintenance if capital isn’t deployed) 
 
Project Status: 
 
• 
Initiation – New project, not authorized yet 
• 
Planning – Project authorized, not started yet 
• 
Executing – Project in-flight  
• 
On-going – Annual program
